ISLAMABAD: Pakistan is among the 10 countries bearing the brunt of the global hunger crisis, with climate-related disasters, economic hardship, displacement and shrinking humanitarian funding pushing vulnerable communities deeper into food insecurity, according to a new report released by international humanitarian organisation Action Against Hunger.

The report, Ten Largest Global Food Crises, released on Friday in connection with World Food Day, warns that an estimated 10.6 million people in Pakistan will require humanitarian assistance in 2026, despite ongoing recovery efforts and improvements in some macroeconomic indicators.

Globally, approximately 177 million people live in the 10 countries where hunger is most concentrated, while acute hunger has doubled over the past decade, affecting 266 million people across 47 countries, says the report.

The countries facing the largest food crises are Nigeria, Congo, Sudan, Yemen, Afghan­istan, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Pakistan, South Sudan and Syria.

In Pakistan, persistent poverty, high food inflation, rising living costs, limited employment opportunities and declining household incomes continue to erode families' purchasing power. Unfavourable agricultural prices and broader economic instability have further undermined livelihoods, leaving millions struggling to afford adequate food.

As humanitarian needs outstrip available resources, vulnerable households are increasingly resorting to damaging coping strategies, including cutting food consumption, selling productive assets and withdrawing children from school to cope with financial pressures.

The report cautions that these measures may provide temporary relief but can deepen poverty, undermine children's education and nutrition, and weaken families' ability to recover from future shocks.

Limited access to healthcare, nutrition services, clean water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), and social protection is compounding the crisis, particularly in rural and disaster-affected areas. Persistent poverty and acute malnutrition remain major drivers of humanitarian needs, while cuts to support services and livelihood programmes are further eroding community resilience.

Pakistan's exposure to climate-related disasters remains a major source of food insecurity. Recurrent floods, droughts, heatwaves, glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) and increasingly erratic monsoon rainfall have damaged infrastructure, reduced agricultural production and weakened livestock-dependent livelihoods.

Crop losses and prolonged dry spells have also increased households' reliance on markets for food at a time when many families have limited purchasing power. Several districts are experiencing prolonged drought conditions, adding to concerns about agricultural output and rural incomes.

The report warns that seasonal hardships can intensify these pressures. The lean season from December 2025 to March 2026, characterised in some areas by extended winter conditions and heavy snowfall, was identified as a period likely to worsen food insecurity by restricting access to markets and essential resources.

Insecurity and regional tensions are adding another layer of pressure to Pakistan's already fragile food security situation.

According to the report, localised insecurity in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan continues to disrupt livelihoods, restrict access to markets and hamper humanitarian operations.
ir_summary: Pakistan is among 10 countries worst affected by global hunger due to climate disasters, economic hardship, and shrinking aid funding.

title: Power users face Rs33bn FCA hit in Nov bills
text:
ISLAMABAD: The power division on Thurs­day projected an additional fuel cost adjustment (FCA) of Rs2.56 per unit for electricity consumed in September, translating into an estimated Rs32.7 billion burden on consumers in November bills.

In a statement, the division said the adjustment would have been significantly higher, by around Rs3.44 per unit, but targe­ted load management hel­ped contain the price shock.

"The Ministry of Energy (Power Division) has aver­ted a potential Rs5-6 per unit hike in the September 2026 Fuel Price Adjust­ment (FPA) through timely measures, including targeted load management, limiting the projected adjustment to Rs2.56 per unit despite rising international fuel prices and constraints on LNG supplies," the statement said.

Over the past two mon­ths, the power division has started issuing advance estimates before the Cen­tral Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) formally makes the regulatory filing required for monthly fuel cost adjustments.

"Targeted load management and other measures helped limit the impact of expensive fuels used for power generation, saving consumers from an additional burden of up to Rs3.44 per unit," the division said.

It confirmed that targeted load management of around two to two-and-a-half hours during September helped reduce reliance on costly alternative fuels, including furnace oil and high-speed diesel and contain the anticipated increase in the FCA.

The division added that supplying imported re-gasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) for power generation at domestic gas prices had further eased the burden on consumers by 83 paise per unit.

"Consequently, the September FPA is expected to be Rs1.45 per unit higher than that of August," the statement said. The August FCA was Rs1.11 per unit, while the estimated financial impact of the September adjustment is Rs32.7bn on consumers' electricity bills in November.

The power division said international fuel prices had risen sharply amid regional conflicts and disruptions to fuel supply chains following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude prices had surged beyond $120 per barrel, compared with the benchmark of around $70 per barrel assumed while determining the base electricity tariff.

Despite Qatar's declaration of force majeure, Pakistan continued efforts to meet its RLNG requirements through available contracted supplies and additional spot cargoes where necessary, it added.

The division also claimed that the combined impact of fuel price adjustments and quarterly tariff adjustments during January-August had been limited to 65 paise per unit, equivalent to an increase of only 1.9pc over the base electricity tariff.

It attributed this partly to tariff rationalisation measures and an additional electricity consumption package for industrial and agricultural consumers, which it said encouraged greater use of power from the national grid.

However, industrial consumers have disputed the claimed benefits of the support package. They contend that the Rs22.96 per unit marginal cost rate benefits only a limited number of consumers, while an actual marginal cost of around Rs34 per unit results in an additional burden of about Rs11 per unit being fed into the average tariff, putting a burden on all consumers.

At their request, Nepra last week held a public hearing on revising or suspending the incremental package, but a decision is still awaited.

The power division said it was continuing to monitor developments in international fuel markets and supply chains while taking measures to minimise the impact of external price shocks on electricity consumers.
ir_summary: Pakistan's power division imposes Rs33bn fuel cost adjustment on electricity bills due to rising international fuel prices.

title: TTAP ‘suspends all talks’ until meeting with Imran
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Thursday announced the suspension of all negotiations with the government, stressing that there would be "no talks" until a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan was arranged and information about his health was provided.

The opposition alliance said all authority for future negotiations would rest solely with its chairman, Mehmood Khan Achakzai.

The decision was taken at a leadership meeting held at Mr Achakzai's residence, where participants reviewed the political situation arising from the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Political tensions between the federal government and the opposition, particularly PTI, had remained high in recent weeks after the party announced a long march demanding the release of its incarcerated founder. The march, initially billed as one towards Islamabad, remained confined to KP before fizzling out following the imposition of governor's rule.

The TTAP strongly condemned the measures in KP, describing them as a "robbery" and a midnight assault on the Constitution and the people's mandate.

It demanded their immediate withdrawal, saying the decision was an insult not only to the people of KP but to those of all provinces. The alliance also anno­unced that it would challenge the move in the Peshawar High Court.

The TTAP condemned terrorism in all its forms and expressed support for the National Action Plan. It demanded that, instead of adopting new policies, the joint resolution of the Aman Jirga approved by the KP Assembly be implemented.

The alliance also sought the immediate release of non-functional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar and detained members of the National and provincial assemblies and other party leaders.

PTI had reported their detention on Oct 11, shortly after the Centre imposed emergency and governor's rule in the province.

The alliance also demanded the release of Imran Khan's sisters, who have been detained for nearly three weeks under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, as well as access to the former prime minister by his family and doctors.

The TTAP also blamed the deteriorating law and order situation in Balochistan on an "unrepresentative" provincial government and "failed" federal policies. It urged the authorities to resolve the province's problems through dialogue rather than force.

The alliance also said it would approach international human rights organisations and the United Nations over alleged restrictions on judicial independence, curbs on the media and violations of human rights and the Constitution.

The federal government imposed emergency under Article 232 and governor's rule under Article 234 on Oct 11 after the cabinet discussed the security situation in KP and accused the provincial government of "deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism".

Meanwhile, some PTI leaders privately criticised the handling of negotiations with the government and the party's response to the imposition of governor's rule.

Speaking to a group of journalists, the leaders blamed Mr Achakzai's "egoistic approach" for contributing to the failure of talks, arguing that he was among the few opposition figures capable of concluding an agreement but had declined to participate directly in key meetings.

They claimed that MWM chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas had taken the initiative in bringing the government and opposition to the negotiating table after little progress had been made by PTI's own leadership.

According to one of the leaders, the plan following the announcement of the long march had been for then-chief minister Sohail Afridi to build political pressure through mobilisation while the party leadership pursued negotiations with the Centre.

However, he claimed little effort was made to initiate negotiations until Mr Abbas intervened and that the march was subsequently delayed by a week to allow talks to proceed.

The PTI figures also questioned the party's preparedness for governor's rule, pointing out that it took several days to approach the courts against the measure.

One leader said the party should have prepared its legal challenge in advance and provided clear instructions to its provincial lawmakers immediately after the Centre's decision.

They also said discussions had begun within PTI about changes to the party's interim leadership and some members argued that experienced political negotiators should be given a greater role.

"Imran Khan had suggested that Barrister Ali Zafar become PTI chairman, but he refused, saying that he wanted to focus on the cases of PTI. Moreover, there are politicians like Malik Aamir Dogar, who knows how to negotiate, but he is even not allowed to chair the meetings of parliamentary party," a party leader said.

However, the leaders acknowledged that JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had clearly communicated his position during the political negotiations, including his refusal to participate in the long march.
ir_summary: TTAP opposition alliance suspends talks with government until meeting with Imran Khan and demands end to KP governor's rule.

title: ECP rejects Punjab’s plea to delay LG polls
text:
ISLAMABAD / LAHORE: Putting its foot down after four years of delay, the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday rejected Punjab's plea to postpone local government ele­ctions until April next year and deci­ded to issue the schedule immediately.

Earlier this month, the electoral body proposed holding local government elections in Punjab on Dec 14 and sent a draft schedule to the Punjab chief secretary for consultation.

However, the Punjab government on Wednesday proposed holding the elections in three phases on April 4, 11 and 18, citing smog, dense fog and adverse winter weather conditions expected during December and January.

On Thursday, the ECP rejected the provincial government's request. The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja.

Commission members Nisar Ahmed Durrani, Babar Hassan Bharwana and retired Justice Ikramullah Khan, as well as ECP Secretary Omar Hamid Khan and other senior officers, attended the meeting.

The commission was briefed that the Punjab government had responded on Oct 14 to the ECP's Oct 2 letter and draft election programme.

Citing dense fog and severe cold in December, followed by the start of Ramazan in February, the provincial government proposed holding local government elections in three phases in April 2027.

The ECP termed the provincial government's response unsatisfactory, saying consultations had been completed on Aug 20, when the provincial authorities had agreed to hold local government elections in Punjab between Dec 15 and Jan 15, 2027.

"Now, the provincial government wants to change the proposed timeframe," the commission said.

The statement added that keeping its constitutional and legal responsibilities in view, the ECP had decided to hold local government elections in Punjab and issue the schedule immediately.

It directed its office to promptly submit the draft election programme for approval.

The ECP also said it had asked the provincial government to provide lists of officers to be appointed as district returning officers, returning officers and assistant returning officers. Expressing disappointment over the failure to provide the lists so far, the commission directed the provincial government to submit them within a week.

The Punjab Local Government and Community Development Department wrote to the ECP on Wednesday, seeking a delay in the local government polls.

The letter, conveying a ministerial committee's decision, cited expected smog, dense fog and adverse winter weather conditions during December and January, followed by the start of Ramazan in February, as reasons for not holding the elections as scheduled.

The letter said the cabinet's ministerial committee had held its second meeting on Oct 5, during which it discussed the ECP's draft election schedule at length. The committee considered scenarios arising from likely harsh weather conditions and Ramazan, it added.

The ministerial committee proposed holding the local government elections in phases to facilitate the deployment of election staff and security personnel, the transportation of polling materials, administrative oversight and access for voters.

The phased approach would also help avoid adverse weather conditions typically experienced during December and January, as well as the period immediately following Ramazan, the letter said.

It added that the Punjab cabinet had considered the committee's recommendations early on Wednesday and approved a proposal to hold the elections in three phases on April 4, 11 and 18, 2027, all Sundays.

The cabinet also decided that the allocation of districts among the three phases could be discussed and mutually agreed upon with the ECP at a dedicated meeting, taking into account administrative, logistical, security and geographical considerations, as well as weather conditions, the letter said.
ir_summary: Pakistan's election commission rejects Punjab government's request to delay local government polls, insisting on immediate scheduling.

title: Lawmakers, govt differ over Discos’ privatisation
text:
ISLAMABAD: The propo­sed privatisation of power distribution companies (Discos) stirred controversy on Wedn­esday, as a Senate panel maintained that the matter constitutionally fell within the domain of the Council of Common Interests (CCI), while the government's top privatisation official insisted that no fresh CCI approval was required.

Adviser to the Prime Minister on Privatisation Muhammad Ali told a subcommittee of the Senate Functional Committee on Devolution that no new CCI approval was needed for the privatisation of Discos. He added that the companies had caused losses of more than $30 billion over the past 15 years.

He said the CCI had approved the privatisation of three power generation companies and nine distribution companies in 2011. It also approved the National Electricity Policy on June 21, 2021, which recommended that the government explore various privatisation options to improve the efficiency of state-owned entities where applicable. Both decisions remained valid, he said.

On the validity of the decisions, the law division, in a Sept 25, 2026 letter, reconfirmed that in light of the 2011 CCI decision, fresh approval was not required for the privatisation of Discos.

Accordingly, the privatisation division maintained that no fresh CCI approval was required in light of the 2011 decision and the 2021 National Electricity Policy, Mr Ali said.

The adviser told the subcommittee that legal and procedural requirements for the privatisation process had been fulfilled.

He said the National Electricity Policy 2021 had been formulated after obtaining recommendations from the provinces and that the privatisation programme had subsequently been approved, with further work undertaken during 2023-24.

Referring the matter back to the CCI at this stage could cause significant delays, affect investor confidence and adversely impact the financial position of power distribution companies, he argued.

Highlighting substantial losses faced by the power sector due to electricity theft and operational inefficiencies, he stressed that privatisation was necessary to improve performance and reduce burden on the national exchequer.

Responding, subcommittee convener Senator Zamir Hussain Ghumro emphasised that the constitutional position and role of the CCI could not be overlooked.

He questioned whether the proposed privatisation was consistent with the constitutional distribution of powers under Article 157, observing that electricity distribution and related matters involved provincial interests.

Referring to previous judicial decisions and privatisation initiatives, he stressed the importance of transparency and protecting provincial interests, and asked authorities to provide relevant decisions and supporting documents for examination. He said provinces, being represented in the CCI, should have an opportunity to consider matters falling within their domain.

Officials informed the committee that the CCI had taken 11 relevant decisions and that, according to available record, no province had formally recorded reservations. They assured that relevant documents and details of provincial consultations would be shared. The minister reiterated that all necessary legal requirements had been met and referring the matter back to CCI was not considered necessary at this stage.

The chairman reiterated that the committee's examination was intended to ensure constitutional compliance, transparency and effective parliamentary oversight, and directed authorities to furnish decisions and supporting documents so the matter could be assessed in light of the Constitution and previous judicial pronouncements.

He said constitutionally the matter was related to CCI and necessary documents must be submitted to examine the process from all aspects.

The subcommittee met under the convenorship of Senator Ghumro to review federal expenditure on ministries, institutions, organisations, statutory bodies and corporations retained by the federal government despite provincial matters following the 18th Constitutional Amendment. It also examined compliance reports and status of matters concerning the CCI.

The meeting was attended by Senators Jan Muhammad Buledi and Poonjo Bheel, secretaries of cabinet, CCI, Establishment Division, special secretary establishment, additional secretary establishment and senior officers.

At the outset, the report of the Auditor General of Pakistan (AGP) and the Accountant General on expenditure incurred by the federal government on ministries relating to provincial subjects was taken up.

The chairman observed that despite 16 years since the 18th Amendment, concerns persisted regarding federal expenditure on devolved subjects, including education and health, which had been notified as provincial matters by the Implementation Commission.

Referring to Articles 168 and 169 of the Constitution and the legal framework governing the audit of public expenditure, he questioned the authorisation and constitutional basis for expenditure of approximately Rs2.6 trillion on the health and education ministries over the past 16 years.

He termed the expenditure of Rs2.6tr by the federal government on the two ministries, which he said had been de-notified in 2010, a misuse of taxpayers' money, arguing that the Centre could spend only on federal subjects.

He said the amount could rise to several trillion rupees once expenditure on other ministries created for provincial subjects was included.

Mr Ghumro expressed concern that the details sought by the committee had not been submitted within the stipulated timeframe and stressed that parliament was the primary authority for authorising public expenditure, and that such expenditure should be confined to federal subjects.

He maintained that expenditure from the Federal Consolidated Fund could not be authorised for devolved provincial matters. AGP officials explained that the audit process was guided by budgets approved by the competent parliamentary forum and acknowledged certain limitations in coverage.
ir_summary: Pakistani Senate panel and government disagree over whether privatization of power companies requires new approval from Council of Common Interests.

title: Gohar moves PHC against governor’s rule
text:
PESHAWAR: PTI Chai­r­man Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Wednesday mov­ed the Peshawar High Co­u­rt (PHC) against the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, req­u­esting the court to declare the move unconstitutional.

The emergency, decl­ared on Sunday, follows heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the PTI-led KP government. The Centre and opposition have been at odds over various issues, particularly the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons cited by both parties behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.

Advocate Shah Faisal Ilyas on behalf of the PTI chairman submitted the petition requesting the PHC to declare the Oct 11 emergency proclamation as "unconstitutional, ultra vires, coram non judice, tainted with malice in law and fact, devoid of objective material, and of no legal effect".

The court was further urged to set the proclamation aside.

Barrister Gohar is represented by a panel of lawyers, including Barrister Sameer Khosa, Salman Akram Raja, Ali Zaman, Sardar Haseeb Ahmad and Zainab Shahid.

As grounds for the petition, Barrister Gohar contended that the issuance of such a proclamation was subject to the "indispensable condition precedent of a prior resolution passed by the provincial assembly of that province".

"No such resolution was ever moved, debated, or passed by the provincial assembly of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa," he contended.

Filed under Article 199 (jurisdiction of high court) of the Constitution, the petition named the Federation of Pakistan (through the secretaries of the Cabinet, law ministry, interior ministry and defence ministry); the province of KP; KP Governor Kundi; the KP Assembly speaker; and the secretary of the KP home and tribal affairs department as respondents.

Sohail Afridi, the now non-functional chief minister of the province following the imposition of governor's rule, was also named as a pro forma respondent.

Barrister Gohar challenged the "constitutionality, legality and vires" of the Oct 11 Proclamation of Emergency in the province, the order deploying army troops to the province, and "all consequential and derivative executive orders, notifications, and bodies" constituted as a result, including the establishment of the KP Advisory Council and the "arbitrary" detention and unseating of Mr Afridi as the chief minister.

He urged the court to order the immediate constitutional restoration of Mr Afridi as the lawful chief minister of KP, along with his provincial cabinet, with full executive powers.

The plea urged the PHC to restrain the federation from "tabling, entertaining, or enacting any provincial legislative business concerning Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in Parliament".

The court was requested to declare as illegal and unconstitutional and to set aside, dissolve or permanently restrain all executive orders, notifications, actions, and bodies created "pursuant to or under the colour of" the proclamation.

The petitioner also challenged the Oct 11 order of army deployment under Article 245, requesting the court to declare it as unconstitutional on the basis that it could not "supplant or bypass the civilian executive and constitutional administration" of the province, and could not be invoked in the absence of a lawful requisition by Mr Afridi-led government.

He also sought directives for the immediate release of Mr Afridi and members of the KP cabinet and assembly from "unlawful executive or preventive detention".
ir_summary: PTI chairman challenges governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as unconstitutional in Peshawar High Court.

title: Pakistan, Oman urge diplomacy to bring peace to Mideast
text:
ISLAMABAD: Paki­stan and Oman on Wedne­sday stressed the need for dialogue and diplomacy to end the conflict between the United States and Iran and agreed to continue working together for regional peace and stability amid escalating tensions in the Gulf and attacks by Yemen's Houthis on Saudi Arabia.

The understanding was reaffirmed during the visit of Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Al Busaidi to Islamabad for the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC), which reviewed bilateral cooperation alongside regional developments.

Although the visit was primarily focused on bilateral relations, the deteriorating regional situation remained a key concern for the Omani minister. Soon after arriving in Isla­mabad on Tuesday night, Mr Al Busaidi spoke to Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to discuss the latest regional developments, including the situation in Yemen, and explore ways to promote peace and stability.

Speaking at a joint media interaction with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar after the JMC meeting, Mr Al Busaidi said the two sides had discussed regional challenges and shared the view that sustained diplomatic engagement was essential to prevent further escalation.

Mr Dar said Pakistan and Oman had a common understanding on the need to resolve disputes through peaceful means.

"We have commonality of view that dialogue and diplomacy is the only way forward. Conflict is no solution to any issue in the world, and we have seen from past history that conflicts take you to no positive conclusion," he said, adding that the two countries had agreed to continue working for regional stability.

The two ministers also underscored the importance of ensuring the safety and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, key maritime routes for global energy and food supplies.

While regional tensions dominated the political discussions, the JMC also took up its regular agenda on expanding economic and institutional cooperation between Pakistan and Oman.

Mr Dar said a key outcome of the session was the establishment and operationalisation of joint working groups on trade and investment, agriculture, oil and gas, and labour and human resource development. These mechanisms would ensure regular engagement and follow-up on decisions taken by the commission, he said.

The two sides also discussed cooperation in ports and logistics, energy, food security, information technology, tourism, education and workforce mobility, with both ministers calling for greater engagement between their business communities.

The ministers also agreed to continue institutional engagement, with the ninth session of the Joint Ministerial Commission to be held in Oman.

Later, PM Shehbaz Sharif received the Omani foreign minister and witnessed the exchange of six agreements and memorandums of understanding aimed at expanding bilateral cooperation.

The agreements included the protocol recording the minutes of the eighth JMC session, a mutual visa exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic, special, official and service passports, and an MoU on records and archives.

Other agreements covered information and broadcasting, information technology and telecommunications, and news exchange and media cooperation.
ir_summary: Pakistan and Oman call for diplomacy to resolve US-Iran tensions and ensure regional stability in the Middle East.

title: PM renews Makkah pact resolve as Riyadh blitzed
text:
ISLAMABAD / RIYADH: Characterising the Makkah Defence Alliance as a "historic" milestone for peace, unity and stability in the region, Prime Minister She­h­baz Sharif on Wednesday reaffirmed Pakistan's "unw­a­vering commitment" to the protection of Saudi Arabia's "sovereignty, territorial integrity and security".

The statement came as powerful explosions rattled the Saudi capital, hours after a Houthi strike hit a building in the area housing energy giant Aramco's operations centre, in a fresh escalation of the war between the kingdom and the Yemeni rebel group.

Most strikes on Saudi Arabia have targeted infrastructure on the outskirts of the capital, but the barrages appear to be getting closer to the city centre.

In the city's downtown, residents have been seen parking their cars to stop and look up at the sky, an AFP journalist said.

On Tuesday night, the white plumes of air defence missiles could be seen streaking across the sky followed by explosions.

While walking down a major avenue, a witness told AFP he "saw a projectile cut­­t­ing across the sky" abo­ve a mall, saying it left "a yellowish trail of light followed by a trail of smoke. Then, we heard an explosion".

"People were calm; no one was speaking. We were scared and all looking up at the sky," he added, requesting anonymity.

More blasts were heard on Wednesday, AFP journalists in Riyadh reported, as messages were received on phones warning of an "aerial threat" and urging people to take shelter.

The alert was lifted a few minutes later.

A Saudi energy ministry official said a building belonging to Aramco in Dhahran was struck on Tuesday, resulting in a "limited fire" but "no casualties or fatalities".

Dhahran is home to Aramco's headquarters, a vast complex comprising several buildings and residential compounds.

In Riyadh, the civil defence agency said four people — two women, a man and a child — were wounded by debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles and that 15 homes were damaged. The Saudi-led coalition, meanwhile, struck oil sites across western Yemen, with spokesman Turki Al-Malki saying the attacks targeted facilities used to supply the Houthis' effort to "threaten the kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea and waterways".

An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah channel said Saudi forces had targeted an oil firm.

Many civilians in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital, fearing shortages, have rushed to queue in front of fuel stations.

Several countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, with France telling its nationals on Tuesday to avoid Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam airports.

In a meeting with the newly appointed secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance, retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood, PM Shehbaz was briefed on the strategy to promote "defence and strategic cooperation" under the pact.

Mahmood was appointed as the first secretary general of the defence alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye last month. The agreement — signed on Aug 7 — empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all.

The premier reiterated that the pact was a "historic milestone for peace, unity, and stability in the region" and wished the secretary general well for his new role as Saudi Arabia, which is a signatory to the pact, has faced escalating tensions with Yemen's Houthi rebels in recent days. The PM said that Pakistan "stands shoulder to shoulder" with Saudi Arabia.
ir_summary: Pakistan reaffirms commitment to Saudi security pact amid Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh and Aramco facilities.

title: Parliament endorses KP emergency
text:
ISLAMABAD: Shortly after the National Assembly passed a resolution endorsing the federal government's imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Wednesday, the Senate also approved the measure.

The Centre imposed governor's rule and emergency in KP on Sun­day, citing the provincial government's "deliberate disengagement" from the fight against terrorism.

Minister for Parliamentary Aff­airs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry tabled motions regarding the proclamation of emergency in both Houses.

In the Senate, the resolution was passed amid protests from the opposition, with PTI senators staging a walkout.

The National Assembly's question hour was suspended as the House took up the emergency resolution. The motion was adopted by a majority vote after Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar opened the debate.

The parliamentary affairs minister read out the presidential proclamation of emergency while tabling the motion.

Throughout Wednesday's proceedings, opposition members participated calmly and did not stage any loud protests, unlike previous occasions when the PTI has opposed the Centre's moves.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also attended part of the session. Pictures of the proceedings show­ed him shaking hands with opposition leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai.

Addressing the House, the law minister said emergency had been imposed in KP because the security situation there was becoming a threat to "national security".

He highlighted a rise in terrorism in the province, particularly after 2021, which he attributed to the provincial government's approach.

"Perhaps there might be foreign, diplomatic and political reasons behind it, which got inflamed due to a political party's point of view," he said.

Mr Tarar maintained that 2,911 incidents of terrorism had taken place in KP between 2021 and 2024, but the number had surged to 3,787 between Oct 15, 2025, and Oct 9, 2026.

He criticised non-functional KP chief minister Sohail Afridi for allegedly ignoring the sacrifices of martyred security personnel and police officers while "preferring to promote his political designs and make visits across the country".

"Even this was announced that the federal capital will be conquered," he said, referring to the PTI's plan to hold a protest march towards Islamabad.

He said two days would be "remembered in the country's democratic history with regard to misfortune and a political party".

On the emergency measures, the law minister said a special mechanism had been introduced for 12 districts of KP.

Speaking after Mr Tarar, Mr Achakzai criticised the former for attempting to portray the provincial government as having failed to tackle terrorism.

Noting the participation of the PPP, which is in power in Sindh, the opposition leader warned that governor's rule would be imposed next in Sindh over the "occupation of water, mines and streams".

"Reverse these decisions," Mr Achakzai said, urging that parliament should be made the centre of power. "And Pakistan will be saved."

He also called for the Centre to give provinces their rights and resources.

Taking to the NA floor, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif recalled the PTI's tenure in the federal government and criticised the party's past actions.

Referring to former prime minister Imran Khan's plan to resettle members of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), he said the PTI had tried to convince the then opposition that "bringing these terrorists back would be better for Pakistan".

Commenting on the current political situation, Mr Asif alleged that the non-functional KP chief minister used to "take directives […] from a person sitting in Afghanistan".

He referred to a TTP statement condemning the imposition of emergency and the deployment of troops in certain areas. "Who is their ally and who is their rival?" he asked.

PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari blamed the PTI for the circumstances that had compelled the Centre to impose emergency in KP, describing the situation as a "political suicide attack" for the party.

However, he urged both the treasury and opposition benches to resume dialogue and make joint efforts to combat terrorism.

He argued that the PTI's actions and statements had left neither the president, the federal government nor him with any legal or political reason to oppose the imposition of emergency in KP.

"But even today, I would recommend to the federal government that we extend our hand forward once again for negotiations, political discussions and try to find a resolution and a middle path," he added.

The PPP chairman said emergency was "always a stopgap measure".

PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan told the NA that his party rejected the Centre's decision to impose emergency in KP.

He questioned what alleged involvement in terrorism had led to the arrest of the PTI founder's wife and sisters, and what charges had been levelled against party MNAs and MPAs who, he said, had also been detained.

"One person is not present in the House currently. When he comes during a joint session, then I will reveal the reality of the negotiations," he added.

He said the PTI had consistently raised its voice against terrorism and stressed that counterterrorism measures should be taken in accordance with the National Action Plan (NAP).

Recounting the Oct 3 talks with the government, Barrister Gohar said the PTI had been asked to immediately call off its protest march.

"I said where did [the topic of] terrorism arise from suddenly," he said.

Noting that the government had raised "five reservations", Barrister Gohar said the PTI was willing to bring the KP Police Act in line with those of Punjab and Sindh.

He also welcomed the PPP chairman's proposal to resume dialogue.

In response, Mr Bhutto-Zardari, pointing towards Barrister Gohar and Mr Achakzai, said: "I believe that none of them is allied with terrorists. I believe that they will definitely want to combat terrorism; however, they cannot deny the fact that their former chief minister contradicted this fact."

At one point during the proceedings, National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq said the Oct 3 dialogue had been held in a cordial atmosphere.

Mr Sadiq praised both sides for "attempting more than their capacity so that the matter is settled".

However, he said some matters were beyond the parties' control and voiced support for reconstituting the same negotiation committees if talks were needed in the future.

Speaking on the floor of the NA, MQM-P's Farooq Sattar said his party supported the decision taken by the prime minister.

"This was an extremely difficult decision, but so unavoidable that you had no other option," Mr Sattar said, referring to the imposition of emergency and governor's rule.

The NA session was adjourned until Oct 16 (Friday).

Meanwhile, the speaker issued production orders for PTI lawmakers Sanaullah Masti Khel and Dawar Kundi, directing that their presence in the House be ensured.

According to the production orders, seen by Dawn, the speaker considered the presence of the two MNAs necessary for the NA session summoned by President Asif Ali Zardari on Oct 13. He noted that both lawmakers were in the custody of the Punjab police.

President Zardari has summoned a joint sitting of parliament today (Thursday) at Parliament House, according to a post on the National Assembly's official account on X.

A notification said the primary purpose of the joint sitting was to formally ratify the governor's rule and emergency measures recently imposed in KP.

Lawmakers are scheduled to consider government resolutions submitted under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution.
ir_summary: Pakistan's parliament approves emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province citing terrorism threats and provincial government disengagement.

title: Air links between Quetta, Zahedan restored
text:
QUETTA: Air links between Quetta and the Iranian cities of Zahedan and Mashhad were restored on Wednesday and an Iran Air flight (IRA 0827) arrived at Quetta International Airport from Zahedan and subsequently departed for Zahedan carrying 80 passengers.

At Quetta International Airport, officials of the Zahedan Chamber of Commerce arriving on the Iran Air flight were received by Quetta Chamber of Commerce and Industry Vice President Jangiyan Dashti Baloch, former presidents Muhammad Ayub Miryiani and Jumma Khan Badizai, Quetta Airport General Manager Khalid Kakar and other officials.

Flights from Quetta to Iranian cities of Mashhad and Zahedan were inaugurated in December 2025. However, the bilateral air service had remained suspended for some time due to the present international situation and has now been resumed.

The restoration of air links is expected to strengthen business ties, boost trade activities and facilitate passenger travel between Pakistan and Iran.

The business community and the people in Balochistan welcomed the resumption of flights from Quetta to Zahedan and Mashhad, describing it as an important step towards improving trade and travel facilities in the region.
ir_summary: Pakistan and Iran restore air links between Quetta and Iranian cities to strengthen trade and travel relations.

title: Balochistan MPAs voice alarm over worsening law and order
text:
QUETTA: Opposition and treasury members of the Balochistan Assembly on Wednesday expressed serious concern over the deteriorating law and order situation in the province, citing a rise in violent incidents and the abduction of women.

Speaker Captain (retd) Abdul Khaliq Ach­akzai, who was presiding over the session, took notice of the situation and sought reports on incidents in Khuzdar and Kalat. He directed the deputy inspectors general (DIGs) of police to appear before the House in person along with the first information reports (FIRs).

During the session, the assembly also passed the Balochistan Water Resources Management Bill, 2026.

Speaking on a point of order, Provincial Assembly member Sardar Abdul Rahman Khetran said the bodies of two brothers had been dumped in Barkhan two days earlier. He said the brothers had been taken away by a banned outfit. Questioning the motive behind the killings, Mr Khetran asked whether the two men were not Baloch and on what grounds they had been killed.

He condemned the killings and said the destruction of bridges through explosions along the N-25 highway harmed ordinary travellers and the people of the province.

Provincial Minister Ali Madad Jattak also condemned the incident, describing those res­ponsible as terrorists. He said the state should be supported in its fight against terrorism.

During the session, member Zamarak Khan Achakzai submitted an adjournment motion concerning the law and order situation in Qila Abdullah and asked the government what steps had been taken to address the worsening security situation.

Provincial Home Minister Ziaullah Langove said several measures had been taken in the district over the past two years, including the establishment of two new police stations, an increase in police personnel and efforts to resolve tribal disputes.

Mr Achakzai said addressing fundamental problems was the responsibility of the state and the government. He noted that Qila Abdullah had previously been notorious for opium cultivation, but the lack of serious action had allowed drug cultivation to spread to other areas.

He said three police officer posts and 200 constable positions were vacant in his constituency. He added that the recruitment process had become so stringent that it was affecting the availability of personnel, while anti-narcotics operations needed to be made more effective.

Jamaat-i-Islami member Maulana Hidayatur Rehman Baloch said the security situation in Balochistan was serious and highways were no longer safe. He alleged that drugs were being sold openly and that the government and relevant institutions had failed to stop it.

He said lawmakers needed to recognise that running a government meant resolving problems faced by the public.

Mr Rehman also raised concerns over the abduction of women in disputes involving marriage and family relationships. He said those responsible for the killing of Asma Jattak's father had yet to be arrested. He added that the names of influential individuals and kidnappers could be disclosed in the assembly, saying he had identified some of them previously.

Mr Jattak said that following the Asma Jattak incident, Laiba Nachari was also abducted in Kalat over a dispute related to a marriage proposal.

Provincial Sports Adviser Meena Majeed Baloch expressed concern over violence and abuse against women, particularly in Kalat, Khuzdar and Jhalawan.
ir_summary: Balochistan Assembly members express concern over worsening law and order, abductions, and killings by banned outfits in the province.

title: Balochistan High Court orders survey of road to examine traffic flow obstructions
text:
QUETTA: The Balochistan High Court on Wednesday ordered a comprehensive survey of Joint Road in Quetta to examine traffic obstructions caused by shops located opposite a proposed filling station, and issues relating to the road-widening project. The court also sought reports from relevant authorities.

A two-judge BHC bench comprising Chief Justice Muhammad Kamran Khan Mulakhail and Justice Muhammad Najmuddin Mengal issued the directives while hearing the case.

The bench directed the director of the Balochistan Traffic Engineering Bureau to coordinate with the director general of the bureau and ensure a comprehensive survey of Joint Road in the presence of representatives from the Advocate General's Office, Pakistan Railways, and the petitioner or their counsel.

The court was informed that shops situated in front of the proposed filling station were disrupting traffic flow and could create another bottleneck on the road.

Counsel for the petitioner said a site inspection had also been conducted. However, he said, despite a decision to remove shops situated on the opposite side of the road in front of the proposed filling station, the necessary steps had not been taken.

The bench observed that the matter could not be resolved without a proper site inspection and a comprehensive survey.

The Advocate General's Office was directed to obtain reports from the Quetta Metropolitan Corporation and the revenue officer regarding existing, newly constructed and proposed shops on both sides of Joint Road and submit them to the court.

The advocate general was appointed convener of the committee and tasked with conducting the survey, while a representative of the Advocate General's Office will determine the date of the exercise.

During the hearing, the petitioner's counsel also raised objections to reports submitted by the Commissioner of Quetta Division and Pakistan Railways. The court expressed concern over the failure to submit the complete PC-I document for the road-widening project, noting that only one page had been provided.
ir_summary: Balochistan High Court orders traffic survey and reports on road widening and shop obstructions in Quetta.

title: Pakistan, Russia agree to finalise extradition treaty
text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Russia agreed on Wednesday to finalise an extradition treaty and an agreement on the exchange of criminals, while holding high-level talks to expand bilateral trade, economic and defence cooperation during the first-ever visit by a Russian interior minister to Islamabad.

The law enforcement understandings were reached during a meeting between Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Kolokoltsev, who arrived Monday on a four-day visit.

Following delegation-level talks, the two sides pledged to sign a memorandum of understanding on cooperation in preventing organised crime and exchanging information, an accord witnessed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Mr Naqvi said the proposed memorandum on preventing organised crime would be an important milestone in cooperation between the two countries.

Both sides also decided to ensure the early implementation of a readmission agreement and agreed to enhance cooperation between Pakis­tan's Anti-Narcotics Force and relevant Russian institutions, as well as between the National Police Academy and the Russian Police Academy, to prevent cybercrime.

Mr Kolokoltsev said joint measures were essential for the prevention of all organised crime, including terrorism, drug smuggling and illegal migration, noting that Russia had brought a 33 per cent reduction in cybercrime through effective measures.

They also discussed sending skilled manpower from Pakistan to Russia, easing the visa regime for tourists and the business community to increase people-to-people contact, and increasing the number of Pakistani students in Russia beyond the current 1,300.

Minister of State Tallal Chaudhry and the Russian ambassador in Pak­istan also attended the meeting.

Separately, Mr Kolokoltsev met with PM Shehbaz on Wednesday, highlighting the "significant potential for expanding bilateral trade and economic cooperation" betw­e­­en the two countries, according to a statement issued by the PM Office.

Mr Kolokoltsev conveyed Rus­sia's readiness to further enhance bilateral engagement and appreciated Pakistan's support at various multilateral forums, particularly the United Nations.

PM Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakis­tan's commitment to further deepening its friendly relations with Russia and making "effective use of existing bilateral mechanisms to adv­ance mutually beneficial cooperation", the statement said.

"He underscored the need to expand cooperation across areas of mutual interest, particularly trade and investment, energy and economic development."

In Rawalpindi, Kolokoltsev cal­led on Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at General Headquar­ters to bolster defence cooperation.

According to Inter-Services Public Relations, both sides discussed the regional security landscape and "underscored the importance of closer institutional linkages and improved coordination between the security institutions of Pakistan and Russia."

CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan's resolve to "deepen its longstanding relations with Russia and expand tangible cooperation in areas of shared interest, particularly in the security domain", while Mr Kolo­ko­ltsev acknowledged the professionalism and sacrifices of Pakistani forces in fighting terrorism.

culture, tourism and multilateral forums, including the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
ir_summary: Pakistan and Russia agree to finalize extradition treaty and enhance cooperation on crime, trade, and defense during Russian interior minister's visit.

title: FCC rejects Bushra’s plea to suspend Al-Qadir sentence
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Constitu­tional Court (FCC) on Wednesday rejected a plea by Bushra Bibi, wife of incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan, seeking suspension of her seven-year sentence in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust case.

"We find no sufficient ground warranting interference with the April 30 Islamabad High Court [IHC] order at this stage," FCC Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan observed while heading the two-judge bench that rejected her plea.

The IHC had declined to suspend her sentence while an appeal against the convictions of both her and her husband remained pending before it.

The FCC bench, which included Justice Ali Baqar Najafi, expressed the expectation that the high court would endeavour to decide the main appeal against her conviction, giving both sides adequate opportunity to be heard while discouraging unnecessary adjournments.

Earlier in the day, the bench had reserved its ruling on the plea, which contended that Bushra Bibi, being a woman and having a serious medical condition, was entitled to suspension of her sentence. It argued that similar relief was contemplated under the first proviso to Section 497(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), which deals with cases in which bail may be granted in non-bailable offences.

In its three-page order, the FCC noted that the application for suspension of the sentence had remained pending before the IHC because of successive adjournments sought by the National Accountability Bureau (NAB).

It observed that without entering into the merits of the application under Section 426 of the CrPC, the IHC had declined to suspend the sentence, principally on the ground that the main appeal had already been fixed for hearing and the appellant's counsel was not providing the requisite assistance for its adjudication.

The record further showed that the appeal, initially fixed for April 30, was subsequently adjourned to May 7 and then to Oct 5.

The principal grievance raised by the appellant's counsel concerned repeated adjournments allegedly sought by NAB, which had prolonged proceedings on the application for suspension of her sentence, the FCC observed.

"Be that as it may, the main appeal having already been fixed for hearing, the appropriate course will be to secure its expeditious adjudication rather than undertake a parallel examination of the merits of the suspension of sentence at this stage," the FCC stated.

The order further said the appellant's assertion that the appeal involved a voluminous record requiring elaborate arguments did not, by itself, furnish sufficient justification for interference with the IHC order.

It was therefore incumbent upon the appellant's counsel to provide full assistance to the IHC in hearing the main appeal, after which NAB would be equally obligated to advance its arguments without unnecessary adjournments, the FCC declared.
ir_summary: Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court rejects Bushra Bibi's plea to suspend her sentence in the Al-Qadir Trust corruption case.

title: Lawyers of Imaan, Hadi boycott ATC proceedings
text:
ISLAMABAD: Lawyers representing human rights activists and lawyers Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha, along with Shireen Mazari, boycotted proceedings of an anti-terrorism court on Wednesday after the judge decided to record prosecution witnesses' statements despite the defence's request to defer the exercise until they could meet the accused.

The court subsequently recorded statements of three witnesses in the absence of the accused and their counsel, taking the total number of witnesses examined so far in the case to six.

ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra recorded the statements after the accused, their counsel and Shireen Mazari, a former minister and Ms Imaan's mother, boycotted the proceedings and walked out of the courtroom over the court's decision to proceed with the recording of testimony.

During the hearing, Aimal Khan Mandokhail, counsel for Imaan and Hadi, informed the court that he had visited Adiala jail but could not meet his clients despite having a court order permitting the meeting.

He said it was a designated meeting day for lawyers, but roads had been blocked around one-and-a-half kilometres away from the jail.

A court official infor­m­­ed the judge that the jail auth­orities had conveyed that the accused would be produced through a video link.

Mr Mandokhail reques­ted the court to ensure physical appearance of the accused. The judge observed that reports had been received from the police and jail authorities indicating that a special vehicle was not available for their transportation.

Prosecutor Raja Naveed Hussain Kiyani requested the court to record the witnesses' statements on the day. The judge agreed, saying the matter of cross-examination could be taken up later.

Mr Mandokhail clarified that his instructions concerned cross-examination and said there were no specific directions from the lead counsel regarding the recording of the witnesses' statements.

He said that they should meet the accused before the proceedings continued.

Hadi Ali Chattha also requested the court to summon the accused to the courtroom, while Imaan Mazari urged that their privacy be respected, observing that conversations in the meeting area were recorded.

He maintained that the accused were the primary stakeholders in the proceedings and had a legal right to be heard.

He said the court had stressed the need to satisfy all stakeholders.

When the recording of the witnesses' statements began, the defence lawyers and Shireen Mazari walked out in protest. Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha's counsel also left the courtroom.

The court subsequently recorded the witnesses' statements in the absence of the accused and their lawyers.
ir_summary: Lawyers boycott anti-terrorism court proceedings over denied access to clients and court's decision to record witness statements.

title: Strategy to end violence against children unveiled
text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Wednes­day launched its first national strategy, seeking to establish a coordinated system for preventing abuse, strengthening child protection and ensuring access to care and justice for millions of vulnerable children across the country.

The National Strategy to End Violence Against Children (2026-2031) was launched by Parliamentary Secretary for Human Rights Saba Sadiq during a national preparatory consultation for the Second Global Ministerial Conference on Ending Violence Against Children, scheduled to be held in Manila in November.

Developed by the Ministry of Human Rights in collaboration with the World Health Organisation (WHO), the strategy comes against the backdrop of widespread violence and exploitation affecting children across the country.

According to the strategy, up to eight in 10 children in Pakistan experience violent discipline, while one in 16 internet-using children aged 12 to 17 faces technology-facilitated sexual exploitation or abuse.

It also says 841,402 children aged 10 to 17 had been married, while millions remain engaged in child labour.

The strategy further highlights the vulnerability of children who are displaced, migrants or living in poor and informal urban settlements.

It seeks to address multiple forms of violence, including physical and sexual abuse, psychological violence, neglect, child marriage, trafficking, child labour and technology-facilitated exploitation.

The framework, based on the internationally recognised INSPIRE approach, focuses on stronger laws, safer environments, support for parents and caregivers, financial stability, response services and life skills.
ir_summary: Pakistan launches a national strategy to prevent violence against children and strengthen child protection systems.

title: KP emergency nod draws opposition senators’ ire
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate's approval of a resolution endorsing the federal government's imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Wednesday followed fierce protests by opposition members, who chanted slogans before eventually walking out of the upper house.

A heated debate between treasury and opposition members was witnessed during the proceedings, during which Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar defended the procedure followed in presenting the resolution and securing its approval.

He argued that a "constitutional resolution" had been laid before the House in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Senate.

As the opposition voiced its objections to the resolution, Senate Chairman Yousuf Raza Gilani urg­ed members to exercise patience.

"This is not a classroom, do not make noise," he remarked as opposition senators continued chanting slogans.

PTI Senator Humayun Mohm­a­­nd said independent Senator Faisal Vawda had predicted months ago that governor's rule would be im­­posed. He alleged that terrorism, cited as the reason for the measure, was merely an excuse and that the real "target is the PTI".

"The decision to impose governor's rule and emergency was taken months ago," he alleged. Seemingly referring to the creation of Bangladesh, he said the federal government's decisions since 1970 had proved wrong.

PTI-backed Senator Hamid Khan also argued that there "seems to be some other objectives behind governor's rule and emergency". Referring to negotiations between the Centre and the opposition ahead of the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in KP, he alleged that the talks "were just a drama" and were held "only to deceive the people".

"The real decision was taken elsewhere long ago," he claimed.

He further said JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who had tried to mediate between the Centre and the opposition, had stated that a decision was taken while negotiations were under way.

"Governments formed on the basis of Form-47 do not have the real mandate," he added.

Mr Khan regretted that after the 26th Amendment, "there is neither any Constitution nor an independent judicial system".

"The judiciary has been stripped of its independence, which closes the avenues to challenge unconstitutional steps," he said.

"Article 232 has to be presented before the House for debate, not just for saying yes. Decision was taken by those whom Constitution does not allow to take the decision, but they have complete dominance over Constitution. At this time, neither is there any Constitution nor any court in the country," he added.

PTI Senator Mohsin Aziz lashed out at federal ministers who had been accusing the party of facilitating terrorism.

"You talk about terrorism, what do you know about terrorism? Peo­­ple of KP sacrificed their children and picked up bodies. […] Did we support Pakistan or terrorists? Those calling people of KP terrorists should be ashamed. These are valiant people who saved this country," he said. Mr Aziz said terrorism stemmed from unemployment, hunger and the lack of hospitals, water and education.

Another PTI senator, Zeeshan Khanzada, accused the federal government of "abducting" Sohail Afridi, who had been rendered non-functional as KP chief minister following the imposition of governor's rule, as well as other PTI MPAs.

JUI-F's Kamran Murtaza said the opposition's resolution against governor's rule should also have been included in the day's agenda, but it had been returned with objections.

Mr Murtaza argued that the relevant material required for endorsing the enforcement of Articles 232 and 234, which deal with the imposition of emergency and governor's rule, had not been presented to the House. He added that senators had to obtain the material through social media.

Members could not be satisfied with a decision until complete information was made available, he said.
ir_summary: Pakistani Senate approves emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid opposition protests and allegations of political targeting.

title: Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly passes ‘amended’ Local Govt Act 2026
text:
GILGIT: The Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) Asse­­mbly on Wednesday cleared the way for the region's first local bodies elections in over two decades by passing the amended GB Local Government Act 2026, while also approving a separate bill to establish an Information Technology Board.

During a session chaired by Deputy Speaker Malik Kifayatur Rehman, the assembly first approved the amended GB Local Government Act 2026 by a majority vote. The legislation aims to hold local bodies elections that have not been conducted in the region for more than 20 years.

Gilgit-Baltistan Minister for Local Bodies Zulfiqar Ali Murad introduced the amended draft in the House to seek its passage.

Although the assembly had previously passed the act with a majority, GB Governor Syed Mehdi Shah returned the bill for reconsideration after raising objections to several points.

Opposition members raised objections when the amended bill was tabled, asking the treasury benches for more time to study and consider the draft. However, the majority of the assembly members favoured the bill, and Deputy Speaker Rehman announced its passage over the opposition's dissent.

Speaking on the floor of the House, Mr Murad stated that the act was reintroduced only after the governor's objections were removed and the revised draft was approved by the GB Cabinet.

Under the new act, municipal corporations have been established in the cities of Chilas, Gilgit and Skardu, where elected members will choose mayors and deputy mayors.

Additionally, union councils and district councils have been established across all districts, with a 17pc quota allocated for women in all local bodies. The passage of the bill follows months of administrative deadlock over local polls.

The dispute emerged after Chief Election Commissioner Raja Shahbaz Khan unilaterally scheduled elections for Aug 2, causing friction with the chief minister, who was not consulted.

The chief minister insisted on conducting the elections under a new 2026 act, while the election commissioner intended to use the previous 2014 act. The election commission subsequently postponed the polls.

Official sources state that a new election date will be announced once the governor signs the amended bill into law.

Separately, the bill to establish the GB Information Technology Board was unanimously approved. Under the legislation, the chief minister will serve as the board's chairman, while a minister or adviser will act as its vice chairman.

Speaking on the occasion, Chief Minister Amjad Hussain Advocate said the board is being established to address long-standing information technology and telecommunications issues and to upgrade internet connectivity faced by residents across the region.

The chief minister told the assembly that governance, tendering, tax collection and other departmental functions are being shifted online.

"The board will invite foreign investors, bring stakeholders to GB from other provinces, and establish IT parks and other facilities for locals, particularly the youth, to ensure their easy and high-speed access to the internet," CM Hussain said, adding that the board will be inaugurated by the prime minister.
ir_summary: Gilgit-Baltistan Assembly passes amended local government law enabling first local elections in over 20 years.

title: Talks on future of Lebanon mission must begin soon: UN
text:
BEIRUT: UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix on Wednesday urged the UN Security Council to begin negotiations on the future of peacekeepers deployed in Lebanon, as Beirut campaigns for an extension to the mandate set to expire at the end of this year.

A UN peacekeeping force known as UNIFIL has been deployed in southern Lebanon since 1978 but the Security Council last year ordered the mission to begin withdrawing at the end of 2026.

Since a new war erupted in March between Israel and Iran-backed Lebanese armed group Hezbollah, the Lebanese government has campaigned for an extension to UNIFIL's mandate, citing its role in monitoring hostilities and facilitating aid deliveries to villages in Israeli-occupied zones.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres earlier this year presented proposals for a continued uniformed UN presence in Lebanon but no action has been taken yet, Lacroix said.

"These proposals are on the table of the Security Council. There has been no movement in the Security Council until now, but I believe that the negotiations will begin ... shortly, in earnest," he said.

"I think it would be better to have a decision soon rather than later, right? Because that would clarify also the horizon for us, certainly from the more limited point of view of our own planning," he said.

Diplomats say the US is not supportive of an extended mandate for UNIFIL, but Lacroix said it was important to focus on Lebanon's request and that negotiations at the Security Council could yield a constructive outcome.

Some 7,500 UNIFIL peacekeepers are still deployed at about 50 positions in southern Lebanon, which would be expected to be handed over to Lebanese army troops if no new UN force is agreed. But since most of those posts lie in territory now occupied by the Israeli military, it remains unclear how Lebanese soldiers could deploy to take over the positions.

Lacroix said that clarity on whet­her a new UN force would deploy to southern Lebanon would help UNI­FIL make sure it does not "leave those positions prematurely before we know what could come next".

In addition to facilitating aid deli­veries and monitoring hostilities, the force operates a hotline to ease any tensions between the Lebanese and Israeli militaries.
ir_summary: UN urges Security Council to negotiate future of peacekeeping mission in Lebanon as mandate nears expiration amid Israel-Hezbollah conflict.

title: Colombia opens embassy to Israel in Jerusalem
text:
JERUSALEM: Colombia on Wednesday officially opened its embassy in Jerusalem, joining a small group of countries including the United States in taking the symbolic step of backing Israeli sovereignty in the contested city.

The vast majority of countries keep their embassies to Israel in Tel Aviv on the grounds that the status of Jerusalem will be settled in a final resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

"This is an important date for the State of Israel. It's also an important date for the city of Jerusalem," Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said during a ceremony while signing the Colombian embassy's guest book.

Colombia's new hard-right president, Abelardo de la Espriella, in July announced that he would move his country's embassy to Jerusalem, a sharp shift from his leftist predecessor. In 2024, president Gustavo Petro severed ties with Israel, one of Colombia's key security partners, over its offensive in the Gaza Strip.

Colombian Foreign Minister Omar Bula said Tuesday's move was "a concrete step toward the restoration of our diplomatic relations; a relationship that should never have been interrupted." "Israel is a strategic partner; it always has been, and from now on it will be so with even greater determination and strength," said Colombian ambassador Tania Gilinski.

"This is the beginning of a golden age in relations between our two countries," Saar said. The Palestinian Authority condemned the move. In a statement, its Foreign Ministry said that "opening an embassy to Israel in occupied Jerusalem constitutes a violation of international legitimacy resolutions…, undermines the international consensus on the legal status of the holy city, and infringes upon the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people." President Donald Trump shattered international consensus in 2018 during his first term by moving the US embassy to Jerusalem, which is home to Israel's parliament, prime minister and most other major governmental institutions.

Since Trump's move, only a handful of small, US-aligned countries have followed suit — Fiji, Guatemala, Honduras, Papua New Guinea, Paraguay and Nauru. Kosovo and Somaliland, which are not member-states of the United Nations, have also opened what they consider their embassies in Jerusalem.

Argentine President Javier Milei, another right-wing Latin American who is an outspoken supporter of Israel, has promised to move his country's embassy to Jerusalem. The status of Jerusalem is one of the thorniest issues in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

Former Colombian president Gustavo Petro broke diplomatic relations with Israel in 2024 over its actions in Gaza and had heavily criticised Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Petro also halted coal exports to Israel, closed Colombia's embassy in Tel Aviv and recalled its ambassador, a move Israel said was antisemitic and a reward for Hamas.

"It is also recognition of a historical truth that no honest person can deny. Today, we are taking a concrete step towards restoring diplomatic relations between our countries, relations that should never have been broken. Israel is a strategic partner. It always has been, and from now on, it will be an even stronger one," Colombian Minister of Foreign Affairs Omar Bula said at the opening.

Israel's foreign ministry noted that Saar and Bula will hold bilateral talks on Wednesday. The Colombian foreign ministry said in a statement the meeting will focus on political dialogue, security and defence cooperation, the strengthening of trade and new opportunities for investment.

Israel occupied East Jerusalem and annexed it in 1967, in a move not recognised by the vast majority of the international community. In August, Colombia's new hard-right government recognised Israel's claim over the Golan Heights, which it seized from Syria in 1967.

The US was until then the only country to recognise Israel's annexation of the territory in 1981. The United Nations maintains that the plateau is Syrian territory under Isr­aeli military occupation.
ir_summary: Colombia opens embassy in Jerusalem, aligning with Israel and breaking from international consensus on the contested city's status.

title: Buildings set ablaze in violent Albanian protests
text:
TIRANA: Demonstrators and riot police clashed in Albania's capital on Wednesday in a second straight day of violence triggered by student protests calling for better university conditions and Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation.

Over several hours, police deployed water cannon and tear gas while demonstrators targeted government buildings and shops in Tirana, smashing windows and on at least one occasion setting a building on fire.

Riot police have routinely tried to push back hundreds of protesters, including with tear gas, but the crowd showed little sign of dispersing. Demonstrators hurled paving stones and petrol bombs, set fire to bins that sent plumes of black smoke into the air, and used street fencing to erect barricades.

Protesters also attacked the finance ministry, using fencing to smash windows and break down doors, with some briefly entering the building. Pushed back by police, protesters moved towards the prime minister's office, where they threw stones at the building and officers, who responded with water cannon.

Earlier, this news agency saw two people climb over the education ministry wall and throw flares into the building. Thick black smoke poured from a window shortly afterwards. Firefighters quickly extinguished the blaze.

Nearby, a group of men smashed the windows of a bank branch before setting fire to documents inside. Police intervened within minutes to extinguish the flames. In another incident, flames engulfed what appeared to be an abandoned building as demonstrators smashed nearby shop windows. Police had appealed for calm, but tensions remained high as darkness approached.

According to the health ministry, six police officers, eight protesters, three journalists and two passers-by received medical attention on Tuesday, including for exposure to tear gas, while 16 people were arrested.

During the night, people also burst through the doors of the municipality building, lighting a fire inside and damaging several other buildings, police said. Demonstrators originally gathered early on Tuesday to demand Rama's resignation and more support for students in the country, but the rally comes after months of anti-government demonstrations in the capital.

Police said officers had "faced constant violence" on Tuesday and were "pelted with stones, blunt objects, firecrackers and Molotov cocktails by groups of masked demonstrators".

Meanwhile, the European Union, which the Balkan nation aspires to join, voiced concern over what it called the "violent escalation at the protest in Tirana". "We take note of the allegations of excessive violence by the police against protestors and journalists," a statement by the EU delegation in Tirana said.

Calling for a prompt investigation, the delegation encouraged "all sides to de-escalate the tension".

For more than four months, anti-government protests have routinely drawn crowds in the tens of thousands.
ir_summary: Albanian students protest for better university conditions and PM's resignation, clashing with police and setting buildings on fire.

title: Judge extends White House access for CNN, MS NOW, Politico
text:
WASHINGTON: A federal judge extended access to the White House for CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists, deciding on Tuesday that President Donald Trump likely broke the law when he tried to ban them, in the latest ruling against him in the press freedom dispute.

US District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a written decision that elaborated on his Sept 24 emergency order that reinstated access for the journalists. The news organisations and press freedom groups have accused Trump of unconstitutional retaliation against journalists for coverage he does not like.

Kelly's order last month gave the CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists access to the White House grounds on a temporary basis. The judge issued a ruling called a preliminary injunction on Tuesday that will remain in effect until he makes a final judgment in the lawsuit brought by the news organisations, unless an appeals court lifts his order.

Kelly wrote that Trump's public remarks made clear that he banned the news outlets because he considered their reporting biased and inaccurate, and not because of national security concerns as government lawyers later asserted in court.

"Simply put, that is unlawful viewpoint discrimination," the judge wrote, adding that "no one should read this decision as suggesting that President Trump's complaints are meritless." Trump appointed Kelly in 2017 during his first presidential term.

Past presidents have battled with the press, but Trump's campaign against the media has been unprecedented. He has upended decades of tradition by denying basic access to many major news organisations, launching personal attacks on journalists for their reporting and elevating media outlets seen as more sympathetic to the administration. He also has filed lawsuits against multiple news outlets.
