ir_summary: Pakistani textile exporters request government support and reforms to address rising costs and maintain export competitiveness.

title: Massive reshuffle in KP bureaucracy under governor’s rule
text:
PESHAWAR: In a massive reshuffle in the provincial bureaucracy, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government, led by the governor, transferred most administrative secretaries, divisional commissioners and deputy commissioners.

A notification from the Human Resource Management Department (HRMD) said Amjad Ali Khan, the industries secretary, has been transferred and posted as the home and tribal affairs secretary. Matiullah Khan, the information department secretary, has been transferred and posted as the health secretary.

Inayatullah Wasim, chairman of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Abbottabad, has been posted as secretary of the elementary and secondary education (ESE) department, while Muhammad Khalid, ESE secretary, has been directed to report to HRMD.

Shahid Sohail Khan, secretary of the administration department, has been posted as law and parliamentary affairs secretary, while Akhtar Saeed Turk, the incumbent secretary, has been directed to report to HRMD. Muhammad Ayaz, secretary of the inter-provincial coordination department, has been posted as finance department secretary, while Kamran Afridi has been directed to report to HRMD from the finance department.

Similarly, Amir Sultan Tareen, the CM's principal secretary, has been posted as the industries secretary, while Fakhr Alam, who was awaiting posting in HRMD, has been posted as the secretary of the population welfare department. Yousaf Rahim has been posted as secretary of the relief, rehabilitation and settlement department.

Abidullah, chairman of the KP Textbook Board, has been transferred and posted as the secretary of the higher education department. Tahir Orakzai has been posted as the housing department secretary, while Manzoor Ahmed has been posted as secretary of public health engineering.

Tashfeen Haider, special secretary of the elementary and secondary education department, has been transferred and posted as secretary of the administration department.

Nisar Ahmed, energy and power secretary, has been transferred and posted as secretary of the science and information technology department, while Muhammad Zubair has been transferred from the transport and mass transit department to the energy and power department.

Mines and Mineral Secretary Muhammad Israr, Communication and Works Secretary Ziaul Haq, Religious Affairs and Haj Secretary Attaur Rehman, Irrigation Secretary Abid Khan, Housing Secretary Anwar Khan, Higher Education Department Secretary Amber Ali Khan, Relief and Rehabilitation Secretary Sohail Khan and Population Secretary Aneela Mahfooz Durrani have been asked to report to HRMD.

Zubair Ahmed, special secretary of the finance department, has been posted as the secretary of the transport and mass transit department, while Amir Latif has been posted as the mines and minerals secretary.

Saqib Raza has been posted as the communication and works department secretary, while Idress Khan, secretary of the Benevolent Fund department, has been posted as the secretary of the auqaf, hajj and religious and minority affairs department. Hamidullah Shah has been posted to the excise and taxation department, while Amir Afaq has been appointed as the agriculture department secretary.

Khalid Ilyas, secretary of the excise and taxation department, has been transferred and posted as secretary of the irrigation department. Masood Younas has been posted as the inter-provincial coordination secretary, while Bakhtiar Khan has been posted as the secretary of information and public relations.

Fayyaz Ali Shah, the health department secretary, has been transferred and directed to report to HRMD, while Mian Adil Iqbal, from the science and information technology department, has also been directed to report to HRMD. Bannu Commissioner Khalid Mah­mood has been posted as the Peshawar commissioner, while Muhammad Ali Shah, who was awaiting posting in HRMD, has been posted as the Mardan commissioner.

Naeemullah, the PDMA director, has been transferred and posted as the Bannu commissioner, while Perwaiz, the special secretary of the agriculture department, has be­en posted as Kohat commissioner.

Shahrukh Ali, special secretary of the home and tribal affairs department, has been transferred and posted as Hazara commissioner. Iqbal Hussain, joint secretary from the federal government, has been posted as the Malakand commissioner.

Meanwhile, Peshawar Commis­sioner Riaz Khan Mehsud, Mardan Commissioner Habibullah Arif, Ko­­hat Commissioner Motasim Billah Shah, Malakand Commissioner Ma­­sood Ahmed and Hazara Com­mis­sioner Shahidullah Khan have been directed to report to HRMD. Besides, most deputy commissioners across the province have also been transferred.
ir_summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government conducts major bureaucratic reshuffle transferring multiple secretaries under governor's rule.

title: Govt denies role as anchor­per­son Iqrarul Hassan ‘picked up’ in Lahore
text:
LAHORE: Anchor­per­son Iqrarul Hassan was allegedly picked up by men in plainclothes, one of whom was wearing an identification tag of the Natio­nal Cyber Crime Investi­gation Agency (NCCIA), from his residence in Lahore in the early hours of Monday, his family said.

Punjab minister Azma Bokhari clarified police had not arrested Mr Hassan and the matter was being investigated.

In a video, Far­ah Iqrar said she and her husband were at their residence in DHA when men in plainclothes broke open the main gate, entered the pre­mises at around 3am and took Mr Hassan away.

She alleged that the men manhandled her during the operation and confiscated two mobile phones belonging to her husband, a laptop and her own mo­­bile phone. She added that a masked woman among the raiding party was wearing an NCCIA identification tag.

Mr Hassan had been critical of the government's policies on social media.

Advocate Mian Ali Ashfaq, counsel for Mr Hassan, said the NCCIA had denied arresting him.

He added that the anc­h­­or had not made any anti-state remarks. "We will move the Lahore High Court for his safe recovery," he said.
ir_summary: Pakistani anchorperson allegedly abducted by plainclothes officials after criticizing government policies on social media.

title: Ex-GB chief minister among several PTI leaders arrested
text:
GILGIT: Former Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister and PTI's regional president Khalid Khurshid Khan was arrested along with KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and several others at the speaker's house in Peshawar on Sunday night, according to the party's official social media page.

A police source also confirmed the arrest of PTI's GB chapter president, saying the former chief minister was wanted in multiple criminal cases.

"Khalid Khurshid and others have been arrested from the speaker's residence in Peshawar," the police source said. Sources said Mr Khurshid had been staying at the KP chief minister's residence since 2023 to avoid arrest by GB police. He reportedly moved to the assembly speaker's residence on Sunday after the imposition of emergency measures and governor's rule in KP. Sources could not confirm whether Mr Khurshid would be transferred to GB for court proceedings or taken to another city.

In December 2024, an anti-terrorism court in Gilgit-Baltistan sentenced Mr Khurshid to 34 years in prison and imposed a fine of Rs600,000 for threatening security institutions during a public gathering.

Anti-Terrorism Court Judge Rehmat Shah also directed the GB inspector general of police to arrest Mr Khurshid and ordered the director general of the National Database and Registration Authority to block his national identity card.

Mr Khurshid had failed to appear before the court despite repeated notices issued during the proceedings. The former chief minister was also named in several police cases related to PTI protests and alleged confrontations with law enforcement authorities in Lahore and Islamabad.

In March 2023, he was accused of using GB police personnel and government resources to provide security for former prime minister Imran Khan during efforts by authorities to arrest the PTI founder in Lahore.

The action followed the federal government's collection of evidence concerning the alleged use of GB police personnel and resou­rces for Imran Khan's security.

Mr Khurshid also faced allegations of using official resources to support PTI demonstrations.

Mr Khurshid was elected to the Gilgit-Baltistan Legislative Assembly from the Astore district on a PTI ticket in the 2020 general elections and subsequently became chief minister.

In July 2023, the GB Chief Court disqualified him from holding public office over allegations that he had obtained a licence from the GB Bar Council using a fraudulent educational degree.

The ruling ended his tenure as chief minister and triggered a political realignment in the region.

Following his disqualification, several PTI lawmakers broke ranks with the party, paving the way for the formation of a coalition government.

Haji Gulbar Khan, a dissident PTI lawmaker, subsequently became the new chief minister of the region.

Despite the court orders and multiple criminal cases, Mr Khurshid had remained outside the custody of GB police until his reported arrest on Sunday.
ir_summary: Former Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister and PTI leader arrested in Peshawar over multiple criminal cases including threatening security institutions.

title: JUI-F moves Senate resolution against KP governor’s rule
text:
ISLAMABAD: Senator Kamran Murtaza of the JUI-F has submitted a resolution in the Senate opposing the imposition of governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The Senate is likely to meet today (Tuesday). The resolution states that the House "expresses serious concern regarding any action that undermines provincial autonomy, the mandate of elected provincial institutions, democratic governance or the constitutional rights of the people".

Referring to Article 232 of the Constitution, Senator Murtaza argued that the provision begins with the words, "If the president is satisfied that a grave emergency exists…".

He contended that the presidential satisfaction required under Article 232 was lacking and that the proclamation of emergency appeared to have been issued mechanically by the president.

"The use of the words 'if the president is satisfied' makes the existence of the constitutionally prescribed conditions a fundamental prerequisite to the exercise of this extraordinary power. Therefore, if the president endorsed the advice tendered by the prime minister and issued the impugned proclamation without due consideration of the relevant circumstances or without the requisite constitutional satisfaction, such action is arbitrary, mechanical and an unconstitutional exercise of power."

Referring to the proclamation of emergency issued by the president under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution in KP, the resolution states that "this House reaffirms its commitment to the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, parliamentary democracy, the rule of law, provincial autonomy and the fundamental rights of the people".

The resolution further argues that at the time the summary was approved, the presidential satisfaction required under Article 232 of the Constitution was lacking.

It calls for the proclamation to be rescinded and revoked immediately, rather than waiting for the 10-day period for parliamentary approval to expire, and for it to be declared ultra vires the Constitution.
ir_summary: JUI-F senator submits resolution in Pakistan's Senate opposing governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as unconstitutional.

title: AJK leaders call for peaceful resolution of Poonch crisis
text:
MUZAFFARABAD: Political leaders in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) have called for a pe­­aceful and dignified resolution of the crisis in Poo­nch division, while ex­­pres­sing concern over the deteriorating law and order situation in the region.

The call was made at a meeting hosted by Muslim Conference president Sar­dar Attique Ahmed Khan at his Rawalpindi residence on Monday.

The meeting was atte­n­ded by PPP leader Sardar Yaqoob Khan, PML-N AJK president Shah Ghulam Qadir, PML-N leader Raja Farooq Haider, leader of the opposition in AJK Assembly Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin, and Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party AJK President Sardar Tanveer Ilyas and others.

According to a statement, the participants called for the restoration of internet services, uninterrupted supplies of food and medicines, and the resumption of communication links and free movement in Poonch division. They also demanded that eligible voters in the region be allowed to participate in the electoral process without delay.

The meeting expressed deep concern over the law and order situation in AJK, particularly in Poonch division, and called for a political settlement of the crisis through peaceful and dignified means.
ir_summary: AJK political leaders demand peaceful resolution to Poonch crisis and restoration of services amid law and order concerns.

title: PPP urges constitutional compliance on KP emergency
text:
ISLAMABAD: A day after the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtun­kh­­wa, the PPP on Monday stres­sed the need to adhere to the Cons­titution in the current situation.

PPP Secretary General Nayyar Hussain Bukhari emphasised the importance of constitutional compliance, saying, "Legal requirements and the parliamentary process must remain fundamental to any extraordinary measure."

Reacting to the imposition of emergency in KP, he said the matter would be brought before parliament, where elected representatives would deliberate on it and take a decision in accordance with constitutional procedures.

Mr Bukhari said the PPP believed in democracy, constitutional supremacy and the sovereignty of parliament.

"The invocation of constitutional provisions may become necessary under extraordinary circumstances; however, any such measure must be based on constitutional requirements rather than political considerations and must remain within the limits prescribed by the Constitution," he added.

The PPP leader said questions had been raised about the KP government's performance in maintaining law and order and its alleged lack of cooperation in combating terrorism.

He said terrorist attacks on security institutions, police stations and places of worship had created serious difficulties for the public, while fear and insecurity had forced residents in several areas to remain confined to their homes.

Mr Bukhari stressed that effective measures to prevent cross-border infiltration and attacks from Afghanistan were essential to safeguarding Pakistan's national security.

He said responsible cooperation between the federal and provincial governments was necessary to eliminate terrorism and protect the lives and property of citizens.

The PPP leader said party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and President Asif Ali Zardari had made concerted efforts to resolve the issue.

However, attempts to find a solution through negotiations had not proved successful.

Mr Bukhari said parliament would have the opportunity to examine the imposition of emergency in KP and determine an appropriate course of action.
ir_summary: PPP calls for constitutional adherence after emergency imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

title: Federal agents search home of Trump critic Ilhan Omar
text:
WASHINGTON: US federal agents searched the Washington home of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of a criminal investigation, officials said, marking a dramatic escalation in President Donald Trump's confrontation with the outspoken lawmaker.

The search was conducted by agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of US immigration enforcement, according to Fox News, citing sources familiar with the matter. The operation, just three weeks before Omar seeks re-election in the Nov 3 midterms, raised concerns about longstanding Justice Department practices intended to prevent law enforcement actions from influencing elections.

The cable network reported that the operation was linked to a criminal fraud investigation concerning immigration paperwork submitted on behalf of the Somali-born congresswoman by her late father when she was a child.

Trump's border enforcement chief Tom Homan told Fox News he was unwilling to give details ahead of any official announcement but confirmed that an "investigation was ongoing for a while" and that "there was a warrant executed this morning." US media quoted the Justice Department confirming that agents had carried out a court-authorised search in the Washington area, but officials did not identify Omar or disclose the nature of the investigation.

The search reportedly began around 6am. Video footage apparently taken by a member of the public and posted to X showed several agents wearing HSI jackets outside Omar's Washington residence. Omar, 44, is a leftist Democrat and fierce critic of Trump, particularly his administration's sweeping crackdown on immigration. The Republican president has repeatedly clashed with Omar, who came to the United States from Somalia as a child and has frequently been the target of his political attacks.

In September, Homan said that Omar was the subject of an ongoing criminal investigation, but again declined to provide details. Omar said at the time that Homeland Security officials had not contacted her about any investigation, dismissing the allegations against her as politically motivated attacks.

There was no immediate public response from Omar to Monday's search. But Xochitl Hinojosa, a former director of public affairs at the Justice Department, criticised the timing of the search. "There's a longstanding rule at DOJ that you don't take overt actions like this before an election, especially when there's a candidate on the ballot," she wrote on X. Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, a senior fellow at the American Immigration Council, wrote on X that the "precedent set by this action is chilling," warning that raids targeting political candidates shortly before elections could become more common.
ir_summary: US federal agents search home of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar in immigration fraud investigation weeks before elections.

title: Nato warns Russia of tough response to any attack
text:
BRUSSELS: Nato's top commander warned Russia on Monday that his forces would destroy "anything and everything" involved in any attack if Moscow was "foolish enough" to launch an assault on alliance territory.

Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich stressed Nato was a defensive alliance. But he outlined a three-pronged approach of blocking, blunting and breaking enemy forces to make any attack "utterly futile".

His remarks come amid heightened tensions between Europe and Russia and lingering concerns among European allies over US President Donald Trump's commitment to Nato's mutual defence pact.

In recent days, Trump has announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin allowing Russia to supply diesel to global markets and renewed his criticism of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

European govts seek Nato assurance over Moscow's 'clandestine operations of arson, drone incursions and cyber disruptions'

European governments accuse Moscow of stepping up a campaign of sabotage, drone incursions and cyberattacks against them, while Russia warned last month it could use nuclear weapons if Nato attempted to cut off its Kaliningrad exclave. Grynkewich did not mention Russia by name but much of his message was clearly directed at Moscow. Nato's 2022 Strategic Concept describes Russia as the alliance's most significant security threat.

"If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight," he said. "We will, in short, ensure any attack, against any ally, proves utterly futile." Grynkewich said Nato's response would not be limited to forces involved in an initial attack. "Should the adversary choose to press the attack or commit his reserves, we will break the warfighting system engaged against us," he said.

"This includes not just the attacking force itself, but anything and everything that supports, sustains, and controls that force." Putin said this month Russia had no plans to attack any European country and wanted to coexist peacefully. Such declarations have not reassured European leaders, given Russia made similar statements before the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Russia has also repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage and other hybrid operations.

Grynkewich said he had decided to talk publicly about Nato's plans because recent acts of sabotage and arson had made people around the alliance nervous. "What I want to do is assure the one billion citizens of our alliance that we've got this. We know what we need to do. We know how we would do it," he said.

He said he also wanted to send a message to anyone considering harming Nato members. Grynkewich sought to downplay concerns about Washington's commitment to the alliance, recalling that Trump spoke of "love" at a Nato summit in Ankara in July. "I was in the room and I felt the love," he said.
ir_summary: NATO commander warns Russia of devastating military response to any attack on alliance territory amid heightened tensions.

title: Musk has ‘spent $366m to help Republicans’ win midterms
text:
NEW YORK: Elon Musk has spent roughly $366 million on the 2026 midterm elections so far, $276 million just since July, trying to help Republicans retain control of Congress, even as Democrats' chances of retaking the US House and Senate have improved.

Musk's largess, which was reported earlier by the New York Times, makes the world's richest person likely the single-biggest political donor in this year's races, according to campaign finance records. There is a lot at stake for Mu­­­sk with House Democrats calling for investigations into his government contracts as CEO of aerospace company SpaceX as well as his work running the Department of Government Efficiency under President Donald Trump.

Here's a breakdown of his political spending, which was confirmed by a spokesman for his super PAC America PAC. Musk has spent $366 million so far this election cycle, which began Jan 1, 2025.

Of that, Musk has donated at least $276 million to Republican groups and his own super PAC since July. Of the $276 million in third-quarter donations: $158 million went to the Senate Leadership Fund, the super PAC set up to help elect Republicans to the Senate that is aligned with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a Republican from South Dakota. $20 million went to the Congressional Leadership Fund, the super PAC set up for House Republicans that is aligned with House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Louisiana Republican. $76 million went to Musk's America PAC.
ir_summary: Elon Musk spent $366 million to support Republican candidates in the 2026 US midterm elections.

title: Gunman kills two Egyptians in Sudan capital
text:
KHARTOUM: A gunman killed two Egyptian nationals and wounded a third in Khartoum on Monday, a Sudanese security official said, two days after an airstrike blamed by a rights group on Egypt killed 72 people near the countries' shared border.

"A gunman opened fire on three Egyptian citizens," the official said. "Two of them died, while the third was injured and transferred to hospital." The official added that police had cordoned off the area and were searching for the attacker.

Egypt's foreign ministry said the victims were truck drivers and that its ambassador in Sudan had been tasked with checking on the injured man and arranging the return of the two bodies to Egypt. The motive behind the attack was not immediately clear, and it was unknown whether it was linked to the airstrike.

The border attack took place in a vast, mineral-rich region that stretches for hundreds of kilometres across the frontier and includes the disputed Halayeb Triangle, a territory claimed by both Sudan and Egypt.

The region has become a magnet for informal miners as Sudan's war has wrecked livelihoods and driven thousands toward the gold trade. Gold remains one of Sudan's few functioning economic lifelines and a major source of revenue for both sides of the conflict. The area is also a key corridor for smuggling.

Much of the gold extracted in army-controlled eastern Sudan is believed to pass through Egypt before reaching international markets via the United Arab Emirates, one of the world's largest gold trading hubs.

Saturday's attack is the second reported strike this year on Jabal al-Uqaydat. In June, airstrikes reportedly carried out by Egypt killed 23 workers at the same informal mine.

At the time, the Egyptian military did not claim responsibility but also said it had conducted a "large-scale operation" against illegal gold mining within its borders.
ir_summary: Gunman kills two Egyptian nationals in Khartoum amid tensions following a recent cross-border airstrike between Sudan and Egypt.

title: Bombings of Russian data centres ‘spur hopes for less disinformation’
text:
PARIS: Recent Ukrainian bombings of Russian data centres have drastically slashed the Kremlin's online propaganda and disinformation activities, some Ukrainian allies and internet users said on Monday.

"The Russian troll bots in my own feed have dropped dramatically already," exiled Russian chess grandmaster Garry Kasparov told millions of followers on X.

Many internet users claim to have noticed a sharp reduction in social media content in favour of US President Donald Trump, Russia or the AfD, a German anti-immigration and pro-Russian party.

They say the reduction is a direct result of strikes against Russian data centres, which have cut off Russian "bots" — autonomous computer programmes used to disseminate large quantities of low-quality content, often in the form of propaganda and disinformation.

At the Warsaw Security Forum on Monday, Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius recommended such attacks to ensure the security of the forthcoming elections in his country and in Poland. "We should ask Mr Zelensky to strike more data centres in Russia; I think that might help," he said, referring to Ukraine's president.

Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky told the forum that since his country began targeting Russian data centres, "it has suddenly become a little easier to breathe on many social media platforms".

Three attacks were reported last week against facilities belonging to Yandex — nicknamed the "Russian Google" — which has tens of millions of users for the country's most popular search engine, as well as its food delivery and taxi-booking apps.

Internet traffic originating from Yandex fell around 35 per cent following an attack on the Sasovo site, then plummeted 99pc compared with a week earlier following the closure of the Vladimir site, according to Cloudflare Radar, which monitors and analyses internet traffic worldwide.

However, experts on Russian online propaganda say it is too early to establish such a cause-and-effect relationship.

"There is currently no evidence to support the claim that the attack on the data centres silenced the Kremlin's 'troll farms'," Nikola Tulechki, a specialist in monitoring online disinformation operations for the organisation "Data for Good" said.

He said a widely shared Cloudflare graphic shows a drop in automated requests from a network controlled by Yandex to websites, and not from bots on social media.

The Antibot4Navalny collective, which tracks influence operations linked to Russia, also believes that the interpretation of the Cloudflare Radar charts is incorrect.

"To those implying that Kremlin-controlled social media bot/troll farms became silent after Ukraine hit a Yandex data center: Hate to disappoint you all," it posted on X.
ir_summary: Ukrainian bombings of Russian data centers reduce Kremlin disinformation and propaganda online.

title: Twenty buildings damaged by work on Athens subway
text:
ATHENS: Construction of a new line for the Athens subway network, halted for months, has damaged 20 buildings in one of the Greek capital's oldest districts, officials said on Monday.

"Safety is a non-negotiable priority for the state and for everyone involved in the project," Transport Minister Christos Dimas told reporters after a meeting on the project.

No building needs to be evacuated and the contractors constructing the project will cover expenses for repair works at each building in the central district of Kypseli, he added.

"The process now covers all 20 buildings with recorded damage," said Christos Fafoutis, the CEO of Elliniko Metro, the state company supervising the project. The Monday meeting followed a protest by hundreds of residents on Oct 3.

The residents of Kypseli, a central Athens district where some buildings are over a century old, had originally reported cracks and other damage to their property beginning in March. Construction work halted on May 8 and has not resumed since.

Elliniko Metro has said that boring in Kypseli found "unforeseeable and undetectable conditions identified in weak geological subsoil".

The Athens town hall and residents had requested written guarantees regarding the structural adequacy of the buildings and an independent public body to certify that these buildings are structurally sound, Mayor Haris Doukas said in July. "Once the works have been completed, the buildings will be safer than they were before," said Giorgos Stasinos, head of the Technical Chamber of Greece.
ir_summary: Athens subway construction damaged 20 historic buildings, prompting government response and resident protests over safety concerns.

title: Yemen escalation
text:
WITH the Houthi Ansarallah movement continuing to target Saudi Arabia, the region stands at a perilous juncture. The Houthi attacks — particularly those targeting the airport at Riyadh — are becoming increasingly destructive, with several people killed and hundreds reportedly injured in Saturday's strike.

The attack was said to be the deadliest the kingdom has witnessed in years. The airport attacks have been condemned internationally, and there have been mass flight cancellations.

The Saudis, who are backing the anti-Houthi Yemeni government, are poised to strike back at the pro-Iran group with even greater force. Yet a small window of opportunity has opened up, with the Iranian and Saudi foreign ministers discussing matters over the phone on Sunday. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reportedly told his Saudi counterpart Faisal bin Farhan that a military approach would "complicate" matters in Yemen, while offering Tehran's good offices to mediate with Ansarallah.

The Houthis are independent actors; framing them as the puppets of Tehran is inaccurate. Yet they do share ideological and geopolitical ground with Iran, and if Tehran talks, the Houthis are bound to listen. Therefore, involving Iran in talks between the Saudis and Houthis could produce positive results. If Riyadh has any reservations, Pakistan — which maintains channels with both Saudi Arabia and Iran — could also be involved. Oman could be another mediating party, as the sultanate has close ties with both Riyadh and Tehran, besides maintaining an open line with the Houthis. The fact is that Muslim countries — Arab and non-Arab — have a significant role to play in defusing the situation both within Yemen and between Saudi Arabia and Ansarallah.

The US has threatened to get involved in Yemen militarily again. This would be a recipe for great disaster. America has done enough damage in the Middle East, and it is the regional states that must lead the peace process. Whether Iran's offer is accepted, or Pakistan and Oman attempt a fresh push for a negotiated settlement, some key points must be kept in mind if there is to be long-term peace.

Firstly, the mutual security of Saudi Arabia and Yemen must be prioritised, and the targeting of civilian targets, such as airports, must stop. A temporary truce should then be called to allow the two sides a cooling-off period and come to the negotiating table. Within Yemen, durable peace can only be achieved through a Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned process, which takes on board all the country's tribes and communities. Such an agreement can also help bring peace to Saudi Arabia, while ending Yemen's humanitarian nightmare. However, escalation from either side can turn the Yemeni conflict into a regional war — something that all peace brokers must do their utmost to prevent.
ir_summary: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia escalate tensions, with diplomatic efforts involving Iran and potential mediators like Pakistan and Oman.

title: FBR told to digitise industrial monitoring by year-end
text:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) on Monday to complete digital monitoring of production in major industries by the end of December 2026 as part of efforts to narrow the gap between actual and potential tax collection.

Chairing a review meeting, the prime minister asked tax authorities to ensure that production monitoring for sales tax covered all manufacturing sectors by the end of the year.

Officials gave a detailed presentation on the results achieved so far through digital monitoring of industrial production.

According to an official announcement by the Prime Minister's Secretariat, the meeting was informed that the digital monitoring system had been fully installed in the sugar, cement, tobacco, tiles and fertiliser sectors.

The system was being installed in the textile, packaged water, packaged juice and packaged milk sectors, and the purchase of equipment for these industries had been completed.

The meeting was informed that the purchase of equipment for the steel, poultry and tyre sectors would be completed by Oct 15, while equipment for tea, household electronics, leather, paper and board, and oil and ghee would be procured by Oct 30.

The monitoring systems in all these sectors are expected to be fully operational by Dec 31, 2026.

The meeting was also informed that several textile companies had voluntarily installed the monitoring system despite resistance from some industries. These included Nishat Mills, Al-Karam Textile, Al-Karam Cotton Mills, J.K. Spinning Mills, Soorti Enterprises, Interloop Ltd, Faisal Spinning Mills, Ibrahim Fibres Ltd, Sapphire Textiles Ltd and Nishat Chunian.

The prime minister commended the companies for their initiative.

A review report on the gap between tax collection and tax potential was also presented to the prime minister, providing an estimate of the country's tax potential.

The meeting was informed that government measures over the past three years had resulted in an additional Rs1.3 trillion in tax collection, representing a 40 per cent increase. The additional revenue had been generated through enforcement measures.

Briefing the prime minister, the FBR said production monitoring was being strengthened through cameras under the faceless system.

The premier directed that obstacles to installing automated production monitoring systems equipped with cameras be removed.
ir_summary: Pakistan's prime minister directs FBR to complete digital monitoring of industrial production by end-2026 to improve tax collection.

title: Digital push could yield $80bn
text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakis­tan could realise economic benefits of $60 billion to $80bn over the next five years through digital transformation, with agriculture, real estate and healthcare expected to gain significantly.

A working paper issued by the Pakistan Digital Authority (PDA) says digitalisation is a major opportunity to accelerate economic growth, improve public service delivery, and streamline government operations.

The working paper has been forwarded to the Ministry of IT & Telecom. However, it notes that the lack of interoperability among government digital systems remains a significant challenge.

The paper adds that digital transformation could generate more than $9bn in economic benefits for the agriculture sector by 2030, while digital reforms in healthcare could yield savings of over $450m.

The real estate sector could attract an additional $15bn in investment by 2030 through digital transformation, the document states. Under the proposed digital framework, the authority will help develop a National Digital Master Plan and digital infrastructure to improve coordination between federal and provincial governments.

The National Digital Master Plan will focus on integrating government systems, reducing administrative bottlenecks and establishing common digital standards across public-sector institutions.

The proposed Pakistan Digital Stack will bring together digital identity, payment systems, and data-exchange mechanisms to enable seamless, secure interactions among government departments.
ir_summary: Pakistan's digital transformation plan could yield $60-80 billion in economic benefits through government system integration and sectoral reforms.

title: An ‘unprecedented’ two-pronged emergency
text:
ISLAMABAD: The federal government's decision to take two-pronged constitutional action in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa will not only render the provincial chief executive and legislature 'dysfunctional', but may also allow it to extend this state of affairs 'indefinitely'.

Soon after the federal government's announcement, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a press conference that the emergency was enforced for an indefinite period, not merely six months.

The president's decisions under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution will now be endorsed by separate sessions of the Senate and the National Assembly, and a joint sitting of both houses. Article 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan stipulates that, if the president believes that a provincial government cannot function in accordance with the Constitution, the federal government can assume control of the province.

This can be done either directly or by assigning the relevant functions to the provincial governor — hence the term governor's rule.

Under this arrangement, the powers of the provincial assembly can be exercised by parliament. However, neither the president nor the governor can assume the powers of the high court or suspend its operations.

Moreover, governor's rule can be imposed for an initial period of two months, with a joint sitting of parliament able to approve an extension of up to two months at a time.

In total, governor's rule can remain in place for a maximum of six months.

Meanwhile, under Article 232, which pertains to the proclamation of an emergency, the provincial assembly continues to function as usual. However, if a provincial law conflicts with a federal law enacted by parliament, the latter takes precedence.

Talking to Dawn, lawyer Basil Nabi Malik explained that the chief minister would remain in office during a state of emergency. However, the federal government could assume certain functions of the provincial government.

An emergency also allows the federal government to make provisions it considers necessary and suspend certain constitutional provisions relating to provincial bodies. However, as with governor's rule, the federal government cannot assume the powers of a high court.

It also empowers parliament to confer powers and impose duties on federal government officers in the province.

It further stipulates that laws passed by parliament solely on account of the emergency will cease to have effect six months after the emergency ends.

The proclamation of emergency lapses after two months unless it is approved by a resolution of a joint sitting of parliament.

Pakistan Institute of Legislative Development and Transparency Ahmed Bilal Mehmoob told Dawn that invoking both articles of the Constitution together was an unprecedented move by the federal government.

In his view, this double-barrelled approach was deliberate, since Article 232 alone did not render the provincial assembly dysfunctional.

"In that case, the provincial assembly continues to function but cannot enact any law which contradicts federal legislation. If the provincial assembly continues to work, it can create a nuisance for the governor and his new provincial set-up," he added.

However, Article 234 can be enforced for an indefinite period, and also serves to neuter the provincial assembly. "This was the reason the Centre used both articles in proclamation of emergency in KP," he added.

The Pildat chief, however, noted that under Article 234, the provincial assembly will automatically become functional after six months.
ir_summary: Pakistan's federal government imposes emergency measures in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, rendering provincial government dysfunctional indefinitely.

title: Where is Sohail Afridi?
text:
PESHAWAR / ISLAMABAD: A couple of hours after the imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was announced on Sunday, the PTI claimed that its now-dysfunctional chief minister Sohail Afridi, who was leading the party's protest march towards Islamabad, had been taken into custody along with some other leaders.

Shafi Jan, an aide to Mr Afridi who had been accompanying him on the protest march, claimed that his boss had been "taken into custody". Shahid Khattak, a PTI MNA, also claimed that Mr Afridi had been arrested.

Later, the PTI issued a statement condemning the "arrest" of Mr Afridi and other party leaders, describing it as an act of "political victimisation and an attempt to weaken the province's elected leadership and democratic institutions".

However, there was no official confirmation of his detention, although sources said that Mr Afridi and PTI's provincial president Junaid Akbar were under house arrest under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO).

Party spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram was quoted as saying that Mr Afridi's "arrest" could not be viewed in isolation from the federal government's decision to impose emergency and governor's rule.

"The developments reflect a broader effort to bypass elected institutions and undermine the constitutional authority of the province," he added.

"The arrest of Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and Junaid Akbar has exposed the political nature of the federal government's actions. These measures are not directed at addressing security challenges; they are intended to weaken [the] PTI, undermine the elected government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and disregard the democratic will of its people," he said.

Mr Akram demanded the "immediate and unconditional release" of Mr Afridi, Mr Akbar and "all other political detainees arrested in connection with the ongoing action against PTI".

He also demanded that the federal government publicly disclose the "legal grounds, specific charges and procedural basis for the arrests of the chief minister and the PTI provincial president".

However, he sounded less certain during a subsequent appearance on Geo News, saying the party had received reports of the arrests of Mr Afridi and Mr Akbar, but had been unable to confirm whether Mr Jan and Mr Khattak were also taken into custody.

"We are unable to contact some people […] Because the internet has been suspended in several areas, we are unable to make contact. You do not know the havoc they have created in KP. People are escaping and going into hiding," he said.

In a clip shared on PTI's official X account, the party's secretary general Salman Akram Raja said, "We do not know where Sohail Afridi is, in what condition he has been kept. Junaid Akbar is also missing."

In a separate statement, the PTI claimed that Mr Afridi, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and the party's provincial president, Junaid Akbar, had been abducted. "Many PTI MNAs and MPAs were already abducted in the last few weeks," it added.

PTI KP Deputy Information Secretary Ikram Khatana said in a statement that "the arrest of Sohail Afridi, Junaid Akbar, Babar Saleem Swati, Shahid Khattak makes it clear that it [the federal government] cannot compete with people".

Meanwhile, State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry told Geo News that some individuals had been detained in view of the law and order situation but did not confirm whether Mr Afridi was among them. "The people who are not wanted in any case will be released," he added. "Those wanted in criminal cases will be dealt with accordingly and the rest would be sent home."
ir_summary: PTI claims its Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi was arrested after emergency was imposed in the province.

title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in governor’s hands after Centre slaps emergency
text:
ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday imposed a state of emergency in 12 districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and placed the province under governor's rule following the president's approval of recommendations made by the federal cabinet.

The measures were appr­oved under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution a day after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met President Asif Ali Zardari to discuss the country's overall security situation.

Following the proclamation, internet and cellular disruptions were reported from parts of the province.

Although there was no official word, internet watchdog NetBlocks said network data showed a major disruption to internet connectivity in parts of KP after emergency was imposed.

The emergency proclamation listed the districts of Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Mar­wat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, and South Waziristan.

The federal government also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in KP. On the ground, shipping containers were placed around the city of Peshawar to block several roads, with heavy police deployment.

The decision to impose emergency provisions came during a special meeting of the federal cabinet on Sunday, chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, where he was briefed on the security situation in KP.

A statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the "provincial government's deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism".

The members proposed, given the "gravity" of the situation, that the PM advise the president to exercise "his constitutional authority and impose an emergency in the province under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution".

Addressing the cabinet, the premier said the PTI-led KP government cannot be allowed to derail the stabilising economy amid tensions between the two sides. "I will not allow them [PTI] to destabilise the economy," he said during the meeting.

On terrorism in KP and Balochistan, the premier said, "The way common citizens are being martyred, the way police officials and security officials, children and mothers [..] there can be nothing more heart-wrenching."

The Cabinet Division issued an order stating that after proclamation of emergency, the government of KP "cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution".

Earlier in the day, the federal government appointed Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam Irfan as the chief secretary of KP. In a separate notification, the federal government also placed Muhammad Yahya Akhunzada at the disposal of the KP government with "immediate effect and until further orders".

Exercising its powers under Article 232, the government ordered that an Area Development Secretariat (ADS), under the superintendence of the Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC), be immediately established to "restore law and order, safeguard the security of the citizens of Pakistan and ensure good governance and development" in Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, South Waziristan (Upper) and South Waziristan (Lower).

It said that the ARDC shall be a representative council comprising the notables from the designated districts and shall be headed by a chairman. The order further said that the ADS shall be headed by the additional chief secretary of the designated districts, who shall be the administrator of these areas. It said that the administrator shall perform all the functions of and exercise all executive, administrative, and law enforcement powers vested in or exercisable by the provincial government in the designated districts.

"All orders, notifications, directions, or actions taken by the administrator shall have the same legal effect as if issued by the provincial government," it read.

The order further said that the provisions of Chapter 3 (provincial governments) of the Constitution's Part IV and Clause 3 of Article 175, which pertains to the separation of the judiciary from the executive, will not apply to the designated districts. The KP Government Rules of Business 1985 will not apply either.

Defending its move, the government alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a "nexus" with terrorist groups. The press conference by government ministers — Atta Tarar, Mohsin Naqvi, Azam Nazeer Tarar, and Tallal Chaudhry — came shortly after the Centre's decision was announced.

Addressing the media in Islamabad, the information minister said all cabinet members who attended Sunday's meeting were of the view that the "PTI government in KP is hand in glove with terrorists and has an unholy alliance with terrorists".

"Terrorists have a clear say in how each district will be run," he alleged, citing reports from the Intelligence Bureau and law enforcement agencies (LEAs). The minister went on to allege that a "power-sharing formula was gradually taking shape between terrorists and the PTI's KP government, which was starting from southern districts and was ingressing further into the entire KP".

Meanwhile, the interior minister warned the groups gathered in parts of KP — an apparent reference to PTI supporters taking part in its protest march — to disperse as they did not have any "provincial protection".

"Whoever is caught, complete legal action will be taken and that person themselves will be responsible for it. We will deal with them strictly, so it is my request that please disperse."

Responding to a query, Mr Naqvi said, "We have to restore law and order in KP, and we will take whatever action is needed for that, and we will normalise the situation as soon as we can."

Asked about the reported arrests of KP ministers, Mr Naqvi said individuals would be held under preventative detention where required to maintain law and order, whereas those "wanted will be arrested".

On the KP emergency, the law minister explained that an Area Development Secretariat (ADS), overseen by the governor, has been formed by the federal government to directly manage 12 districts "that were nearly in a war situation".

He noted that parliament assumes the legislative powers of the provincial assembly as the latter stands non-functional.
ir_summary: Pakistan's federal government imposes emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa due to security concerns and provincial government disengagement.

title: Rs268bn power tariff burden on consumers opposed
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) has opposed an additional Rs268 billion burden on consumers sought by former Wapda distribution companies (Discos) through prior-year adjustments in power tariffs.

In a comprehensive representation, the country's top business body, representing large and small businesses, including manufacturing industries, asked the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) to reject the "inflated claims" previously disallowed by the regulator or disputed by third parties.

The representation follows tariff petitions filed by 10 Discos seeking adjustments to the indexation of multiyear tariffs (2025-30) for calendar year 2027 and other consumer-end tariff adjustments.

Collectively, the Discos have claimed Rs2.64 trillion in revenue requirements for CY2027 on account of distribution and supply of power.

The FPCCI said it had constituted a special Energy Advisory Committee (EAC) to review tariff filings, including claims related to working capital, power purchase prices, prior-year adjustments (PYAs) and returns on revenue base.

The committee found that Discos were seeking to pass hundreds of billions of rupees in prior-year adjustments on to consumers.

It said a substantial portion of these claims was retrospective, contested by third parties or previously disallowed by Nepra. Some claims were inconsistently calculated against the Discos' own formulas or lacked sufficient disclosure for independent verification.

The EAC reviewed all 10 Discos' CY2027 indexation and PYA petitions, including financial statements and annexures, on behalf of FPCCI's constituent chambers, trade and industry associations.

According to the FPCCI, Islamabad Electric Supply Company's (Iesco) PYA claims exceeded 212 per cent of its proposed annual margin, while Sukkur Electric's claims amounted to 113pc of its distribution margin.

Faisalabad Electric's PYA claims amounted to 91pc of its distribution and supply margin, followed by Multan at 68pc and Quetta at 60pc.

The corresponding shares for Lahore, Peshawar and Gujranwala electric companies stood at 41pc, 40pc and 32pc, respectively. Tribal Electric did not disclose the figures.

"These are not routine formula-based true-ups and ought not to be approved as such," the FPCCI said.

The representation included itemised objections for each Disco and a cross-company comparison, identifying disputed amounts, grounds for objections and proposed disallowances based on petitions, financial statements and annexures published by Nepra.

The FPCCI demanded that its objections be made part of each Disco's tariff-setting process, including public hearings, and that the companies respond in writing to specific objections before the hearings.

It also urged Nepra to reject undifferentiated lump-sum PYA claims, require component-wise substantiation and allow trade and business bodies to participate in hearings.

Faisalabad Electric has sought Rs535bn in revenue requirements for 2027, including Rs57bn in PYAs. The FPCCI called for rejecting Rs26bn in claims involving 11-year post-retirement benefits and previously disallowed supplementary charges.

Gujranwala Electric sought Rs70.4bn, including Rs17bn in PYAs linked to 19-year-old Azad Jammu and Kashmir sovereign receivables. Sukkur Electric claimed Rs68bn, including Rs36bn in PYAs.

Lahore Electric sought the highest revenue requirement, Rs759bn, including approximately Rs33bn in PYAs. The FPCCI said Rs27bn in claims were liable to be rejected because they had not been verified.

Iesco submitted the largest PYA claim of Rs158bn within its Rs525bn revenue requirement. The FPCCI said 70pc of Iesco's PYA claims were either disputed or involved noncash items, had been filed as a lump sum and should be rejected.

Peshawar Electric sought Rs233bn in revenue requirements, including Rs35bn in PYAs. Of these, Rs33bn related to seven-year-old input tax claims that the FPCCI described as inadmissible.
ir_summary: Business group opposes power companies' request to pass Rs268 billion in tariff adjustments to consumers, urging regulator to reject claims.

title: OBITUARY: The last living link to Khairpur’s princely past
text:
THE significance of Mir Geo­rge Ali Murad Khan Talpur II, the last ruler of the former princely state of Khairpur who died on Oct 5, lies in more than just having witnessed the disappearance of a world. In Khairpur's final years, he presided over an experiment in representative government and social development that deserves to be remembered.

Born in Brighton on June 29, 1933, the eighth Talpur ruler of Khairpur was named George after King George V, whom his father, Mir Faiz, admired. In 1944, his father suffered a breakdown and the state was then run by the British Resident with the aid of local ministers.

The announcement of the end of the British Indian Empire under the June 3, 1947 plan meant that Khairpur, in treaty relations with the British since 1838, would regain its sovereign status on Aug 15, 1947, when British paramountcy laps­ed. Thus, in order to make the transition smoother, the British deposed the ill Mir Faiz, and on July 24, 1947 the 14-year-old George Ali Murad became the Mir of Khairpur, with his uncle Ghulam Hussain Talpur as Regent.

Khairpur celebrated Aug 15 as its Independence Day, but its position on the railway linking Punjab and Sindh made it strategically vital to Pakistan. Negotiations followed, and on Oct 3, 1947 the regent signed the Instrument of Accession, making Khairpur the first contiguous princely state to join Pakistan. It ceded defence, foreign affairs and communications, but retained its sovereignty and the power to accept or reject a future constitution of Pakistan.

Joining Pakistan brought new challenges and opportunities and Mir George Ali Murad rose to both. After a stint at Cambridge, he assumed full ruling powers in September 1951. Teaming up with Mumtaz Kizilbash, chief minister since 1948, he oversaw a series of reforms that changed the nature of the state and the life of its people.

In a first, Khairpur held Pakistan's first elections on the basis of universal adult franchise and its 15-member Assembly, elected in May 1950, was the country's first fully democratic chamber. No wonder then, when Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan inaugurated it, he noted that Khairpur had "stolen a march on others".

The genius of the Mir was that he recognised and appreciated democratic government and worked with it for the uplift of his people. Soon under the Government of Khairpur Act 1953 the state became a province, with the Mir as its constitutional head, akin to a governor.

Khairpur also led the way in development. Its income nearly tripled, from Rs5.7 million in 1948 to Rs16.9m in 1955, giving Khairpur a per capita budget income of Rs53 against Punjab's Rs20. No doubt this was spurred on by the Khairpur Textile Mill, established in 1951, which employed over 2,000 people. Over 22 per cent of the budget went to education, the highest of any unit in Pakistan. Education was free up to Matric, with free books and hostels, and elementary education was compulsory for boys. As a result, its literacy rate nearly doubled in 10 years.

But just as things were going well, all came to a halt. Faced with the centre's plan to merge all of western Pakistan, the Assembly protested that Khairpur was "ahead of even the Governor's provinces in Pakistan in several respects" and that its people "cannot be compelled against their will to merge…" But these protests fell on deaf ears. Under mounting pressure, the Assembly voted for merger on Nov 10, 1954 and the Mir signed on the dotted line, ceding to Pakistan "his sovereignty and all his rights, authority and powers as Ruler of the State". A state founded in 1783 came to an end with the inauguration of One Unit on Oct 14, 1955.

The merger of the state took its toll on the Mir. He withdrew from public life, but remained deeply attached to Khairpur's heritage and landscape, turning the family's old hunting ground at Mehrano into an exemplary wildlife sanctuary.

Yet his most enduring attachment was to the people of Khairpur. In his foreword to my book A Princely Affair (2015), he lamented: "Sixty years after the 'merger' with Pakistan, the people of Khairpur are still waiting for Pakistan to provide even a fraction of the services and benefits provided by my state." With his death, the last living link to Khairpur's princely past is gone. However, the question of what that past achieved, and what its people still expect from Pakistan, remains.

The writer is dean, School of Economics and Social Sciences at IBA Karachi and author of A Princely Affair: Accession and Integration of the Princely States of Pakistan 1947-55.
ir_summary: Obituary of the last ruler of Khairpur princely state, covering his role in accession to Pakistan and governance reforms.

title: Army called ‘in aid of civil power’
text:
ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, after imposing an emergency and governor's rule in the province.

The authorisation of the army deployment was made through Statutory Regulatory Order, issued by the interior ministry on Sunday.

According to the order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the federal government authorised the deployment of army troops and assets in aid of civil power for the "safety of life, security of persons and property of citizens as well as security of government installations" in the province.

The authorisation lasts for the duration of the proclamation issued regarding the imposition of an emergency and governor's rule. The notification cited powers conferred to the government under Article 245 of the Constitution.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, in consultation with the Military Operations Directorate at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, would determine the number of troops and assets necessary, the notification added.

Copies of the order were forwarded to the president's secretary, prime minister's adviser, the KP governor's secretary, the Military Operations Directorate GHQ Rawalpindi, the KP home secretary, the inspector general of police (IGP) in the province, the Peshawar High Court registrar and other officials.

The order, issued by Section Officer CAF(C) Dr G.M. Mahmoodi, will be published in the next issue of Gazette of Pakistan Part-II.

The emergency imposition comes a day after PM Shehbaz met President Zardari and discussed the country's overall security situation.

That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations.

On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government's efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.
ir_summary: Pakistan's federal government deploys army in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under emergency rule for security and protection of government installations.

title: Another slain seaman’s family seeks return of his remains
text:
KARACHI: Just days after kidnapped sailors from MT Honour 25 were reunited with their families, another Pakistani seafarer's family is seeking the return of his mortal remains, following his demise after his ship came under attack near the Strait of Hormuz last month.

Muhammad Hammad Obaida, a third engineer and crew member aboard the Panama-flagged oil tanker MT El Gaia, was killed in an attack on the vessel on Sept 13, off the coast of Oman.

Nearly a month on, however, the grieving family in Pakistan, including his three-year-old son and pregnant wife, is still waiting for his repatriation.

Media reports provide conflicting accounts of the incident, which took place north of Oman's Musandam peninsula. According to multiple accounts, the tanker came under attack on Sept 13, while Reuters reported that it was towed to an Omani port around five days later.

While US and Iranian authorities traded blame over who was behind the strike, the bodies of two sailors — a Pakistani and an Indian — who had perished in an engine room fire were only discovered days after the incident, when the men were found to be missing during a headcount.

According to Hammad's family, they came to know about the incident through one of his colleagues on Sept 26.

Hammad had left home only a few days earlier, on Sept 6. Just a day before the attack, he had spoken to his mother over a video call.

"He was showing me around the ship… He was happy to be back at work," his mother, Ather Pervaiz, told Dawn.

Hammad, 34, was a qualified marine engineer who had graduated from Glasgow University in the UK.

When his younger brother Fawwad took out his phone to show us a picture, Hammad's three-year-old son, Musa, who had been busy playing with blocks on the floor, suddenly looked up and ran to take the phone from his uncle.

"This is my Baba," the toddler exclaimed, adding, "He is with Allah Mian [God Almighty] now."

He kissed the phone screen as both his elders struggled to hold back tears.

"Hammad's son needs to say a final goodbye to him. His young widow is expecting their second child. His father, brother, sisters and I have accepted what happened as God's will. But please bring us his remains so that we can at least give him a respectful burial," Ms Pervaiz said quietly.

Fawwad explained that despite writing countless letters and rea­ching out to the Pakistan Embassy in Oman, the Foreign Office and the prime minister through social media, the family had received no clear official response.

"We also approached the Sindh government… and were told that the matter was in the government's knowledge," he added.

Fawwad said the Pakistani embassy in Oman had confirmed that two bodies were awaiting DNA testing in the country, but no Pakistani authority had collected a DNA sample from the family to expedite identification.

"I am also in touch with Vivek, the brother of Indian seafarer Sumit Kumar, whose body was found alongside my brother's," he stated.

When contacted, the Foreign Office confirmed that the bodies of a Pakistani and an Indian seafarer were lying in a hospital mortuary in Oman, awaiting DNA testing for identification.

Responding to Dawn's query, the FO spokesperson said the bodies had been severely disfigured, making DNA testing necessary and delaying the repatriation of the remains to their families.
ir_summary: Pakistani seafarer's family seeks repatriation of remains after he was killed in a ship attack near Oman, amid conflicting reports.

title: Perilous misstep
text:
THE federal government on Sunday made good on its threat to dismiss an elected government and impose governor's rule and emergency in KP. The president obliged.

The head of state, the only civilian elected twice to that office, has now imposed governor's rule three times: Punjab in 2009, Balochistan in 2013, and now KP — though the ruling PML-N is the main driver behind the latest move. His party, the PPP, has done so six times in the short history of Pakistani democracy, the others being in 1973 (Balochistan), 1975 (the then NWFP), and 1994 (again, KP). There is, therefore, nothing novel about Sunday's move. However, it is a measure that has never achieved what its authors intended, and has more often than not backfired. That, perhaps, is why even those unsympathetic to the PTI government in Peshawar had been warning Islamabad not to take this step. In going ahead with it, the centre assumes responsibility for any blowback.

The imposition of governor's rule in Balochistan in 1973 is instructive. In February of that year, the then prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto dismissed the Balochistan government led by Sardar Attaullah Mengal, and also removed the then governor, Mir Ghaus Bakhsh Bizenjo. The centre ruled directly through Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti and sent in the army, fuelling an already smouldering insurgency. Many elected Baloch leaders turned separatist. The province never really recovered. KP is not Balochistan, and the PTI is no separatist movement. But the parallel of an elected leadership being swept aside on the pretext of security is unmistakable. The experience of the 1973 decision should be seen as a warning that this is how estrangement from the federation begins.

There is no political justification for governor's rule. If the authorities felt terrorism was increasing in some tribal districts and adjoining areas, they could have limited themselves to imposing a targeted emergency under Article 232, as they have already done. To deprive an entire province of its elected government is not only undemocratic; it can also be severely counterproductive, as history shows. The stated reason for Sunday's decision is terrorism. The real target is perceived to be the only provincial government the opposition held, and the agitation it was leading. The PTI government may have faltered on several fronts, but in a democratic society, those failings are supposed to be addressed through the electoral process, not through executive fiat. Under Article 234, the proclamation lapses within two months unless parliament approves it. That is where this ill-considered action should be challenged on principle: lawmakers would do well to scrutinise it, and the courts to test whether the constitutional threshold was actually met. Islamabad must extricate itself from this quagmire before it deepens, and leave KP's governance to those its people have elected to oversee it.
ir_summary: Pakistan's federal government imposes governor's rule in KP province, dismissing an elected government citing security concerns.

title: Import fraud
text:
THE under-invoicing of imports from China is not an allegation. It is an open secret in Pakistan's markets — one that has been known for years. The gap between imports recorded from China and what China itself reports exporting is estimated to be in the range of $3.5-5bn in any single year. The Faisalabad loom owners have described this practice as one of the reasons their business is suffering. Yarn and cloth are the visible case, but the practice runs through the entire import trade from China — from machinery parts and chemicals to electronics, tyres, and household goods. Traders declare a fraction of the true value, pay duty and sales tax on that fraction, and sell at prices no domestic competitor can match. It could not happen at this scale without Customs. Valuation is checked at the port. When the same understatement recurs across the same products, importers, clearing agents, and officers who pass the consignments, year after year, it points past carelessness to facilitation.

The damage is easy to trace. The exchequer loses duty and tax every day. Local manufacturers are forced to compete against goods whose prices have been shaved by a pen stroke. Mills close, looms are sold, workers go home. Then the same industry is told to become competitive and increase exports. It cannot, while its home market is being undercut by tax evasion that the state declines to acknowledge. It also corrupts what the country knows about itself. Imports are undercounted, so the trade deficit and the revenue gap are misstated, and policy is built on wrong numbers. The tools are already in place. Pakistan and China operate an electronic data exchange between their Customs administrations, and Islamabad has asked Beijing for real-time data. Applied to every shipment, not just textiles, comparing the Chinese export declaration with the Pakistani goods declaration would show mismatches in value and quantity at once. Large gaps should mean investigation, penalties, and prosecution. It is an argument for collecting what the law already requires, from everyone, equally. Cheaper power and easier credit mean little to a producer who is underpriced at the border. The government has assured the loom owners that their problems will be resolved. Controlling under-invoicing at the Pakistan-China border should be a good start.
ir_summary: Pakistan faces widespread under-invoicing of Chinese imports causing revenue loss and harming local industries, with state complicity suspected.

title: Paralysed prisons
text:
PAKISTAN'S overcrowded jails distort the intention of imprisonment — rehabilitation, education, and occupational development. The Annual Prisons Data Report 2026, compiled by the National Commission for Human Rights and Justice Project Pakistan, reveals that attention to lengthy confinement, delays in trials, and difficulties in obtaining bail has been long overdue. It also finds that Pakistan's jails, built for 68,832 people, were operating at over 160pc of their capacity. The prison system currently holds 41,681 more people. As a result, 110,513 are packed in tight, squalid spaces. Three out of every four inmates are caught in legal paralysis and are awaiting trial. Punjab and Sindh have witnessed a substantial rise in inmate numbers, with prisons in KP and Balochistan still operating within capacity.

That the prison system is fractured is no surprise. Dismal sanitation, malnutrition, absent healthcare, and overcrowding define it. Not only are inmates compelled to devise sleeping rosters, they also face mental health hazards. Those with psychosocial debilities face endless jail time and abuse without medical care. Troublingly, the number of women in jail is on the rise. Since 2024, their numbers have gone up by 46pc; a number of children, too, await trial. These conditions illustrate how easily citizens are deprived of civil freedoms. For decades, there has been little meaningful change. The crisis is worsened by overreliance on custodial measures. While the various initiatives to improve the jail infrastructure must be appreciated, an overhaul in the bail and surety processes, along with speedy trials, can actually reduce the under-trial population. Meanwhile, serious health concerns are widespread, with reports of cases of hepatitis, HIV, and diabetes. Insight into how individual conditions — such as mental health issues and drug addiction — worsen without treatment is the hallmark of a system that cares for its people, prisoners included.
ir_summary: Pakistan's prisons are severely overcrowded with most inmates awaiting trial, facing poor conditions and health crises.

title: Measuring decent work
text:
The fourth edition of the Labour Rights Index, launched on the eve of the World Day for Decent Work (October 7), shows that between January 2024 and January 2026, far more countries strengthened their labour laws than weakened them. The global debate on jobs is shifting from how many jobs are created to what kind and quality.

A frequent argument is that most countries already have enough labour laws and that the real problem is implementation. Implementation matters, but a right that does not exist in law cannot be implemented. If the law provides no maternity protection or no right to organise, no amount of labour inspection can create these rights.

The United Nations Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights recognises that legislation is an indispensable step for rights at work. Sustainable Development Goal indicators 5.1.1 (equality) and 8.8.2 (trade union rights) already assess national legislation.

Produced by the WageIndicator Foundation and the Centre for Labour Research, the 2026 Labour Rights Index covers 168 countries and scores 48 components under 10 indicators. The benchmarks come from International Labour Organisation (ILO) Conventions and UN instruments the world has already agreed upon.

The Index is deliberately de jure. The 168 countries account for more than 95 per cent of the world's population, nearly half of whom live in countries whose legislation provides "reasonable access to decent work" (countries scoring 70.5-80 out of 100). Measuring the law separates legal deficits from implementation deficits.

The long-term evidence does not support the feared race to the bottom. A 2025 ILO working paper, based on the Centre of Business Rights Labour Regulation Index and covering 117 countries between 1970 and 2022, finds that worker protection has increased steadily and that protective reforms were positively linked to a higher labour share of income.

The Organisation for Economic Co-o­peration and Development's 2026 review of employment protection finds that between 2019 and 2025 many countries strengthened regulation of temporary contracts, while virtually none significantly reduced protection on open-ended contracts.

A similar finding appears in the World Economic Forum's Global Gender Gap Report 2026. The average global gender gap has narrowed to its best recorded level, with around 70 per cent of the gap now closed. All 97 economies tracked continuously since 2006 have made progress.

The Labour Rights Index tells a similar story: 134 legal changes in 70 countries between 1 January 2024 and 1 January 2026. Setting aside minimum wage revisions, 38 reforms raised a component score, and another 60 strengthened the law without changing the score. Nine legal changes lowered a score and four weakened protection without affecting it. That is more than seven improvements for every setback.

The reforms span regions and income groups, from Lesotho and Egypt to the Kyrgyz Republic and Colombia. However, new working-time rules lowered scores in Egypt, India (Uttar Pradesh) and Lesotho.

Freedom of association and collective bargaining remains the weakest area globally, and around 36pc of the population covered still lives in countries where the law offers limited access to decent work or worse.

South Asia remains the lowest-scoring region (with an average score of 58, against 92 for Europe). The region is moving, however. India's four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025, giving India the region's highest score (71.5). Bangladesh's Labour (Amendment) Act, 2026 and Pakistan's Punjab Labour Code 2026 came after the 1 January 2026 reference date.

Pakistan shows why legislation matters. It has long relied on more than 40 fragmented labour laws, a structure largely reproduced at the provincial level after the 18th Amendment. The Punjab Labour Code 2026, enacted on 10 February, repeals 26 labour laws and extends protection to agricultural, domestic, home-based and platform workers, and strengthens maternity, childcare and collective rights.

Pakistan's official 2026 score of 52.5 does not reflect this Code's provisions. Assessed against the new Code, Pakistan's score rises to 86, moving Pakistan from "basic access" to "approaching access to decent work." This does not make workers better off overnight; implementation is the real test. But now there are rights that can be inspected, litigated, and bargained over.

Artificial intelligence is reshaping occupations, platform work is blurring the line between employment and self-employment, and climate change is exposing workers to heat stress. The answer is not to preserve every job. As the 2025 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences highlighted, innovation-driven growth displaces some jobs; the challenge is to protect workers rather than jobs, while ensuring a strong floor of labour rights.

Good legislation cannot guarantee decent work. But decent work cannot be built without good legislation. The evidence supports cautious optimism. Exploitation, informality and attacks on trade union rights have not disappeared. But the legislative reforms tell the story of a march to the top. The task now, in Pakistan as elsewhere, is to turn rights on paper into rights at work.
ir_summary: A new global index shows more countries strengthened labor laws than weakened them, focusing on de jure rights like maternity protection and unionization.

title: Fixing the export challenge
text:
Pakistan earned $30.14 billion from goods exports in the year to June 2026. That was 5.9 per cent less than the $32.04bn of the year before.
