Turkiye, the alliance's third member, is following a different legal route. Article 92 of the Turkish Constitution gives parliament authority over the deployment of Turkish armed forces abroad, subject to specified exceptions.

The issue has since moved towards parliamentary consideration in Ankara. Ruling AK Party spokesman Omer Celik said on Oct 7 that the agreement was expected to be sent to parliament within days, while Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Oct 8 that the necessary work for its submission had been completed.

Mr Fidan described the agreement as defensive, saying Turkiye would not send troops to another country to carry out attacks on its territory. He said military delegations would assess Saudi Arabia's operational requirements, including air defence and technical support, while Ankara was also pursuing a diplomatic track.

Mr Khan said Turkiye had committed itself under the agreement to providing the support needed to strengthen the alliance's defensive capabilities, adding that each country had its own procedures.

He cited the participation of the Turkish foreign minister, defence minister and chief of defence forces in the Oct 5 meeting as evidence of Ankara's commitment.

Pakistan remained in favour of political dialogue and de-escalation, the spokesperson said, but argued that prospects for talks depended on the Houthis' willingness to change their conduct.

"We are not saying that diplomacy is not a solution or that we should only fight a war. We fully agree that peace can only be achieved through diplomatic means. However, this also depends on whether the other side is willing to pursue peace. If they are ready, we can consider the next steps," he said.

He questioned whether talks could be productive while the Houthis continued attacks on infrastructure and maritime routes, saying the group appeared to believe such actions would give it leverage.

"In such a situation, I do not think talks would be fruitful; they would simply be futile. Therefore, the parties must first come to terms with the situation before moving forward diplomatically," Mr Khan said.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday strongly condemned repeated attacks by the Houthi militia against Saudi Arabia, including the targeting of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport, which resulted in civilian deaths and injuries.

In a post on X, the prime minister commended the vigilance and professionalism of the Saudi armed forces and the Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition in intercepting multiple ballistic missiles and protecting civilian lives and critical infrastructure.

"Pakistan stands in unwavering solidarity with the leadership and people of our brotherly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," he said.

PM Shehbaz said that in line with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and recent decisions of its Strategic Political and Defence Committee, Pakistan's commitment to the kingdom's sovereignty, territorial integrity and security remained resolute.

He said Pakistan fully supported Saudi Arabia's legitimate right to defend its people and protect its cities and vital infrastructure.

"The Houthi militia must immediately cease these attacks. We will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Saudi Arabia in the face of these threats," the prime minister said.
ir_summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office says parliamentary approval is not required for military deployments under the Makkah pact, citing executive authority.

title: ‘Legal trade won’t face curbs in Balochistan’
text:
QUETTA: Chief Collector of Customs Enforcement (Operations), Islamabad, Muhammad Jamil Nasir Khan, has assured traders of Balochistan that legal trade will not face unnecessary restrictions and announced measures to accelerate Customs clearance and auction of seized goods.

Speaking at a meeting with representatives of the Quetta Chamber of Commerce and Industry, he said Balochistan-related cases would be reviewed daily at the Central Assessment Unit from 5pm to 11pm.

He said that Customs operations would be automated within eight months to make cargo inspections and clearance faster and more convenient.

Quetta Chamber representatives highlighted serious problems confronting traders, including repeated inspections, unnecessary checkpoints and cargo vehicle fires.

They said that goods and vehicles worth billions of rupees had been destroyed at locations along Mastung Road and Ziarat Cross, with affected parties still awaiting compensation.

They also reported that between 3,000 and 3,500 cargo vehicles remained stranded, urging authorities to expedite clearance and auction of seized goods.
ir_summary: Customs official assures Balochistan traders of no unnecessary restrictions on legal trade and announces automation of clearance processes.

title: Trial courts can reject time-barred suits on their own initiative: SC
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court has ruled that a trial court can reject a palpably vexatious or time-barred lawsuit on its own initiative at the earliest stage, without waiting for a formal application from the defendant.

"There is no bar or embargo under Section 3 of the Limitation Act, 1908, or Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), 1908, preventing a court from dismissing a suit or rejecting a plaint on its own initiative, without a formal application from the defendant, if it is barred by law," observed Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar while heading a three-judge SC bench that took up an appeal against a Sindh High Court (SHC) order.

The case concerned a dispute over a house in Army Officers Housing Colony, Askari-IV, on Rashid Minhas Road in Karachi.

The original plaintiffs, including Abdul Wahab Shah, had filed a suit seeking a declaration, possession and partition. In September 2024, the trial court rejected their plaint, ruling that the suit was barred by limitation. The plaintiffs challenged the decision before the SHC, which set aside the rejection order and directed that all pending applications, including one seeking amendment of the plaint, be decided together. The defendant, Muhammad Islam Badshah, then challenged the high court's decision before the SC.

In an eight-page order, Justice Mazhar observed that a court's power to reject a plaint did not always depend on an application under Order VII, Rule 11 of the CPC. The powers conferred by Section 3 of the Limitation Act were broader in cases where a suit was found to be time-barred, allowing the court to dismiss it and bring the proceedings to a close.

A court was responsible for dismissing fundamentally flawed suits to save judicial time and prevent unnecessary litigation, without conducting a mini-trial or examining the written statement, the judge said.

If a plain reading of the plaint showed that it was palpably vexatious or meritless, the trial court could invoke Order VII, Rule 11 of the CPC to terminate sham litigation at the earliest stage. This applied where the plaint disclosed no actionable legal right or injury constituting a cause of action, or where the suit was expressly barred by an applicable statute or law, the judgment stated.

The court could exercise this power even before issuing summons to the other side, thereby saving judicial time and shielding parties from vexatious and misconceived litigation, Justice Mazhar emphasised.

Before rejecting a plaint, however, the court must examine whether it discloses a cause of action; whether the relief claimed is undervalued and, if so, whether the plaintiff has failed to correct the valuation within the prescribed time; and whether the relief is properly valued but the plaint is written on insufficiently stamped paper, with the plaintiff failing to supply the required stamp paper within the time allowed. The court must also determine whether the suit appears, from the statements in the plaint, to be barred by law, the judgment said.

The underlying principle is that ineffectual and unproductive lawsuits should be disposed of at the outset so that judicial resources can be devoted to serious and genuine disputes. At the same time, courts should not allow procedural manoeuvres designed to delay proceedings. A meaningful reading of the plaint is essential to reach a just conclusion, the judgment added.

If a suit is inherently incompetent because of an express or implied legal bar, rather than a formal, technical or curable defect, it should not be allowed to burden judicial proceedings further. However, the law does not permit the rejection of a plaint in parts. If even one prayer is maintainable, the entire plaint cannot be rejected. Where questions of law and fact are intertwined, the suit should proceed to the written statement and discovery stages. The court may then determine the dispute by framing preliminary issues or conducting a regular trial, ensuring both parties have an equal opportunity to present their cases.

The proper course in such matters is to frame issues and decide them on merit in light of the evidence. Courts must ensure substantial justice and avoid leaving parties without a remedy, the judgment held.

Concluding the order, the SC directed the trial court to decide the maintainability of the civil suit in accordance with law after giving both parties an adequate opportunity of hearing, and then proceed further. The SC also set aside the SHC's Feb 6, 2025, order to the extent that it directed the question of maintainability to be decided alongside the application seeking amendment of the plaint.
ir_summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court rules trial courts can dismiss time-barred lawsuits without defendant applications to save judicial time.

title: Bilawal, Rana Sana made members of JCP
text:
ISLAMABAD: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and Adviser to the Prime Minister Rana Sanaullah on Friday were made members of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP).

Two seats in the JCP were vacant after the recent resignations of PPP Senator Farooq H. Naek and PML-N member Aftab Sheikh.

Both Mr Bhutto-Zardari and Mr Sanaullah will represent parliament as members of the treasury benches in the respective Houses — the National Assembly and the Senate.

The nominations were made by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who is also Leader of the House in the National Assembly, as well as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Ishaq Dar, who is the Leader of the House in the Senate, under Article 175A (2)(vii) of the Constitution.

A notification for the appointments was issued on Friday by the JCP with the approval of Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi, who is also the body's chairperson.

The next JCP meeting is scheduled for Oct 13, when the body will meet to consider extending the term of the Sindh High Court's constitutional benches.

The JCP is mandated by Article 175A of the Constitution to appoint judges of the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), Supreme Court, high courts and Federal Shariat Court.

The commission also evaluates the performance of the judges of the high courts.

Under the 26th Amendment, changes were made to Article 175A, which reconstituted the JCP with the inclusion of four members of parliament — two each from the treasury and opposition, one from the National Assembly and the other from the Senate.

The commission consists of chief justices of the SC and the FCC, the next most senior judge from each court, and two judges from each court jointly nominated by the chief justices for two years.

It also comprises the federal law minister, the attorney general of Pakistan, an advocate with no less than 15 years of practice in the SC, two members from the Senate and the National Assembly each from the treasury and opposition benches, and a woman, non-Muslim or technocrat other than a member of the parliament, who is qualified to become a member of the parliament.
ir_summary: Pakistan's PM appoints Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and Rana Sanaullah to the Judicial Commission of Pakistan representing parliament.

title: Balochistan govt approves reforms in key sectors
text:
QUETTA: The Baloc­histan cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti on Friday, approved a series of measures aimed at promoting economic development, improving public services and strengthening administrative governance across the province.

Briefing the media, Adviser to the Chief Minister on Information and Political Affairs Shahid Rind said the decisions reflected the government's commitment to public welfare and practical reforms.

The cabinet approved the Balochistan Mineral Development Fund Policy to ensure that revenue from natural resources contributes to public welfare and provincial development. It also endorsed draft tourism and cultural policies to promote investment, employment and the protection of historical heritage.

In education, the cabinet approved the Balochistan Non-Formal Education Act, 2025, targeting the enrolment of approximately 1.6 million children aged 10 to 16 who are outside the formal education system. Double-shift teaching in government schools was also approved to accommodate more students using existing infrastructure.

To revive economic activity, the cabinet approved incentives for reopening closed industrial units. Amendments to public procurement rules were approved to expand electronic bidding, enhance transparency and encourage competition. Electronic bidding will be mandatory for tenders exceeding Rs500,000 across relevant procurement categories.
ir_summary: Balochistan government approves economic, education, and governance reforms including mineral fund policy and non-formal education act.

title: LHC seeks report on facilities for Imran’s sisters in jail
text:
LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday sought a report from the jail authorities on the provision of medicines, clothes and other basic necessities to the incarcerated sisters of PTI founder Imran Khan.

Mr Khan's three sisters, Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Dr Uzma Khan, have been in detention for nearly three weeks under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.

Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi were detained for 30 days on September 21, ahead of the party's September 27 protest call, which was later postponed to October 4. Aleema Khan was detained a day earlier, on September 20.

On Friday, Justice Abher Gul Khan took up civil miscellaneous applications filed by Aleema's son, Shahrez Khan, and Noreen's daughter, Sakeena Niazi. The applications, filed earlier this week, alleged that the detainees had been denied medicines and meetings with their family members and counsel.

During the hearing, counsel for the petitioners, Rana Mudassar Umar, told the court that 19 days had passed since the detentions, but the three sisters had not been provided with medicines and clothes.

Justice Abher Gul Khan observed that Aleema had been provided with clothes and medicines.

However, the counsel maintained that the items had been supplied only after court orders and that nothing had been provided earlier.

Mr Umar requested the court to direct the jail authorities to provide Ms Noreen with books, medicines and other essential items as well.

The judge asked the counsel to specify the items required, observing that only those approved by the court would be allowed into the jail.

The counsel sought permission to provide medicines, clothes, books and food items to the three sisters. The judge said the court would seek reports from the jail superintendent on the applications.

The hearing was adjourned until October 12.

Detention plea disposed of Separately, the Lahore High Court on Friday disposed of a petition challenging the detention of Aleema and her driver, Muhammad Amir, after expressing satisfaction with a report submitted by the Punjab Home Department.

Justice Abher Gul Khan heard the petition filed by Shahrez Khan, who had challenged the detention orders against his mother and her driver.

During the hearing, a provincial law officer submitted a report on behalf of the Home Department, stating that applications seeking redressal of the petitioner's grievances had been filed with the department.

The law officer informed the court that the relevant appellate authority would decide the applications in accordance with the law.

After expressing satisfaction with the report, the judge disposed of the petition.
ir_summary: Lahore High Court seeks report on jail conditions for Imran Khan's detained sisters under public order law.

title: Trump to hold inquiry into Fed official at White House
text:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump will summon Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook to the White House for a hearing on his administration's allegations she made false statements in connection with her mortgages, escalating his bid to fire her just weeks ahead of elections that will determine if Trump's Republican Party maintains control of Congress.

Trump has been trying to fire Cook for more than a year as he moves in unprecedented ways to exert more control over a central bank he views as refusing for political reasons to lower interest rates as he wants. Lawyers for Cook said on Friday any fair hearing would show there is no legal basis for firing her.

"As President, it is my job to ensure the laws are faithfully executed, including by firing subordinates who cannot be trusted to tell the truth and follow the law," Trump said in a notice on the White House website on Friday.

"To assist me in carrying out that responsibility, the Committee shall investigate the allegations against Governor Cook and report to me whether there is 'cause' for Governor Cook's removal," according to the notice, dated October 7.

The committee will hold a closed, in-person hearing at the White House "to consider the evidence and allegations against Governor Cook," the presidential memorandum said. Members of the committee, its representatives, or Department of Justice personnel will question her for "no longer than four hours." If the hearing is "anything close to objective, the conclusion will be that Governor Cook did not commit mortgage fraud, leaving no cause to remove her from the Federal Reserve Board," Cook's lawyers Abbe Lowell and Norm Eisen said in a statement. "Governor Cook welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name and demonstrate there is no legal basis to fire her."

They said they had engaged with the White House about the process.

Trump first tried to fire Cook, the first Black woman to serve on the central bank's board, in August 2025. No president has ever tried to fire a sitting Fed governor before. Central banks are widely seen as needing political independence to ensure their ability to fight inflation as needed.

The case led to the US Supreme Court ruling earlier this year that the president could not remove a Fed governor without adequate cause and needed to follow a clear process to lay out the reasons and provide evidence.

The ruling left Cook in her position but kicked the case against her back to a federal district court.

Cook was appointed to the Fed board in 2022 by former President Joe Biden, a Democrat, and was reappointed in 2023 to a term that lasts until 2038.
ir_summary: Trump summons Fed official to White House hearing over mortgage allegations, escalating his bid to fire her before elections.

title: US begins fresh push to end Ukraine war
text:
MIAMI: Ukrainian, European and US officials met in Miami on Friday in a renewed diplomatic push to end the war in Ukraine, with Washington seeking a way out of a dangerous stalemate.

President Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to hold two days of talks with Ukrainian negotiators and European representatives, seeking to forge a common proposal for ending the conflict, US officials said.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned on Thursday that the war had reached a potentially explosive impasse, with the lack of a negotiated settlement raising the risk of further escalation.

"The other way that stalemates end is through escalation," Rubio told reporters in Lisbon, warning that the conflict could spread to neighbouring Nato countries.

"We do not believe that there is a military solution to this conflict," he added.

The Miami meeting follows visits to Moscow and Kyiv last month by Witkoff, a longtime Trump confidant, and Kushner, the president's son-in-law, as Washington seeks to revive negotiations that have yielded little progress.

US negotiators have since been developing fresh proposals with Russian and Ukrainian officials, a source familiar with the discussions said.

Among the ideas being considered is a partial ceasefire covering attacks on energy infrastructure and grain shipments, according to Axios.

Ukraine has indicated a willingness to explore such an arrangement, but Russia has shown little enthusiasm for the proposal, the US news outlet reported.

With winter approaching, the prospect of continued fighting and attacks on vital infrastructure has added urgency to the search for a settlement.

The renewed diplomacy comes against a backdrop of deadly Russian attacks, including a strike on buses in the frontline Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk that killed 30 people.

Trump's repeated attempts to broker an end to the war have foundered over Moscow's sweeping territorial demands, particularly its insistence on controlling all of Ukraine's eastern Donbas region, including areas still held by Kyiv.

Zelensky has rejected surrendering Ukrainian-held territory, warning that Russia could use it as a springboard for another attack.

Russia, which launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, occupies roughly one-fifth of Ukrainian territory.

The Miami discussions are also expected to cover security guarantees designed to protect Ukraine against future Russian aggression and plans for the country's post-war economic recovery, US officials said.

National security advisors from Britain, France and Germany have been invited, along with representatives of Nato and the European Union.

European officials have expressed concern over high energy costs and the wider economic consequences of the conflict, according to the US sources.

Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov and intelligence chief Rustem Umerov will be among Ukraine's representatives, alongside senior negotiators Sergiy Kyslytsya and David Arakhamia.

Witkoff and Kushner briefed Trump on their latest proposals Thursday, at a meeting also attended by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other senior officials, Axios reported.
ir_summary: US officials lead diplomatic talks with Ukraine and Europe to negotiate an end to the war and avoid escalation.

title: Online media censorship rising in India, says Reporters Without Borders
text:
SINCE the start of 2026, the removal of journalistic content from social media has been on the rise in India and a recent change in rules leaves online platforms with just three hours to take down the content in question, Reporters Without Borders (RSF) said in a statement on Friday.

Investigative reports on lead-bullet shootings in India-held Kashmir, the forced displacement of communities to make way for a Google data centre project and a student's account of alleged police violence are being swiftly taken off social media at the authorities' request, the RSF said in its report.

"In February, new rules came into force that cut the time-limit gr­a­nted to social media platforms to remove reported content from 36 hours to just three.

"This shorter timeframe leaves platforms little time to carry out a thorough review of requests before removing the content," according to RSF.

The Software Freedom Law Centre (SFLC), a New Delhi-based organisation that works to defend online freedoms, told RSF: "In 2026, there were 40 instances of content takedown and blocking of accounts held by journalists or media organisations.

"However, media reports suggest that the actual number of such content removals might be much higher than recorded."

The Indian government issued nearly 200,000 removal orders, according to data consulted by the Indian Express. The orders were transmitted via Sahyog, a government portal, betw­een March and July, compared with just 2,312 between Oct 2024 and Oct 2025.

Launched by the home affairs ministry in Oct 2024, the portal enables law enforcement agencies to request the immediate removal of online content from digital platforms and has helped to automate these removals.

"Journalists find it increasingly difficult to challenge these restrictions, owing to lack of transparency about which authority initiated a takedown, under which legal provision and the basis for enforcing the same," emphasised the SFLC.

The RSF called upon the Indian government to end arbitrary takedown requests targeting the press, make the legal basis for each measure public and ensure there is an independent assessment of journalistic content before it is subject to any restrictions.

The organisation also appealed to Meta, X and other platforms to subject any request concerning a media outlet or journalist to "human and legal review".

Accounts of Kashmiri media outlets and marginalised communities were blocked in February, notably due to content on police violence.

Meta blocked the Facebook and Instagram accounts of three major Kashmiri media outlets – Greater Kashmir, Rising Kashmir and Kashmir Life – without publicly explaining the reasons for these measures.
ir_summary: Reporters Without Borders reports increasing online media censorship in India with faster content removal rules and lack of transparency.

title: 30 killed in Sudan drone strike
text:
KHARTOUM: A drone strike launched by Sud­an's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) killed 26 women and four children on Friday near the southeastern border with Ethiopia.

The latest front line in Sudan's war between the regular army and the RSF is the border region with Ethiopia, which is facing its own internal conflict that threatens to escalate into a regional war.

Since Sudan's war broke out in April 2023, it has killed more than 200,000 people, aid workers estimate, and created the world's largest hunger and displacement crises.

This year alone, nearly 100,000 people have been displaced across Blue Nile state, according to UN figures.

In a displacement camp in Blue Nile's Abu Shendi, survivors "buried 26 women and four children" from Friday's strike, one person involved in the burial said.

The drone hit just outside the camp, near an informal gold mining site, where women earn a daily wage using chemicals and their bare hands to clear gold nuggets from clumps of earth men have extracted. The victims included "young girls who work with their families in refining the gold", another eyewitness said.
ir_summary: Sudan's RSF paramilitary killed 30 civilians in a drone strike near the Ethiopian border amid ongoing civil war.

title: US to livestream firing squad execution
text:
WASHINGTON: The execution by firing squad of convicted military base shooter Nidal Hasan will be livestreamed, a Pentagon official said, drawing sharp condemnation Friday of the plan to broadcast the killing.

Hasan's execution, set for Dec 3, is poised to be the first that the US military has carried out by firing squad since World War II.

"It will be livestreamed. Details will follow," the Pentagon official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP of the death sentence imposed on the US Army psychiatrist who shot dead 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009.

Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth said in a video posted on X on Thursday that Hasan is "going to get a firing squad of soldiers, as it should be, and we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public".

"People need to understand that... there's serious consequence for these types of things," Hegseth told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec.

The UN has condemned the plan to livestream the execution, saying it would amount to torture.

"The livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture," the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights said in a message.
ir_summary: US military to livestream firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter, drawing UN condemnation as torture.

title: American barbarism
text:
WITH the spectre of defeat in the upcoming midterm elections looming large over the Trump administration, the Republicans are resorting to desperate attempts to rally their base.

Right-wing American media, GOP candidates, and the incumbent US administration, who have spewed Islamophobia ad nauseam, have now found a perfect prop in convicted mass murderer Nidal Hasan, who shot and killed 13 at the Texas Fort Hood military base in 2009.

Hasan is to be executed by firing squad on Dec 3, according to a Pentagon announcement, and US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth is to ensure his execution is livestreamed to the world. Seemingly threatened by the emergence of progressive, well-liked Democratic politicians such as Zohran Mamdani and Abdul el-Sayed, both of whom have greatly upset those who believe American politics should be limited to specific religions and races, the Trump administration is asserting its version of American 'greatness'.

And, having run out of political answers, it is doing so in the most Trumpian manner imaginable: by publicly killing a Muslim man and celebrating the accomplishment.

To be clear, Hasan has been convicted under US law and — although this paper does not support executions — deserves to be punished for his crimes. However, to turn him into a prop for election theatrics is a new low even for the current Trump administration. It is no wonder that the announcement of a livestreamed execution has drawn condemnation from both sides of the aisle and led critics to draw parallels with the lynchings of Black Americans — a similar public spectacle in early 20th-century America.

If this grotesque and reprehensible deed is accomplished, the US will join the ranks of a handful of totalitarian states that have practised public executions in recent memory. That list includes the Afghan Taliban regime. As Nietzsche warned, "if you gaze long into an abyss, the abyss also gazes into you". America is gradually turning into the regimes it most despises.
ir_summary: US plans to livestream execution of Muslim convict for political gain, drawing bipartisan condemnation and comparisons to historical lynchings.

title: Midterm break
text:
AMERICAN President Donald Trump's statement that he will not launch a fresh attack on Iran before the US midterm elections does little to calm fears of renewed war in the Gulf. In effect, the US president has only promised to postpone the attack, when he should have committed to indefinitely suspending hostilities in favour of dialogue.

Clearly, it is a calculated political move: the Iran war is unpopular with the American people, mainly because of the inflation and high petroleum prices it has caused. Mr Trump may be holding off on a new assault to prevent a complete drubbing of the Republicans at the ballot box. What is perplexing is the mixed messaging. While refusing to rule out a post-midterms attack, he also said that the Iran war was going to end "very soon".

Most observers have lost count of how many times he has said this. He added that talks with Tehran were "productive". Should the world believe that a new attack is imminent after the US elections? Or is the US looking to wind things down? Perhaps those calling the shots in Washington themselves do not know. It is also a matter of concern that Israel is reportedly contemplating another attack on Iran.

Both the US and Israel need to halt their destructive misadventures in the Middle East. Their irresponsible warmongering has resulted in widespread bloodshed across the region and has upended the global economy. Washington and Tehran have exchanged proposals on how to end the conflict. Mr Trump and his cohorts, therefore, need to concentrate exclusively on the diplomatic track, instead of fuelling speculation regarding fresh hostilities.

Already, the Yemen conflict is spiralling out of control. If the US and Israel were to spark another round of violence with Iran, the consequences for the entire region — indeed the world at large — would be grim. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is already constrained. If Bab al-Mandeb were also to be closed, and the export of petrochemicals from the region curtailed further because of conflict, the entire world will pay the price for the deadly follies of Mr Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Therefore, instead of speaking in riddles, President Trump must commit his country to the peace process, offer the Iranians a fair deal, and bring his military home from the Middle East.
ir_summary: Trump delays potential Iran attack until after US midterms, raising concerns about renewed conflict and need for diplomacy.

title: Aurangzeb reviews retailers’ tax scheme
text:
ISLAMABAD: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said on Friday that the government was working to simplify tax procedures and help retailers meet their tax obligations by bringing them onto the tax roll.

The minister reviewed progress on the retailers' tax scheme and discussed measures to facilitate registration and broaden the tax base. State Minister for Finance Bilal Azhar and Chairman of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) Rashid Mahmood Langrial attended the meeting.

An official announcement said the meeting reviewed progress and measures to speed up compliance with the scheme. The meeting was held at a time when the response from the traders was below expectations.

Mr Aurangzeb emphasised that the scheme offers a simplified route for retailers to join the formal tax system and contribute to the country's economic development. The minister emphasised the need to assess implementation experience and address operational matters to ensure its success.

The meeting reviewed progress on registrations and tax returns under the scheme, including existing taxpayer participation and applicable tax payment requirements.

The meeting also discussed efforts to identify and map unregistered retailers using available data and relevant identification records. The FBR briefed the meeting on data validation and the need to ensure that registration records accurately reflect the businesses concerned.

The minister emphasised a balanced approach that combines taxpayer facilitation with targeted, well-documented measures.

Emphasising the scheme's longer-term purpose, Mr Aurangzeb noted that the Retailers' Tax Scheme should not be seen as a one-year arrangement limited to 2026. It is intended to provide a simplified route for small retailers to enter and remain in the formal tax system in the years ahead.
ir_summary: Pakistan's finance minister reviews progress on a tax scheme for retailers to broaden the tax base and simplify compliance.

title: Afridi-led protest march circles back to home turf
text:
PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi led the PTI's long march into Peshawar on Thursday evening on the fifth day of the protest, promising to unveil the party's next major move in Swabi as its eventual destination remained unclear amid changes to the route and disruption of cellular services in parts of the provincial capital.

The march, launched from Lakki Marwat on Oct 4 to demand the release of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, was initially billed as a march on Islamabad, but its route has since been revised several times.

Separately, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan said gatherings were now planned in Mardan on Oct 10 and Swabi on Oct 11, after which the party leadership would decide its future course.

A post by the PTI's official X account shortly after 6pm on Thursday said that the Afridi-led convoy had reached Hayatabad Toll Plaza in Peshawar. It also shared pictures of hundreds of supporters gathered to welcome the KP chief minister.

"God willing, by the time it reaches Swabi, this caravan will become the largest long march in Pakistan's history," the PTI asserted.

Addressing supporters at the toll plaza, CM Afridi urged them to maintain their determination for the "struggle for true freedom".

"There might be some discomfort, but this pain is not greater than the pain Imran Khan is enduring in jail for us," he said.

While Mr Afridi said he would announce the next plan of action after proceeding to other areas of Peshawar, he also said the public would be "thrilled" upon hearing his plan when he reaches Swabi.

He added that their next stop after Peshawar would be Charsadda, where he would share some details of the next course of action.

In a video shared by the PTI, Mr Afridi could be seen raising slogans of "Free Imran Khan", with supporters chanting in harmony.

Ahead of the protesters' arrival, an unannounced disruption of cellular and mobile internet services was reported since last night in several areas of the provincial capital.
ir_summary: PTI's protest march led by KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi continues through Khyber Pakhtunkhwa demanding Imran Khan's release.

title: Higher fuel costs weigh on October power bills
text:
ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Thursday notified electricity consumers of an additional burden of Rs16 billion by allowing Rs1.11 per unit in higher fuel costs in October billing.

In a notification, Nepra said it had decided that the "positive fuel cost adjustment (FCA) for August 2026, i.e. Rs1.1086 per kWh … shall be applicable to all the consumer categories of K-Electric and ex-Wapda distribution companies (XWDISCOs), except lifeline consumers, electric vehicle charging sta­tions and prepaid consumers of all categories who opted for the prepaid tariff".

The regulator said the higher FCA would also apply to consumers under the incremental consumption package.

Discos and K-Electric are required to reflect the fuel cost adjustment for August 2026 in the October 2026 billing month.

The Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) had reported that the actual average fuel charges component for August 2026 amounted to Rs8.8265 per kWh, against the reference fuel charges component of Rs7.0998 per kWh approved in the applicable notified consumer-end tariff.

Accordingly, it had demanded an additional FCA of Rs1.73 per unit for electricity consumed in August 2026.

After certain adjustments, Nepra worked out the actual fuel component of the tariff at Rs8.2084, instead of Rs8.8265 as claimed by CPPA, thus allowing an additional FCA of Rs1.11 in October billing, instead of the Rs1.73 per unit demanded by CPPA.

The higher additional fuel cost in August stemmed from expensive RLNG imports from the spot market, as contracted supplies from Qatar remained under force majeure, besides higher coal imports and lower-than-estimated availability of cheaper hydropower and nuclear generation.

Hydropower was originally targeted to account for about 41 per cent of total power generation, but its share fell to just below 38pc, while the share of nuclear power was estimated at 16.4pc but turned out to be 10pc due to an outage at Karachi's nuclear power plants.

As a consequence, the share of imported coal-based generation increased to 15.6pc, instead of 7.4pc as originally planned.

Hydropower has no fuel cost, while the average nuclear fuel cost rose to Rs3.15 per unit due to lower utilisation, up from Rs2.5 per unit.

In contrast, imported coal-based generation cost Rs17 per unit. The cost of local coal-based generation was reported at Rs5.5 per unit.

The cost of RLNG-based generation was reported at Rs45.93 per unit, even higher than the Rs45.25 per unit cost of furnace oil-based power generation, which also includes a petroleum levy of Rs73,000 per tonne.

The FCA is reviewed monthly under the tariff regime applicable across the country and usually applies to consumers' bills for one month only.

Under the tariff mechanism, fuel cost changes are passed on to consumers only monthly through an automatic mechanism. In contrast, the federal government builds quarterly tariff adjustments into the base tariff to reflect changes in power purchase prices, capacity charges, variable operation and maintenance costs, and use-of-system charges, including the impact of transmission and distribution losses.
ir_summary: Pakistan's power regulator approves higher electricity bills due to increased fuel costs from expensive LNG and coal imports.

title: Lawyers back PTI march, demands
text:
QUETTA: The All Pakistan Lawyers Action Committee has declared its full support to the march and demands of Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf.

In a statement issued here on Thursday, chairman of the committee Ali Ahmed Kurd, and representatives of different bar associations and councils said the PTI march would be a historic struggle for strengthening democracy and the rule of law in the country.

The lawyers said the PTI move is aimed at supremacy of the Constitution and law, an independent judiciary and parliament and against the ongoing political and economic crisis, deteriorating law and order, illegal arrests of political and human rights leaders and workers, inflation and lawlessness.

They called for the immediate release of PTI founder Imran Khan and other party leaders and workers detained across the country.

The committee urged the government to immediately accept all demands of the PTI and ensure safety of the participants in the party's peaceful rally. It warned that if governor's rule was imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa or any 'undemocratic action' was taken, lawyers would launch protests against it across the country.
ir_summary: Pakistani lawyers support PTI's political march demanding democracy, rule of law, and Imran Khan's release.

title: Youth must choose skills, development over violence: Bugti
text:
QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti has urged the youth to make thoughtful decisions about their future and choose the path of dignity, education, skills and development instead of violence.

He said the gap between the youth and the state will be bridged through education, skills development, employment, merit and meaningful dialogue.

The chief minister said that the government will provide all possible support to enable young people to become part of the formal economy instead of engaging in illegal activities.

He was speaking at a certificate distribution ceremony at the Chief Minister's Secretariat on Thursday.

"The government's objective is not merely to train young people and issue them certificates, but to enable them to stand on their own feet," the chief minister said.

He said the government would provide skilled youth with a conducive environment, interest-free loans, business support and continued guidance so that they could establish respectable businesses in their respective areas or anywhere in the country.

Referring to the government's employment programme for youth in border districts, CM Bugti said it had been launched to provide young people with opportunities for legal employment and businesses instead of an economy based on illegal activities.

He said attempts to push Balochistan's girls towards violence, make them wear suicide jackets and use them for anti-state activities were contrary to the traditions of society, as well as Islam and human values.

He said efforts to distance young people from the state through anti-state propaganda could be countered by providing them with education, skills, employment and opportunities.

Separately, JUI-F Balochistan chief Senator Maulana Abdul Wasey has called for the withdrawal of the "private militia" present in Balochistan, saying it should be sent back. He said the Baloch­istan government and the chief minister were either powerless or taking decisions in instalments.

Speaking at a press conference, Maulana Wasey said the Balochistan chief minister had apologised so many times that "even apologies have now become discredited".
ir_summary: Balochistan Chief Minister urges youth to choose education and development over violence and anti-state activities.

title: 25 terror outfits operating from Afghanistan, UN chief told
text:
ISLAMABAD: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday said that 25 terrorist organisations currently operating from Afgha­nistan posed a major threat to global peace.

He was speaking during a meeting with United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres at the Ministry of Interior.

"The international community needs to work together to deal with this threat. Pakistan is fighting a global war against terrorism," Mr Naqvi said.

The meeting, also attended by Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudary, discussed the global and regional situation and matters related to UN peacekeeping missions.

The interior minister said that Pakistan would continue to play its full role in UN peace missions, adding that officers and personnel of Pakistani police were also serving in the UN police. He noted that Pakistan had sacrificed 181 lives in peace missions.

The UN chief said that Pakistan's participation in UN peace missions had always remained prominent, adding that Islamabad's role for world peace was commendable.

Mr Naqvi thanked the UN secretary general for extending generous assistance to Pakistan during natural disasters. Special secretary interior, additional secretary interior and senior officials were also present on the occasion.

Mr Guterres recognised Pakistan's participation in peacekeeping missions, saying it had always been "prominent". "Pakistan's role in world peace is commendable," he said.

After the meeting, Mr Guterres concluded his two-day visit to Pakistan, which "provided an important opportunity to reaffirm Pakistan's longstanding partnership with the United Nations", the Foreign Office said in a statement.

The UN chief's visit highlighted "Pakistan's unwavering support for multilateralism", the FO said.

Previously, Mr Guterres also met President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar.

On Tuesday, in a meeting with Mr Guterres, Mr Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to the UN charter, multilateralism and settlement of disputes through dialogue and diplomacy. He also highlighted Pakistan's ongoing diplomatic efforts in support of regional peace and stability.

While briefing the UN chief on India's violation of the Indus Waters Treaty and international law, Mr Dar reiterated Pakistan's call for a just and peaceful resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute.

He further highlighted Pakistan's support for Palestinians and their legitimate struggle for self-determination and statehood, the FO said.
ir_summary: Pakistan's interior minister tells UN chief that 25 terrorist groups in Afghanistan threaten global peace and discusses UN peacekeeping cooperation.

title: PHC puts KP CM on notice over use of official helicopter for protest
text:
PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Thursday sought a reply from the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister to a contempt petition seeking his punishment for allegedly violating an earlier court judgement barring the use of government resources for any march, protest or political activity.

A bench comprising Chief Justice SM Attique Shah and Justice Ijaz Khan issued a notice to the chief minister after a preliminary hearing of a petition filed by PML-N MPA Zahir Khan.

The petitioner requested the court to punish CM Sohail Afridi in accordance with law for the alleged "wilful disobedience and contempt" of the court's judgement and order dated October 23, 2025. The petitioner prayed that the court initiate contempt proceedings against the chief minister, summon him in person and direct him to explain, on affidavit, the circumstances, purpose, authorisation and source of payment relating to his use of the official helicopter to travel to and lead the protest march.

He also requested the court to direct the chief minister to produce the relevant official flight authorisation, logbook and expenditure record before the court.

The next date of hearing will be fixed later. Chief Minister Sohail Afridi is the sole respondent in the petition.

Appearing for the petitioner, Barrister M. Yaseen Raza Khan stated that a writ petition had been filed before the court in 2024 against the use of official government vehicles, machinery, personnel and other public resources for political protests, rallies and protest marches.

He said the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government, through its chief executive/chief minister, had been arrayed as Respondent No. 1 in the said petition.

He said the petition was finally decided by the court through a judgement dated October 23, 2025, whereby several directives were issued to the respondents and all concerned authorities.

"Accordingly, we dispose of the writ petition; however, the respondents and all concerned authorities are directed to ensure, with utmost diligence, that no official vehicle, machinery, or manpower under their control is deployed, used, or permitted to be used for any protest, march, rally, or political activity of any nature," Barrister Yaseen quoted the judgement as stating.

He argued that the direction of the court was clear, unequivocal and binding upon the provincial government, the respondent and all authorities and functionaries working under their control.

He said that, notwithstanding the clear and binding direction of the court, the chief minister, on October 4, 2026, personally availed himself of and used an official helicopter of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government to travel from Peshawar to Lakki Marwat to participate in, launch and lead a political protest march organised by his political party, PTI.

"The official helicopter was thus placed at the personal disposal of the respondent for facilitating his participation in an expressly political activity prohibited by the judgement and order of this Honourable Court," the counsel pointed out.

He contended that the alleged violation was not confined merely to the transportation of the chief minister, as the use of the official helicopter necessarily involved the deployment of its pilots, crew, fuel, technical staff, ground arrangements, security personnel, protocol officials and other public resources.

He added that the entire official machinery accompanying and facilitating the flight was therefore employed to enable the chief minister to reach and lead the political march, in direct and manifest violation of the court's judgement.

He argued that the alleged wilful and deliberate disobedience of the binding judgement and order of the court by the chief minister warranted the initiation of contempt proceedings and appropriate action against him in accordance with law.
ir_summary: Peshawar High Court issues notice to KP CM for allegedly using official helicopter for protest, violating court order.

title: Ministries told to give data to ‘Digital Nation’
text:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday directed all federal ministries to complete necessary measures within the stipulated time to provide relevant data to the Digital Nation Pakistan programme.

Presiding over a meeting here, the prime minister said the central, national-level data centre being established under the Digital Nation Pakistan programme would play a key role in delivering government services and public facilities.

He said assigning responsibilities to federal ministries and providing relevant data to the central data centre would bring the government system in line with modern requirements.

"The Digital Nation Pakistan programme is essentially aimed at ensuring efficient and convenient services for citizens nationwide," he said. The sharing of data among institutions had played a key role in the successful implementation of the fuel subsidy scheme for deserving segments of society, he added.

He said the digitisation of the ministry's performance and relevant data was also important in curbing corruption and institutional mismanagement.

PM Shehbaz also welcomed the introduction of QR codes to ensure the supply of quality medicines across the country.

The meeting was told that digitisation in key public-service sectors, particularly health and agriculture, was being completed on priority basis to facilitate the masses.

The IT ministry, in coordination with the ministry of law, was also taking special measures to make relevant national laws available at a single platform to provide better guidance for future legislation, officials said.

Work on digitising priority sectors was continuing in line with the prime minister's directives, with special measures being taken to promote digital government services, a digital economy and digital public facilitation, the meeting was told.

A detailed briefing was also given on the provision of health ministry data to the central data centre and the use of digitisation to verify the quality of medicines.
ir_summary: Pakistan's prime minister directs ministries to provide data for a national digitization program to improve government services and curb corruption.

title: Israeli soldier killed in Lebanon
text:
JERUSALEM: The Israeli army said on Thursday that one soldier was killed and three others were slightly wounded in south Lebanon, where the military has occupied a band of territory since invading in March in response to Hezbollah attacks.

"Captain Eliav Haim Tzapalamus, aged 21, from Haifa, a combat officer in the 603rd Battalion, 7th Brigade, fell in combat in southern Lebanon," the army said.

Tzapalamus is the 17th Israeli soldier to be killed since a ceasefire was reached in June between Israel and Hezbollah.

Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a framework deal that involves the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the region.

On Thursday, visiting EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said in Beirut that the bloc favoured avoiding a security vacuum and extending a UN peacekeeping mandate in south Lebanon.

The EU's top diplomat also said that the bloc would soon be launching a training mission for the under-resourced Lebanese army.

Israeli airstrikes and ground operations in Lebanon have killed more than 4,300 since March, according to Lebanese official figures.
ir_summary: Israeli soldier killed in south Lebanon amid ongoing conflict and ceasefire with Hezbollah.

title: Trump says comment on LA was misinterpreted
text:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said comments he made that Iran could "take out" California cities had been misinterpreted and that he was instead referring to the need for people to tolerate higher gas prices.

Trump made the remarks at a political rally in Nebraska on Monday as he spoke about Americans' wartime economic sacrifices.

"Remember, with the war, it's just artificial, it's a little bit high, it's a small price to pay," he said then. "It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let 'em take out Los Angeles, let 'em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it's going to be over with very soon." California's Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans quickly rebuked the remarks.

"What I was talking about was that a temporary increase in the price of Gasoline is a small price to pay for Iran not having a Nuclear Weapon," Trump said in a Truth Social post on Thursday.

"If you want to see a big price, can you imagine what it would be like if they bombed San Diego and/or Los Angeles?" he continued, saying he loved both cities.

Trump has shrugged off cost-of-living concerns stemming from the Iran conflict before.
ir_summary: Trump clarifies his controversial remarks about Iran potentially attacking US cities, linking gas prices to nuclear security.

title: Crew splashes down after 8-month mission on ISS
text:
WASHINGTON: An astronaut crew that carried out an eight-month mission aboard the International Space Station splashed down as planned on Thursday off the coast of California.

After a more than 27-hour return journey, the Dragon capsule carrying Crew-12 landed safely in the Pacific Ocean, according to space agency Nasa's live broadcast.

"We are so excited to be back on planet Earth after an incredible mission on the International Space Station," said American astronaut Jessica Meir, the mission commander. The spacecraft was then hoisted onto a specialised ship, and the four occupants — Meir, American Jack Hathaway, French astronaut Sophie Adenot and Russian cosmonaut Andrei Fedyaev — were helped out one by one. They will undergo initial medical checks on the ship before being transported by helicopter to land, and then fly to Houston, Texas, home to the Nasa centre responsible for astronaut operations.

During the mission, Adenot became the first French female astronaut to venture outside the space station for a spacewalk. In all, she undertook three spacewalks on Aug 18 and 25, and Sept 1. Four new crew members for the ISS docked at the orbiting laboratory last week and will stay for approximately six months.

Continuously inhabited for the last quarter-century, the aging ISS is scheduled to be pushed out of orbit before crashing into one of Earth's oceans sometime around 2030. Despite many international cooperation agreements falling apart after Moscow invaded Ukraine in 2022, the United States and other ISS partners have continued wor­king with Russia on the space station.
ir_summary: Astronaut crew returns from International Space Station mission, highlighting continued US-Russia space cooperation despite Ukraine conflict.

title: UK navy sailor accused of plot to pass intel to foreign power
text:
LONDON: A serving member of Britain's Royal Navy appeared in court on Thursday accused of plotting to leak intelligence to a foreign power.

Teddy Young, 24, who joined the navy in April 2024, is alleged to have abused his high-level security clearance while deployed on a navy vessel, according to a written summary of the allegations presented to the court.

He allegedly accessed secret defence and intelligence data and plotted to pass on the information while on his first deployment which began seven months later in November 2024. The foreign power involved was allegedly Russia, according to UK media reports.

Young, who was remanded in custody, was not asked to enter a plea during the short hearing at Westminster Magistrates' Court in central London.

His next appearance will be at London's Old Bailey court on Oct 16.

Young was arrested by counter-terror police at his home in Bedfordshire north of London on Tuesday.

London's Metropolitan Police said earlier he had been charged with obtaining protected information in order to benefit a foreign power under section 1 of the National Security Act which covers principal espionage offences.
ir_summary: UK Royal Navy sailor charged with espionage for allegedly leaking intelligence to Russia.

title: Maduro, wife Flores charged in US over alleged torture
text:
NEW YORK: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores both were hit with an additional US criminal charge on Thursday stemming from accusations they tortured political opponents to retain their grip on power in the South American country.

Maduro and Flores were charged with an additional count of conspiracy to commit torture in addition to the drug trafficking charges they previously faced, according to a superseding indictment filed in Manhattan federal court. Flores, 69, and Maduro, 63, were captured by the US military on January 3 in their Caracas home and brought to New York to face the drug charges.

The surprise raid ended the socialist Maduro's 13 years in power in oil-rich Venezuela, which has since boosted cooperation with the US under the leadership of Maduro's former Vice President Delcy Rodriguez.

Maduro and Flores pleaded not guilty to the drug charges and have been held at Brooklyn's Metropolitan Detention Center since their capture. Their trial is scheduled for June 1, 2027.

Separately, Flores is expected to appear in a US court on Thursday to urge a federal judge to release her from jail for health reasons while she awaits her drug trafficking trial next year.

At a hearing set to start at 10:30am in Manhattan federal court, Flores' lawyers are expected to ask US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein to grant bail so their client can undergo a cardiac procedure and recover in a more comfortable environment.
ir_summary: US charges Venezuelan ex-president Maduro and wife with conspiracy to commit torture against political opponents.

title: Ex-prince Andrew raid warrants ruled ‘unlawful’
text:
LONDON: Disgraced former prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor won a UK legal challenge over searches of his royal homes after police agreed the warrants they obtained were "unlawful", a High Court judge disclosed on Thursday.

However, the court in London must still decide whether police can continue to hold items seized in the raids, with both the judge and police stressing the investigation remained ongoing. King Charles III's brother was arrested on his 66th birthday in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office related to his links to late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

He was released the same day, after hours of police questioning, but has remained under investigation. He has denied all wrongdoing in his associations with the American financier. Thames Valley Police (TVP) searched his former home in Windsor, west of London, and Sandringham, eastern England, but it has now emerged Andrew subsequently launched a legal challenge over the legality of the warrants used.

The Daily Telegraph first reported the legal challenge late Sunday. The newspaper noted it was the first time a member of Britain's royal family has challenged the lawfulness of criminal proceedings against them since the trial of Charles I in 1649.

In the first detailed public disclosures about Andrew's legal action, judge Nicholas Hilliard on Thursday revealed the police had agreed "the search warrants were unlawful". But "the fact that the search warrants were quashed does not bring an investigation to an end, or mean that the whole of the investigation was unlawful''.
ir_summary: UK court rules police warrants for searching Prince Andrew's homes were unlawful, but investigation into his Epstein links continues.

title: Beneath the surface
text:
THE IMF's staff-level agreement with Pakistan on the fourth balance-of-payments and the third climate financing reviews came with little drama — which itself says something.

The mission spent two weeks in Islamabad, wrapped up the 2026 Article IV consultation, and left with a deal that releases $1.2bn once the IMF Executive Board approves it. Nobody expected a different outcome. The Fund is unlikely to push hard against a borrower that is hitting its fiscal targets. Compare this with March, when talks went virtual, ended without an agreement, and dragged on until the Board cleared funds in May. The recent round made fewer headlines because the hard bargaining over the budget had already been done. The current budget is built around a primary surplus of 2pc of GDP, and the lender is now collecting on that commitment. A programme that has settled into a routine reassures markets. It also shows how little room Islamabad has to depart from the script.

The lender's own assessment is generous. It says the authorities have successfully navigated the fallout of the Middle East conflict and that policies have preserved stability. Reserves stand at about $21.5bn and inflation has eased from its May peak. Yet, a closer look shows that, at 10.3pc in September, inflation remains well above the State Bank's medium-term target range. Last year's growth of 3.6pc, with an annual population growth of nearly 2pc, leaves per capita gains thin.

The World Bank put poverty at about 42.4pc for 2025, and said growth was too weak to prevent an additional 1.9m people from slipping below the line in a single year. Exports tell the same story. Goods exports fell about 6pc to $30.1bn, of which textiles accounted for $17.9bn. Imports rose 8pc to $69.8bn, widening the merchandise trade deficit to $39.6bn. Growth in IT services kept total exports near $40bn, which though welcome, is no substitute for a manufacturing base that sells more abroad.

The recommendations deserve more attention than the headline figure. The lender wants the fuel support scheme phased out, calling it costly and too broadly targeted. Unwinding a broad subsidy is politically harder than agreeing to end it on paper. It also wants timely tariff adjustments so that the circular debt does not return, a medium-term tax strategy, private participation in power distribution, better governance of SOEs, and progress on privatisation. Many who have read the earlier review statements will recognise the list. When the same agenda is repeated, the question one must ask is: how much has changed? The Fund's language of commitment does not answer it. The tranche will arrive. What the government has yet to demonstrate is an economy that grows fast enough to cut poverty and sells more abroad — an issue that cannot be put off much longer.
ir_summary: IMF approves $1.2 billion for Pakistan after review, praising economic stability despite persistent inflation and poverty challenges.

title: Moscow disagreement
text:
THE fact that a consensus on how to deal with terrorism originating in Taliban-ruled Afghanistan eludes regional states was made clear at the recently held Moscow Format moot. The event was attended by nearly all of Afghanistan's neighbours, including Pakistan. However, there was no joint statement issued because, in the words of the Russian envoy for Afghanistan, "our Afghan and Pakistani colleagues didn't see eye to eye".

The Taliban regime had also sent its representatives. The main sticking point was the Taliban's objection to including Afghanistan in a "terrorist context". However, as Pakistan's envoy put it, it was essential to address "the menace of terrorism emanating from Afghan soil". Russia offered its good offices to help de-escalate matters between Kabul and Islamabad, though it noted that the Moscow Format was not a forum for resolving bilateral disputes.

Both the Taliban's denialism, and Russia's apparently soft stance towards the Afghan terrorism problem, are unfortunate. Groups that find shelter in Afghanistan under the Taliban threaten the entire region. Thus, all of Afghanistan's neighbours need to speak with one voice regarding the 'export' of terrorism.

Russia is the only state that recognises the Taliban regime. Moscow has its own reasons for indulging the Taliban; these include the need to fight IS-K, which is a common enemy of Russia and the Taliban rulers, as well as to check US and Western influence in Afghanistan. But engagement with Kabul must not be allowed to obscure the fact that some of the deadliest terrorist groups in the world find refuge on Afghan soil.

Other regional forums, such as the SCO and the ECO, have highlighted the need to address the terrorist threat emanating from Afghanistan. China, which has significant economic interests in Afghanistan, has also pointed to this terrorist threat. The UN Security Council, too, has frequently noted that Afghanistan under Taliban rule has once again become a haven for various terrorist groups.

Pakistan's insistence, therefore, that Afghanistan's terrorism problem be highlighted reflects the reality of the situation. If Kabul addresses the issue sincerely and restrains terrorist groups, it will benefit not only the Afghan people but the entire region.
ir_summary: Regional talks in Moscow on Afghanistan's terrorism issue failed due to disagreements between Pakistan and the Taliban regime.

title: Vanished girls
text:
THE scourge of female disappearances in Pakistan should be a matter of shame. Institutional reforms and criminalising chauvinistic traditions remain long overdue measures. The Lahore High Court, during the hearing of a case of disappearance, was informed by Punjab's police chief that over 500 cases of girls reported missing were still pending in the province. The figure was shocking for the court. Not only was concern expressed at the ordeal of the families of the missing, the negligence of police was also underscored in this regard. Chief Justice Aalia Neelum inquired about mechanisms to tackle cases involving women and children. The IGP stated that such incidents would be handled by special committees.

The crisis of our 'missing' daughters has detrimental repercussions for victims. Those recovered are forced to live with multiple accusations from their kin who often suspect sexual exploitation. Many fall prey to sex trafficking and are sold to organised prostitution networks, or are registered as kidnap cases when they run away to escape forced marriages. As most of them hail from poor areas and families, the authorities often dismiss their kidnappings as 'elopement', without any investigation. That it takes various court orders for police to pursue these abductions implies gross apathy, negligence, and the absence of accountability. For years, adequate action to arrest the trend in the rural and urban areas of the province, and the lack of protection for victims who return or are rescued against the tag of 'dishonour', have been non-existent. It is time these cases were also seen as part of the thriving sex trafficking rings in the country. In 2022, police figures showed that 3,571 abducted girls and women were missing across Punjab; a total of 40,585 women were kidnapped between 2017 and January 2022. Keeping the girl child safe entails going beyond reasons of domestic dispute and investigating prolonged disappearances as possible cases of trafficking.
ir_summary: Lahore High Court hears about over 500 missing girls cases in Punjab, highlighting police negligence and institutional failures in Pakistan.

title: PSX retreats despite $1.2bn IMF lifeline
text:
KARACHI: Amid persistent volatility stemming from regional and political concerns, the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) faltered on Thursday after staging an early rally driven by a staff-level agreement (SLA) between Pakistan and the visiting International Monetary Fund (IMF) staff mission.

Strong buying at attractive valuations lost steam mid-session as investors took profits after an upsurge in oil prices revived fears of energy supply disruption amid attacks on oil tankers and heightened the risk of higher imported costs amid inflationary pressures.

Topline Securities Ltd said the index saw a volatile session, initially gaining around 906 points on positive sentiment following the signing of the SLA. However, early gains failed to hold as investors took profits at higher levels, and the index fell 1,138 points, or 0.68 per cent, to close at 167,442. The index traded in a wide range of 167,450-169,487 during the session.

Ali Najib, Deputy Head of Trading at Arif Habib Ltd, said the market opened on a positive note following a successful IMF review and the completion of the 4th Extended Fund Facility and 3rd RSF reviews, paving the way for $1.2bn in disbursements, subject to Executive Board approval, bringing total disbursements under the two programmes to $5.7bn.

However, the positive momentum faded as international oil prices surged nearly 4pc, amid heightened Middle East supply concerns, increased shipping attacks in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, and US production disruptions. Renewed US-Iran tensions further dampened sentiment, prompting profit-taking at higher levels and pushing the index into negative territory.

On the sectoral front, power generation increased 5.1pc year-on-year in August, while net metering's share in total generation edged up 10bps. However, net-metered units fell 27.2pc month-on-month, suggesting greater reliance on the national grid.

Index-heavy stocks remained under pressure, with United Bank, Fauji Fertiliser, Systems Ltd, Engro Fertiliser, Pakistan Oilfield, Pakistan Petroleum, Habib Bank, Fatima Fertiliser, Engro Holdings, and Bank Alfalah emerging as the major detractors, collectively shaving approximately 601 points from the benchmark.

Investor participation weakened sharply as trading volume plunged 37.65pc to 365.86 million shares and traded value dipped 20.76pc to Rs17.6bn. K-Electric led the volume chart with 29.6m shares.

Analysts expect the market to remain volatile, as support from the IMF agreement is offset by elevated oil prices and geopolitical risks. The 167,000-170,000 range remains key for the week's final session, with attention focused on oil prices and foreign flows.
ir_summary: Pakistan's stock market fell despite IMF loan progress due to oil price surge and regional tensions.

title: Karachi IT Park hits snags again
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Karachi IT Park project has faced another delay after two rounds of tendering failed to attract any bids, prompting the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunications to adopt a new strategy for awarding the project.

According to a report prepared by the ministry, work on the IT Park is now targeted to begin in June 2027. A third tender will be issued after an independent review of the complete bidding documents.

The ministry has set Oct 25, 2026, as the target date for completing the vetting of the bidding documents. An independent construction contracts consultant will review the revised request for proposal (RFP) before the re-tendering process.

The ministry plans to obtain approval for re-tendering from Korea Exim Bank by Nov 15, 2026, with the third tender scheduled to be issued on the same date.

Interested eligible Korean companies will be invited to participate in an open competitive bidding process. The deadline for submission of bids has been set for Jan 4, 2027. Technical bids will be evaluated by the project's technical committee, while financial bids will be assessed separately. Following the evaluation process, the Project Steering and Review Committee will examine the final recommendations.

The final approval of the bids will be obtained from Korea Exim Bank, according to the ministry's documents. The government has set March 25, 2027, as the target date for signing the contract for the Karachi IT Park.
ir_summary: Pakistan's IT ministry delays Karachi IT Park project again after failed tenders, plans new bidding with Korean firms and Exim Bank funding.

title: Flour millers deliver another price shock
text:
KARACHI: As the Sindh government gears up to release wheat stocks at Rs12,500 per 100kg bag from Oct 15 to stabilise flour prices, fearless millers on Thursday further jacked up prices by Rs6 per kg across various flour varieties.

The total increase by the millers in the last few days stood at Rs20 per kg, as the provincial government and the city administration did not take serious notice of the surging flour prices.

After the fresh increase of Rs6 per kg, the rates of flour No. 2.5, maida and fine flour, issued by the mills, are now Rs161, Rs173 and Rs176 per kg, respectively.

Consumers will face further price shock in the coming days when retailers pass on the impact of the latest hike.

The Sindh government has 346,414 tonnes of wheat stock. With 190,000 tonnes from the Pakistan Agriculture Storage and Services Corporation and 300,000 tonnes of imported wheat to be added, the total stocks available for release will increase to 836,414 tonnes.
ir_summary: Flour millers in Sindh raise prices despite government plans to release wheat stocks to stabilize costs.

title: Minister orders food price monitoring amid surge
text:
ISLAMABAD: The National Price Monitoring Committee (NPMC) on Wednesday reviewed wholesale-retail price gaps and prices of essential commodities and directed relevant authorities to monitor transport fares.

A meeting of the NPMC, presided over by Planning and Development Minister Ahsan Iqbal, reviewed the monthly and weekly inflation situation, prices of essential commodities and implementation of previous decisions.

An official announcement said the minister expressed concern over rising prices of essential commodities, particularly wheat flour, and directed provincial and district administrations to strengthen monitoring of supplies, market arrivals, hoarding, profiteering and unjustified price increases.

Mr Ahsan directed the authorities concerned to compare current transport fares with fares prevailing after the previous fuel price increase to determine whether the increase in fuel prices had resulted in any disproportionate rise in fares.

He also directed the Ministry of Food Security to examine why DAP prices remained high in Pakistan despite a decline in international prices, stressing that the benefit of lower international prices should be reflected in the domestic market.

The minister directed that the inspection and quality assessment report regarding ghee, edible oil and milk products be submitted within one week. He said that if the industry had proposed third-party validation, its cost should be borne by the industry and not the government.

He asked the provincial governments to closely monitor wholesale and retail prices and take enforcement action where unjustified gaps existed, particularly in major markets including Lahore and Karachi. He also called for close monitoring of supply chains and distribution costs to prevent disproportionate pass-through of fuel price increases to essential food prices.
ir_summary: Pakistani minister orders monitoring of food prices and transport fares to control inflation and prevent profiteering.

title: Economic Coordination Committee raises duty on tyre, bike parts import
text:
ISLAMABAD: The government on Thursday increased additional customs duty (ACD) on import of tyres and motorcycle parts produced locally and approved first-loss coverage for small and medium enterprises and small farmers.

The decisions were taken at a meeting of the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the cabinet, presided over by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb.

The committee also approved investment of Export Development Fund (EDF) resources in government securities and allowed Rs57.85 billion in supplementary grants a day after a staff-level agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and at the conclusion of the first quarter of the fiscal year.

Under the decision, the government increased ACD from 4pc to 11pc on import of radial tyres and motorcycle parts that are manufactured locally. It also increased ACD from 11pc to 31pc on motorbike parts imported by local manufacturers. Both measures are aimed at facilitating local manufacturers of radial tyres and motorcycle parts.

"On a summary submitted by the Revenue Division, the ECC approved an amendment to SRO 693(I)/2006 concerning the levy of additional customs duty on import of tyres being manufactured locally. The measure is aimed at promoting domestic manufacturing," an official statement said.

The ECC also approved a financing framework developed by the State Bank of Pakistan to facilitate the inclusion of Agency Financial Institutions (AFIs) under the government's existing Risk Coverage Schemes for Small Enterprises and Small Farmers through wholesale and agency arrangements. The framework provides for first-loss coverage to loans up to 20pc for SMEs and 10pc each to small farmers and medium size industries.
