"The framework aims to broaden access to finance by leveraging the outreach of eligible microfinance and non-banking financial institutions," the statement added.

The ECC also approved an Addendum to the Second Supplemental Trust Deed of the Credit Guarantee Trust Fund (CGTF), originally meant for Prime Minister's Mera Pakistan Mera Ghar scheme, expanding its scope to facilitate more effective utilisation of the existing credit guarantee facility to support affordable housing finance.

The meeting approved 11 supplementary grants totalling Rs57.85bn.

These included Rs2bn for the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority to facilitate implementation of its approved business plan in line with the prime minister's vision. It also approved another Rs11.329bn for the Industries and Production Division to meet the immediate funding requirements of the Utility Stores Corporation and facilitate completion of its closure process.

On the request of the Privatisation Division, the ECC approved Rs8bn for the Public Private Partnership Authority (P3A) to support the development and implementation of infrastructure projects through public-private partnerships. The meeting also approved a Rs10bn grant for the Ministry of Railways to provide budgetary cover for the Thar Coal Rail Connectivity Project and facilitate the utilisation of indigenous Thar coal for power generation and other industrial sectors.
ir_summary: Pakistan's Economic Coordination Committee raises import duties on tires and motorcycle parts to protect local manufacturers.

title: EXPLAINER-Makkah pact and defence of the Kingdom
text:
THE Makkah alliance has moved, in less than two months, from a political declaration towards practical cooperation, though it remains a few steps short of becoming a fully operational military alliance.

Its Strategic Political and Defence Committee, which met in Riyadh on Oct 5, decided "to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments".

The operative part of the decision, however, is narrower than some of the headlines it has generated. The three countries agreed to "take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the Kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the Parties".

The Saudi urgency to see the alliance working is understandable. Through September and into early October, Yemen's Ansar Allah group, commonly known as the Houthis, fired missiles and drones towards southern Saudi cities and energy facilities, with Riyadh saying the attacks also targeted the holy cities. One such strike hit a power station in Madina supplying Masjid-i-Nabvi.

At the same time, the Aden-based Presidential Leadership Council announced a counteroffensive to reverse Ansar Allah gains along the Red Sea coast. Government forces, backed by coalition air support, claimed to have recaptured Mocha and positions near Bab al Mandeb, although those claims remain contested.

The Riyadh meeting and developments in Yemen came within a day of each other and are politically linked, even if they are not demonstrably part of the same operational plan. The committee's statement, importantly, made no reference to Mocha, Bab al Mandeb or operations inside Yemen, and did not name the Houthis.

The alliance has nevertheless covered considerable ground since its inception on Aug 7. An inaugural summit was followed by a meeting of the Strategic and Political Committee in Istanbul at the end of August.

On Sept 25, the three countries' military chiefs met in Riyadh and agreed to pursue intelligence sharing, military coordination and capability integration, though they made no mention of a joint command. On the sidelines, Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman also discussed continuing "joint efforts" against attacks on the Kingdom.

The Oct 5 meeting took the next institutional steps, endorsing retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood as the alliance's first secretary general, placing the Riyadh-based secretariat under his charge and authorising the rapid deployment of military forces and capabilities already "agreed".

The progress so far includes a political commitment, an institutional head and secretariat, two committee meetings, a meeting of military chiefs and a decision to begin implementation.

What remains missing is a standing assigned force, a joint commander, publicly defined rules of engagement and a published military doctrine. There is also no public authorisation for Pakistani or Turkish forces to participate in combat operations inside Yemen.

In fact, Turkish officials told Reuters on Wednesday that Ankara was "sending mainly defensive and technical support to Saudi Arabia to help it fight the Houthis, adding that the support expected from Turkiye was only in the form of military equipment, intelligence sharing, and weapons systems, and that no other form of deployment had taken place as part of the alliance so far.

Understanding the alliance requires answers to basic questions that remain unresolved as to what constitutes a threat or an attack, against whom has the alliance been formed, what would trigger a response, and who would decide on action and through which command structure?

In the absence of a published charter and doctrine, its working principles have to be pieced together from the August agreement, subsequent government statements and the Oct 5 decision.

The threat, in the language used by the parties, is an armed attack on a member's security, sovereignty or territorial integrity, with particular emphasis on protecting Makkah and Madinah. There is, however, no public definition covering attacks on forces, ships, diplomatic missions or personnel outside national territory. The Houthis are impliedly identified as the attackers, while Iran is widely seen as their enabling power, but neither is named in the agreement.

Collective deterrence appears to mean making the commitment credible through military readiness, coordination and the ability to respond. No punishment strategy has been published, while a response seems contingent on a request from the country under threat, agreement on the measures to be taken and compliance with each country's national laws.

Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar has described the agreement as defensive, without an offensive agenda. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said Pakistani and Turkish forces would play a supporting role, including reconnaissance, while Saudi forces conduct combat operations.

The Oct 5 decision, which provides for deployment inside the Kingdom rather than a joint campaign, is consistent with this narrower interpretation. The capabilities under discussion, including air and missile defence, reconnaissance, intelligence, counter-drone systems and technical support, also point to a defensive design.

Yet the gap between the public positions of Pakistan and Türkiye, and Saudi expectations, is already visible. Prince Khalid said after the meeting that the committee had affirmed solidarity "in confronting the sinful aggressions that targeted the Kingdom and the Holy Sanctuaries, activating collective deterrence against these aggressions, and against all those standing behind them".

The reference to Houthi attacks is clear enough, but "all those standing behind them" is a broader Saudi political signal absent from the joint statement and not further defined. Pakistan and Turkiye have maintained that the alliance is not directed against another country.

The three partners may not wish to emphasise their differing interests, but these are clear. Riyadh wants protection for its territory and greater pressure on those attacking it, whereas Pakistan wants to honour its commitment to Saudi Arabia without being drawn into another Yemen war or a confrontation with Iran and Türkiye seeks a larger regional security role but faces its own political and legal constraints. The agreement can accommodate these differences as long as its mission remains defensive.

Its language is carefully circumscribed as it refers to capabilities already "agreed", rather than whatever forces Riyadh might request, and specifies deployment inside the Kingdom under national legislation. An Article 5 like commitment that still requires consultation, agreement and action under national law does not amount to an automatic military response.

Saudi Arabia can therefore expect defensive reinforcement on its territory, political backing and supporting capabilities for its existing campaign. It cannot yet treat the agreement as an automatic commitment to operations beyond its borders or as a joint military doctrine against unnamed states or groups backing the Houthis.

The reference to national legislation is particularly important. In Pakistan, a wider military role could revive debate over the unanimous parliamentary resolution of April 2015, which called for neutrality in the Yemen conflict while pledging that Pakistan would stand shoulder to shoulder with Saudi Arabia if its territorial integrity or the two Holy Mosques came under threat.

A deployment to defend Saudi territory and the holy sites, including the Pakistani presence already there, can be presented as consistent with that resolution. Participation in fighting around Mocha, however, would be much harder to reconcile with its language.

Any move beyond defensive deployment could therefore require fresh political authorisation, raising questions about how far the government could depart from the earlier parliamentary position.

Turkiye faces a different constraint as Article 92 of its constitution requires parliamentary approval for deploying troops abroad, and no such approval has been publicly reported. Equipment, technical teams and specialists can move faster than military units, allowing Ankara to contribute within a legal process different from Pakistan's.

The trilateral framework is also building on, rather than replacing, the existing Pakistan-Saudi military relationship. Under the 2025 Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement, Pakistani air and support elements were already deployed in the Kingdom.

This was possibly what Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry meant when he recently told a CNN interviewer that Pakistani troops have been in the Kingdom "for decades", and across multiple domains.

The understanding between Field Marshal Munir and Prince Khalid to continue cooperation against the attacks kept that bilateral channel active while aligning it more closely with the Makkah Alliance.

The additional capabilities envisaged under the Oct 5 decision are more likely to involve air defence, intelligence, reconnaissance and specialist support than a large Pakistani ground contingent for Yemen, which would sit uneasily with both the 2015 resolution and the government's stated position.

The next test is how far implementation goes and whether additional Pakistani air defence or air assets are moved to Saudi Arabia, whether Turkish systems and specialists arrive, and whether the supporting role remains confined to Saudi territory. Any extension into fighting along the Red Sea coast would turn the difference between the agreed text and Riyadh's wider interpretation of "all those standing behind them" into a substantive issue.

There is also a practical obstacle to an integrated defence alliance, which is that interoperability remains undeveloped. The three militaries operate different equipment ecosystems, and there is no public evidence of a common air picture, joint fusion centre or system through which a Turkish or Pakistani sensor can routinely cue a Saudi weapon.

Intelligence cooperation has indeed been agreed, but cooperation does not in itself mean integration. For now, the alliance can add capabilities to Saudi Arabia's defences without necessarily being able to fight as a single force.
ir_summary: Saudi-led Makkah alliance moves towards military cooperation amid Houthi attacks and Yemen conflict developments.

title: KP CM Afridi seeks law to impeach governor, rejects operations
text:
• KP CM tells chief secretary, police chief not to follow 'unconstitutional' orders• Insists Centre's counterterrorism approach failed; claims KP can restore peace within 100 days• Joins march supporters in Bara; says future strategy to be announced in Swabi• Kundi says governor's rule, emergency will be imposed 'to save KP'

PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Wednesday took strong exception to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi's meeting with the chief secretary and provincial police chief and called for legislation to provide for the governor's impeachment for "violating the Constitution".

"A prime minister and the chief minister can be sent home through a vote of no confidence. If there is no law, the KP Assembly will legislate [for impeachment of the governor] and nobody will be allowed to derail democracy," Mr Afridi said.

In a video message shared by his office, the chief minister accused the governor of acting unconstitutionally and attempting to provoke the provincial government but said his administration would continue to abide by the law and Constitution.

"We will follow the Con­s­titution and that hurts 'them'," Mr Afridi said while chairing a meeting of the provincial cabinet.

His remarks came a day after Governor Kundi cha­i­red a meeting with Chief Secretary Shahab Ali Shah and KP Police Chief Zulfiqar Hameed on the province's security situation.

Mr Afridi urged the two officials not to comply with any unconstitutional or illegal order from anyone.

KP Advocate General Shah Faisal Utmankhel told the meeting that under Article 131 of the Constitution, the governor could seek information from the chief minister, but could not do so independently.

"If I do not order you to take an unconstitutional step, do not obey if someone pushes you to follow any unconstitutional order," Mr Afridi said.

The chief minister direc­ted the chief secretary to advise the provincial admi­n­i­stration against involvement in any unconstitutional activity and ordered the inspector general of police to investigate firing on PTI workers in Upper South Waziristan.

Mr Afridi accused the PPP-affiliated governor of staging a "drama" by convening the security meeting and termed the move unconstitutional. He said the provincial assembly, cabinet and government were fully functional and that such a meeting was unacceptable when the provincial government enjoyed a two-thirds majority.

Turning his criticism towards the PPP, Mr Afridi blamed former president Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, along with Gen Yahya Khan, for the separation of East Pakistan and accused President Asif Ali Zardari of seeking to create a similar situation.

"We will not allow any conspiracy to break up Pakistan to succeed," he said, alleging that the PPP had always prioritised personal interests over national interests.

Meanwhile, Governor Kundi said later on Wednesday that an emergency or governor's rule would "definitely" be imposed in KP if the prime minister and the president considered it necessary to "save the province" amid the security situation.

Speaking to Geo News, Mr Kundi said there had been precedents for the imposition of an emergency or governor's rule.

"In Balochistan, the PPP had to end its government for law and order and impose an emergency," he said. Asked whether such a measure would be sustainable if imposed in KP, Mr Kundi said, "The first thing [to decide] is when and whether it is imposed. We can discuss its sustainability in another programme."

Mr Afridi also reiterated his opposition to the Centre's counterterrorism policy and said his government would not allow further military operations in the province.

He maintained that terrorism had again been "imposed on the province" and said his government had worked to strengthen the police, Counter-Terrorism Depar­tment and Special Branch since he took office on Oct 15, 2025. Mr Afridi alleged that successive federal governments had imposed military operations on KP since 2004, displacing people who had still not received full compensation.

He claimed nearly Rs100bn in compensation remained outstanding and said tribal families displaced from their homes had been promised Rs400,000 per household, but many had yet to receive the full amount.

He also referred to a commitment to provide Rs370m to Rs380m a month to displaced people from North Waziristan living at the Baka Khel camp, stressing that the promised payments were still not being made.

Mr Afridi said KP was fighting terrorism while also dealing with the consequences of federal policies and claimed peace could be restored within 100 days if the approach advocated by provincial stakeholders was adopted.

He argued that the Centre's counterterrorism policy had failed to bring peace either in KP or Balochistan and called for a change in approach. "A shift in policy is necessary. KP can establish peace within 100 days," he said.

Later on Wednesday, PTI workers from Bara, Jamrud and Landi Kotal welcomed the chief minister in his hometown of Bara as he travelled towards Peshawar as part of the party's march.

Addressing supporters from the top of a truck, Mr Afridi said no pressure tactic could weaken his resolve and again vowed not to allow further military operations in KP.

He said the rights of the province would be pursued and announced that the future strategy for the march would be unveiled on reaching Swabi.

The chief minister and participants in the march were expected to stay overnight in Bara before leaving for Peshawar on Thursday (today).

The provincial cabinet approved forwarding to the federal government a joint resolution adopted by the KP Assembly condemning an incident in which the chief minister was allegedly taken away by Punjab Police in a vehicle, separated from his security detail and later left on the roadside without security during a visit to Punjab.

The cabinet also approved obtaining $250m in World Bank financing for the READY-KP project under the bank's applicable financing terms.
ir_summary: KP Chief Minister seeks impeachment law for governor and rejects federal counterterrorism approach, asserting provincial authority.

title: PMDC exam for foreign graduates rescheduled
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Medical and Den­tal Council has rescheduled the National Regist­ration Examination (NRE) Step-I from Oct 11 to Nov 8 due to unavoidable circumstances and now foreign medical graduates will face a nearly monthlong delay.

In a notification dated Oct 5, the PMDC cited "unavoidable circumstan­ces" for the move and said Step-1 of the NRE exam will now be held on Nov 8.

A senior PMDC official told Dawn on Wednesday that the decision was made due to the prevailing political situation and possible road closures.

The rescheduling comes after the PTI on Oct 4 launched a long march from Khyber Pakhtu­nkhwa towards Islama­bad, despite warnings from the federal government against such a move.

NRE is a mandatory requirement under an Act of Parliament, aimed at ensuring transparency, standardisation, and quality in medical and dental education and professional practice in Pakistan.

The National University of Medical Sciences in Rawalpindi is entrusted with conducting NRE to "ensure credibility, integrity, and transparency," according to the PMDC.

The exam is conducted in two steps at least twice a year in accordance with the approved NRE standards, structure, and syllabus, and as per a curriculum at par with the medicine and dentistry degrees in Pakistan.

Foreign medical graduates who have earned degrees in medicine or dentistry in languages other than English have to clear two steps or the NRE exam in order to start a house job and get a licence to practise in Pakistan.
ir_summary: Pakistan's medical council reschedules exam for foreign graduates due to political unrest and possible road closures.

title: IMF holds back clearance for industry power tariff plan
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Interna­tional Monetary Fund (IMF) did not immediately clear a proposed time-of-use electricity tariff for industry aimed at boosting consumption during off-peak hours as its team concluded a fortnight-long review with Pakistani authorities on Wednesday without announcing a staff-level agreement.

Official sources said the talks had concluded successfully and a staff-level agreement was expected to be announced by the IMF shortly.

They said both Fund program­mes — the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility and $1.4bn Resi­lience and Sustainability Facility — were being implemented in "letter and spirit" and they did not foresee any hurdle to IMF executive board approval for the disbursement of about $1.2bn within four to five weeks.

The IMF staff mission, led by Iva Petrova, did not issue its customary end-of-mission statement, pending approval from the Fund's headquarters.

Sources said the IMF had sought more data and clarifications on the proposed time-of-use (TOU) tariff. Since the proposal was not part of the ongoing programmes, the staff may come up with its formal position from Washington. "The package is pending with the IMF," an official source said.

The proposal is aimed at addressing a growing "duck curve" in electricity demand caused by an unprecedented shift towards solar and other alternative energy sources, leaving grid capacity underutilised during the day while demand rises sharply after sunset.

Under the proposed package, the government wants to raise fixed charges for industry to recover a larger share of capacity costs while lowering energy charges through three or four different tariff bands during the day.

At present, industry pays about Rs1,250 per kilowatt per month in capacity charges, recovering around 20 per cent of the fixed costs attributable to the sector. However, the industry is required to pay higher variable rate for energy part.

The power division believes the existing structure offers little incentive to industry to increase grid consumption to reduce its overall electricity costs.

It has argued that the reform is also necessary for the financial sustainability of the power system by balancing demand and supply more evenly over 24 hours.

The division has proposed incr­e­asing the capacity charge to Rs7,000-8,000 while reducing the energy charge to Rs8-9.50 per unit between midnight and 9am compared to Rs16-18 per unit at present.

For the solar hours between 9am and 4pm, the energy charge has been proposed at Rs5.60-6.30 per unit, before rising to Rs10-11.30 per unit from 4pm to midnight.

According to a regulatory filing earlier this week, the power division believes the structure would encourage industry to use more grid electricity during solar hours and help stabilise the system. It said expensive grid supply under the existing rigid tariff structure was encouraging industries to shift towards solar, wind and other sources.

Official sources said the IMF had made no new demands during the review except for some makeup adjustments to bridge past slippages.

The revenue target remained unchanged, with greater emphasis on meeting the half-yearly target following first-quarter collections that exceeded the target, they said.

The two sides also agreed to expedite groundwork for targeted gas subsidies through the social protection system to help contain gas sector circular debt, while moving towards implementation of BISP-based subsidies for the poorest electricity consumers from January next year following the introduction of a revised base tariff.

Power distribution companies have already filed petitions for base tariff adjustments during the review period to demonstrate preparedness for the transition.

The government also assured the IMF of plans to reduce cross-subsidies borne by industry and curtail gas sector debt, which has risen to around Rs3.6 trillion, including principal payables of about Rs1.8tr and an almost equivalent amount in accrued interest and late payment surcharges.

Gas companies have reported that the introduction of the protected category for domestic consumers, with tariffs of Rs200-350 per mmBtu, widened the pricing gap and contributed to the increase in circular debt.

Only four of the 12 consumer slabs covered the cost of gas supply during winter, while tariffs remained below breakeven levels for around eight months of the year despite substantial fixed charges.

Not to be defined as prior action but the authorities may have to take a few procedural steps between conclusion of ongoing talks with the IMF and the scheduling of its executive board meeting to ensure smooth processing of Pakistan's case for disbursement of $1.2bn and seek waivers for a couple of unavoidable slippages that had already happened for the end-June 2026 period.

The IMF structural benchmark committed by the government requires major policy reform by the end of January next year to replace the budgeted tariff differential subsidy and cross-subsidy system with a targeted budgeted subsidy framework for low-income consumers via BISP.

The World Bank is assisting the government to link power consumers to national socio-economic registry. The government has given an undertaking to complete the technical linking along with validity checks by the end of November to determine eligibility criteria.
ir_summary: IMF delays approval of Pakistan's proposed industrial electricity tariff plan, seeking more data during review.

title: Govt still willing  to talk to PTI, but refuses to be ‘held hostage’
text:
ISLAMABAD: Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Wednesday that the door remained open for talks with the main opposition PTI but stressed that the party could not hold the government "hostage" to its demands.

Talking to the media, Mr Sanaullah said the government would not allow the opposition to use dialogue as a tool to make political demands.

"The doors for talks are open," he said, recalling Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's remarks a day earlier urging the PTI leadership to sit down with the government and abandon its protest plans.

However, he said negotiations could not be used to strong-arm the government. The PML-N leader accused the PTI of obstructing efforts for peace and lamented a growing culture of intolerance and "below-the-belt" politics.

Hours-long negotiations between the government and opposition during a second round of talks ended in deadlock on Sunday. The meeting at Parliament House began on Saturday afternoon and continued into the early hours of Sunday. Discussions focused on the PTI's planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad.

After the talks collapsed, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi accused Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of "sabotaging" the negotiations by changing the draft of an agreement after points had already been settled.

However, PTI leaders said reconciliation with the government was not possible without involving incarcerated party fou­nder Imran Khan in the dialogue process.

They also said the talks failed because the government was unwilling to pursue a collective strategy against terrorism.

Mr Sanaullah rejected the PTI's claim that it was being excluded from decisions on the Centre's counterterrorism policy as "completely wrong" and "misleading".

He said the reasons for the deadlock had been misrepresented and maintained that the counterterrorism policy was already being implemented through daily intelligence-based operations (IBOs), which he said were producing "huge success". He also claimed the PTI opposed such operations.

In June 2024, the government announced a reinvigorated "Operation Azm-i-Istehkam" but, following criticism, clarified that it would involve intensifying ongoing IBOs and later rebranded it as "Vision Azm-i-Istehkam".

Mr Sanaullah said the armed forces and law enforcement agencies were making sacrifices to sustain these operations.

He also rejected claims that fresh military operations would lead to large-scale displacement, saying the ongoing IBOs would continue under the existing counterterrorism policy.

Speaking about tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan, Mr Sanaullah said Islamabad had been "fair" in demanding that Afghan territory not be used for terrorist attacks against Pakistan.

He said that during several rounds of talks, the Afghan interim government had accepted as valid evidence presented by Pakistan regarding attacks emanating from Afghanistan, but it had declined to guarantee that its territory would not be used for terrorism against Pakistan.

"Pakistan's policy is that it has the right to neutralise training camps or any activity on Afghan land that could cause terrorism in Pakistan later on," Mr Sanaullah said, adding that the policy was based on Pakistan's experience over more than four decades.

He accused the PTI of opposing the policy and prioritising politics over "national interest".

Referring to the party's previous protests in Islamabad, including those in 2022 and 2024, Mr Sanaullah said the recent rise in terrorism had claimed the lives of children, civilians and soldiers in KP.

"On one hand, the martyrs' bodies are lying there, and on the other hand, the entire provincial government is playing the dhol and chanting slogans, urging people to join the march on Islamabad," he said and termed the attitude of the KP government "unacceptable".

Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif criticised the PTI-led KP government over its "complete detachment from terrorism in the province and criminal indifference".

"Enough is enough!!!" he wrote in a post on X.

"The PTI provincial government is roaming the streets for a so-called failed political long march, while its facilitators have unleashed a fresh wave of terrorism against the people of KP during this very time," he said.

Mr Asif referred to Tuesday's attacks in Dera Ismail Khan, in which customs officials were among five people killed.

He accused the provincial cabinet, including the chief minister, of ignoring the security situation while remaining focused on their "politically failed long march".

The defence minister also criticised the chief minister for reportedly scheduling a meeting to question the inspector general of police and the chief secretary over their attendance at the governor's security meeting.

He accused the provincial government of abandoning the people to the threat of terrorism and alleged that it was in "complete collusion"

with terrorists, citing evidence of a "facilitator ecosystem".

Recalling past arrests of former premier Nawaz Sharif and his family members, as well as PML-N leaders, Mr Asif said, "Time has proven that the allegations were just allegations and they were imprisoned at Imran Khan's behest."

Yet, he stressed, the PML-N fulfilled its parliamentary role responsibly under the Constitution and did not hold the country and institutions "hostage".

The defence minister said the "time has come to make crucial decisions", adding that KP could no longer be left "to the mercy of incompetent, insensitive rulers and Taliban allies".

He stressed that the unity of the country could not be put at risk. "An entire province cannot be held hostage. Enough is enough," he said.
ir_summary: Pakistani government official says talks with opposition PTI are possible but rejects being pressured over demands and counterterrorism policy.

title: Meeting to tackle Iran trade hurdles next week
text:
GWADAR: Chiefs of Gwadar Port Authority (GPA) and Customs Transit Trade on Wednesday decided to convene a comprehensive multi-stakeholder meeting next Thursday to finalise a concrete action plan for streamlining transit trade and cargo movement to Iran via Gwadar Port.

GPA Chairman Noorul Haq Baloch met Customs Transit Trade Director General Irfan Javed at the Directorate General of Customs Transit Trade Office.

The decision to convene a meeting followed discussions on facilitating, streamlining, and organising cargo transit to Iran through the Gabd/Rimdhan 250 border crossing.

Officials noted that despite clear directives from the Ministry of Commerce and the Federal Board of Revenue, cross-border trade via Gwadar Port continues to face operational bottlenecks.

In a separate engagement in Karachi, Mr Baloch met Karachi Port Trust Chairman retired Rear Admiral Shahid Ahmed at the KPT head office to discuss enhancing connectivity and maritime economic growth. The officials exchanged views on current cargo traffic patterns and strategic measures to strengthen Pakistan's maritime sector.
ir_summary: Pakistani officials plan a meeting to streamline transit trade and cargo movement to Iran via Gwadar Port.

title: No more talks before meeting Imran: Achakzai
text:
QUETTA: Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) chairman, National Assembly Opposition Leader and head of the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) Mahmood Khan Achakzai has said negotiations between the government and opposition cannot resolve Pakistan's crisis without a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan.

He was addressing a PkMAP gathering at Baz Muhammad Sha­heed Ground in Zhob on Wednesday to mark the anniversary of the Oct 7, 1983, martyrs of democracy.

Mr Achakzai said that if one side was consulting its leaders and stakeholders, the PTI and opposition had the right to meet the jailed ex-premier. "Until I meet Imran Khan, I will not be part of any negotiations," he said.

He said the PTI had placed its trust in him and he would strive to honour it. "Why is the government afraid of our meeting with Imran Khan?" he wondered.

Mr Achakzai warned that imposing governor's rule or an emergency in KP would have serious political consequences. "Impose governor's rule if you wish; we will announce people's rule and hold protests in every district," he warned.

He said the situation had reached a point where Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had no option but to move forward.

He said powerful quarters had tried to break Imran Khan, but, by the grace of Allah, he had remained steadfast. "The time has now come for those who sought to break him to begin breaking themselves," he said.

Mr Achakzai urged all political forces to agree on at least one national agenda to establish a course of action for a prosperous future of Pakistan's 250 million people.

Recalling the Oct 7, 1983, protest against military dictator Gen Ziaul Haq, he said PkMAP workers had taken to the streets against martial law and the usurpation of the people's right to govern themselves.

Protesters were directly fired upon, he said. He miraculously survived, while four companions were martyred, dozens injured and hundreds arrested.

"Today, we pay tribute to the sacrifices of all those martyrs," he added.

He said an enormous amount of Pashtun blood had been shed over nearly half a century, but powerful vested interests remained unsatisfied. The only "crime" of the Pashtuns, he said, was their love for their land.

Mr Achakzai said Pashtuns must set aside mutual grievances, resolve disputes through jirgas and strengthen unity and solidarity.

He said appointments to the posts of Chief Election Commis­s­i­o­ner and Election Commission members whose terms had expired sho­uld follow the procedure prescr­ibed by the Constitution and law.

He said he was ready to meet the prime minister at any neutral, public venue.

On the occasion, Mr Achakzai also demanded that judges, political leaders and workers who had opposed martial law and the Provisional Constitutional Orders be declared national heroes.

Welcoming the Russian foreign minister's statement on Afgha­ni­s­tan at the 18th meeting of the Moscow Format Consultations, he said powers that had intervened in Afghanistan, along with their allies, owed the country a debt.

They were responsible, he said, for fulfilling their obligations towards Afghanistan's stability, development and prosperity.
ir_summary: Pakistani opposition leader Achakzai demands meeting with jailed Imran Khan before any government negotiations, warning of protests.

title: Marriage can be dissolved on Shiqaq sans proven cruelty: SC
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Wednesday held that a marriage could be dissolved on grounds of Shiqaq (irreconcilable discord) under the residuary provision of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 even when cruelty was not proven.

"A marriage may be dissolved by a court, but neither spouse should be judicially deprived of a lawful right, nor judicially burdened with a stigma, without the foundation of law and evidence," the court observed in its judgement.

Headed by Justice Shahid Waheed, a five-judge SC bench comprising Justices Naeem Akhter Afghan, Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, Ishtiaq Ibrahim and Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb took up two connected petitions filed by Zainab Bibi and Iram Naz Begum against two Peshawar High Court orders.

Both cases arose from family suits in which the wives sought dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty and claimed maintenance, dower and dowry articles. However, the family courts found cruelty unproved but dissolved the marriages through Khula, directing the wives to return the dower. The appellate court and the PHC largely upheld these decrees.

Before the SC, the wives raised two principal grievances: first, that their marriages could not lawfully be dissolved through Khula because they neither sought nor consented to it, as their cases were founded on cruelty; and second, that their financial claims should have been allowed in full.

Authored by Justice Waheed, the 15-page judgement drew a distinction between Khula and Shiqaq. It explained that Khula proceeded from a wife's voluntary election to obtain release from the marriage and ordinarily carried financial consequences.

Shiqaq, by contrast, arose from an objectively established condition of serious matrimonial breach and did not depend on the wife's surrender of dower or any benefit as consideration for her release.

The judgement held that the family courts had erred in converting the petitioners' claims for dissolution on the ground of cruelty into decrees of Khula without obtaining their clear and voluntary consent or election.

"Those decrees, to the extent that they rest upon Khula, cannot be sustained," the judgement ruled, although it did not set aside the dissolution altogether.

"The matrimonial relationships have undergone a serious and continuing rupture; reconciliation has failed; the evidence does not establish the statutory ground of cruelty; and the record, taken as a whole, establishes a condition of Shiqaq of the kind contemplated by verse 35 of Surah An-Nisa of the Holy Quran and recognised under Muslim law, thereby bringing the cases within the residuary provision contained in section 2(ix) of the Act of 1939," the SC explained.

The dissolution could therefore lawfully be sustained, but on a juridical basis different from that adopted by the family courts, the SC judgement noted, adding that the petitioners' marriages were liable to dissolution on the ground of Shiqaq falling within section 2(ix) of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939, and not on the basis of Khula.

However, the directions requiring the petitioners to return, surrender or waive their dower merely as a consequence of Khula should consequently be set aside, the SC ruled. Their entitlement to dower would be determined in accordance with the Act of 1939, it declared.

The SC observed that the Quranic emphasis on reconciliation in cases of Shiqaq was meaningful precisely because it contemplated the possibility that reconciliation might fail. "The law should neither rush towards separation nor prolong a matrimonial relationship which has ceased to serve its lawful purposes," the judgement held.

Where reconciliation had failed and the relationship had reached the condition of Shiqaq, the judicial task was to bring the matter to a lawful conclusion without unnecessary attribution of blame or deprivation of rights, the judgement explained.

The SC emphasised that courts must distinguish between an unhappy marriage and one in a state of Shiqaq.

"Mere incompatibility, occasional disagreement, anger, short separation or the existence of matrimonial litigation cannot, by themselves, satisfy the test. The court must be satisfied that the breach is genuine, serious and continuing; that the matrimonial relationship has ceased to function in accordance with its essential purposes; and that reconciliation has failed despite meaningful judicial effort," the judgement emphasised.

"It [Shiqaq] requires a genuine and continuing rupture of such character that the essential purposes of marriage cannot realistically be fulfilled, coupled with failure of reasonable efforts at reconciliation."
ir_summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court rules that marriage can be dissolved due to irreconcilable discord without proven cruelty.

title: UK, Poland to boost border, drug cooperation with Pakistan
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Uni­ted Kingdom and Poland on Wednesday agreed to enhance cooperation with Pakistan against illegal migration, narcotics and organised crime and to sign various memorandums of understanding (MoUs).

Interior Minister Moh­sin Naqvi and Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhary held separate meetings with British Minister of State for For­e­ign Affairs Stephen Doug­hty and Polish Minister and Head of the Council of Ministers Tomasz Siemoniak.

In his meeting with the British minister, Mr Naqvi stressed the need for joint measures to curb the trend of travelling to the UK on fake student visas.

During the meeting with the Polish minister, bilateral relations and ways to further enhance security cooperation were discussed.

The two sides agreed to finalise various MoUs, including one on Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA), at the earliest. It was also agreed that a delegation of the Ministry of Interior, led by Mr Chaudhary, would visit Poland soon.
ir_summary: UK and Poland agree with Pakistan to enhance cooperation on border security, illegal migration, and narcotics control.

title: Peshawar High Court rejects Afridi’s plea challenging ECP proceedings
text:
PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court on Wednesday rejected a petition filed by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi challenging proceedings initiated against him by the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) for allegedly violating the election code of conduct during by-elections in Haripur in November 2025.

A bench comprising Justice Syed Arshad Ali and Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali pronounced a short order dismissing the petition without touching the question of the ECP's jurisdiction in light of an earlier court order.

The detailed judgement will be issued later.

With the dismissal of the petition, a stay order earlier granted in favour of Mr Afridi also stands vacated.

Following the preliminary hearing of the petition earlier this year, the court had ordered, "In the meanwhile, the respondent-ECP may proceed with the matter; however, it shall not pass any final order adverse to the petitioner (Sohail Afridi) till further orders."

The development assumes significance amid growing tensions between KP and federal governments over the ongoing protest march.

A panel of lawyers appeared for the petitioner, including Adnan Ali, Bashir Khan Wazir, Barrister Sarwar Muzaffar Shah and Inam Yousafzai. The ECP was represented by Additional Director General (Law) Khurram Shehzad and Additional Director (Law) Samran Jehangir, while Barrister Sajeel Sheharyar Swati appeared for the complainant against Mr Afridi before the ECP.

In November last year, the chief minister and by-election candidate Shehrnaz Omar Ayub, backed by PTI, had challenged notices issued to them by the ECP for allegedly violating the election code of conduct.

Mr Afridi had challenged a notice issued to him by the ECP on Nov 20, accusing him of delivering a provocative speech against government functionaries in connection with the by-election in NA-18 Haripur.

The ECP contended that the CM's speech was contrary to the code of conduct issued by the commission for the by-election.

Mr Afridi had asked the high court to set aside the impugned notice. However, on Nov 26, the court dismissed both petitions, observing that no adverse order had so far been passed against the petitioners.

The bench had observed that it expected the ECP, in the first instance, to determine its jurisdiction in the matter before proceeding further with the inquiry.

Mr Afridi again approached the court earlier this year, contending that the ECP had been proceeding against him without first deciding the question of its jurisdiction, contrary to the Elections Act, 2017.

ECP counsel Khurram Shehzad argued that the petition was not maintainable and was liable to be dismissed as no order had so far been passed against the petitioner.

He submitted that the proceedings pending before the commission were independent in nature and separate from those pending before the district monitoring officer (DMO).

He argued that the ECP had two types of jurisdiction — one concerning civil wrongs and the other concerning cases of a criminal nature.

Under Section 15 of the Elections Act, 2017, he said, the ECP could take cognisance of matters relating to implementation of the code of conduct on its own motion as well as on a complaint filed by an aggrieved person.

He contended that an almost identical petition had been dismissed by the court in November last year.

Mr Afridi's counsel, Adnan Ali, stated that the ECP had issued the controversial notice to the chief minister on Nov 20, 2025.

"The allegation pertained to remarks made against election staff and influencing the election," he said.

"The speech delivered by the chief minister was outside the jurisdiction of NA-18 Haripur, where the by-election was held on Nov 23, 2025," the counsel argued.

He said that once the DMO had issued a notice to Mr Afridi under Section 234 of the Elections Act, the ECP lacked jurisdiction to issue another notice to him under Section 15 of the Act.

He argued that the ECP had clubbed a private complaint filed by a rival candidate with its suo motu proceedings. He contended that the ECP was exercising the powers of the DMO. "Here, both the ECP and the DMO issued notices, and the DMO also submitted a report to the former," he argued.

"Let the Election Commission hear you; present whatever your response is before them," Justice Arshad Ali remarked.

The bench observed, "This is merely an inquiry by the Election Commission, not a formal action. There is no legal bar preventing the Election Commission from conducting an inquiry."

However, Mr Afridi's lawyers maintained that the ECP had initiated a process under which the petitioner could face disqualification.
ir_summary: Peshawar High Court rejects KP Chief Minister's petition challenging Election Commission proceedings over alleged election code violations.

title: Mamdani slams Oct 7 attack, calls Gaza war ‘ongoing genocide’
text:
WASHINGTON: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Wednesday marked the third anniversary of Hamas's Oct 7, 2023, raid on Israel by condemning the killings and abductions that day while describing Israel's subsequent military campaign in Gaza as an "ongoing genocide".

"This day is profoundly painful for so many New Yorkers," Mamdani said in a statement. "It marks three years since the horrific war crimes of Oct 7. On that day, Hamas killed more than 1,100 Israelis and abducted 251 others."

"We grieve alongside our many friends and neighbours who still carry that unthinkable loss," he said. But Mamdani said the suffering had continued beyond the Oct 7 raid, accusing the Israeli government of carrying out a "devastating, ongoing genocide in Gaza".

According to his statement, more than 74,000 Palestinians, including more than 21,000 children, have been killed in Gaza. He also said more than 1,400 Palestinians had been killed even since the "so-called ceasefire".

Mamdani said the suffering had intensified with Israeli attacks on ambulances waiting outside hospitals, drone strikes targeting residential buildings or journalists, and the rejection of food-aid shipments at border crossings.

"Many New Yorkers are reckoning with this unbearable grief, and we mourn alongside them — all while knowing that our tax dollars fund these war crimes," he said.

The mayor also criticised the US government for what he described as complicity in the violence, saying that "our federal government continues its complicity with every arms shipment."

Three years after the Oct 7 raid, Mamdani said there should be a rejection of what he described as a world in which "occupation and apartheid continue" and "war crimes are met with impunity".

"To honour the dead, we must fight for a world in which every person can live with freedom, safety, and dignity," he said.
ir_summary: New York City Mayor condemns Hamas attack and calls Israel's Gaza campaign an ongoing genocide.

title: France suspends use of stun grenades to police student protests
text:
PARIS: The French government said on Wednesday it was pausing the use of stun grenades in its policing of student protests, after a 15-year-old boy's hand was blown off during a clash with riot police, fuelling protesters' accusations of police brutality.

Protests showed no sign of easing, with more than 500 schools closed a day after demonstrations swept across the country, and unions representing high-school students, teachers and other workers planning more marches for Thursday.

The wave of protests has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace President Emmanuel Macron. Speaking to the nation on Wednesday evening, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would review the demands made by students and present proposals at the end of October on issues ranging from renovating buildings to make more teachers available, but gave no details.

"In the past, too many promises were not kept, quite simply because they were untenable," Lecornu said. "What I want are concrete, quick and fully funded answers." The lack of an immediate government response, which was decried by student leaders after talks at the education ministry earlier on Wednesday, appeared unlikely to quell the protests.

At Lycee Lamartine, a high school in central Paris, protesters sang the Marseillaise, chanted slogans and performed Mexican waves as they blockaded the entrance to the school.

"We saw there were lots of crumbling walls, a shortage of teachers in public schools, absent teachers," said Gabriel Fillieule, who used to attend a public school but now goes to a private one. He and others said they were protesting to demand better learning conditions for all.

While most of Wednesday's blockades were peaceful, police used tear gas and pushed back protesters in a street barricaded by rubbish bins outside Sciences Po university in central Paris. Rights groups, labour unions, students and some opposition politicians have accused the police of using disproportionate force to quell the wave of protests.

Elsewhere in Europe, where budgets have been under pressure as governments respond to successive cost-of-living and energy crises, students in parts of Belgium staged similar protests. In the Belgian city of Liege in the southern French-speaking Wallonia region, at least 107 people have been arrested in connection with student protests this month, the Belga news agency reported. Teachers are also on strike.

In Portugal, the main teachers' union FENPROF launched an indefinite strike in mid-September over working conditions, with teachers refusing to do any unpaid work beyond the 35 hours a week mandated by law. And in Spain, teachers' unions have been protesting conditions in state schools. Teachers in Madrid plan a strike on October 14 to press demands including a reduction in hours, smaller class sizes and higher salaries.
ir_summary: France suspends stun grenade use in student protests after a boy's injury, amid widespread anger and demands for education reforms.

title: Western civilisation is ‘at an inflection point’, says Rubio
text:
ATHENS: Western civilisation is at a crossroads as it faces multiple threats, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in Athens on Wednesday, calling for a rebuilding of alliances and for Europe to "awaken from its long slumber".

"We are at an inflection point... not only in the history of my nation but an inflection point in the whole of our civilisation," Rubio said in a speech beneath the Acropolis. Mr Rubio insisted on the US right to flex its "national power" in a fiery speech. "Either we choose to act now, or lose the choice to act at all," the top US diplomat said.

The western world must embrace "national power" and technological innovation or risk sliding into decline, he said. His speech, packed with praise for ancient heroes such as Alexander the Great, follows an address in February where he argued that Europe was threatened by mass immigration and called for it to defend Christian civilisation.

The United States under President Donald Trump has made its choice, according to Rubio. "We choose the unapologetic pursuit of national power: to take back control of our critical supply chains, to reindustrialise our economy, to rebuild our defence, to fight for dominance of the technologies and industries of the future," he said.

"There is new competition between great powers again. There is vulnerability, aggression, terrorism, a whole universe of new threats and attacks again," Rubio said. "We must rebuild our institutions and our alliances to face these threats together," he said.

Rubio said that in Europe he saw encouraging signs of what Washington hoped "will be the beginning of a generational shift, skyrocketing defence spending, a flurry of new partnerships and programmes, expanded manufacturing and production." "We believe that Europe can awaken from its long slumber and rekindle the fire that was lit here millennia ago," he said.

His speech, which was packed with praise for the ancient Greeks, followed an address in February when he argued that Europe was threatened by mass immigration and called for it to defend Christian civilisation. Rubio, who arrived from Iceland as part of a European tour, underlined the "critical" US alliance with Greece. He flagged the energy sector, and announced a joint agreement on information-sharing on drug trafficking and terrorism.

"As you see a world that faces... destabilising events, you recognise how important this alliance with Greece is to the United States," he said, referencing conflict in the Middle East and the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

In the Middle East, he argued that Iran had "lost complete control" of the strategic Strait of Hormuz, seeking to offer reassurance at a time when the United States is struggling to find a way out of the war just weeks before key US legislative elections. Rubio took part in a "strategic dialogue" with Greece on regional and energy security amid high tensions triggered by the wars in Iran and Ukraine. He is to meet conservative Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis, before departing for Lisbon.

The wars in Iran and Ukraine have highlighted the fragility of energy supply routes, and Greece is positioning itself as a key hub in southeastern Europe, particularly for the transport of natural gas.
ir_summary: US Secretary of State Rubio calls for Western nations to strengthen alliances and military power against global threats.

title: FBR expands electronic production monitoring
text:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has extended electronic production monitoring to the leather, paper and paperboard sectors, authorising four private vendors to install and operate camera-based monitoring systems across industrial sectors.

The move is part of the FBR's efforts to strengthen sales tax monitoring and curb tax evasion by obtaining production data directly from manufacturing units rather than relying solely on figures declared by registered manufacturers. The monitoring system is already operating in several industries.

The expansion brought additional manufacturing sectors into a system through which the tax authority can directly observe production activity and maintain records of factory operations, reducing its dependence on production figures declared by registered manufacturers.

The FBR issued SRO 1751 of 2026 on Wednesday to notify that production by registered manufacturers of leather and paper and paperboard would be electronically monitored under Chapter XIV BA of the Sales Tax Rules 2006.

In a separate authorisation, the FBR approved four vendors to supply, install, operate and maintain production-monitoring equipment across five sectors — packaged tea, household electronics, paper and paperboard, edible oil and ghee, and leather.

Obsidian Technologies will monitor textile spinning, while Tollink Pakistan covers aerated beverages and bottled water. ISSM Labelling Solutions monitors textile spinning, tiles, packaged milk, packaged juices and bottled water, while Authentik covers aerated beverages, packaged milk, packaged juices and bottled water.

Under the new arrangement, IP cameras and Network Video Recorders (NVRs) will be installed at production lines. The cameras will continuously capture production activity in real time, while the NVRs will retain recordings for at least two months.

The vendors will be responsible for procuring, installing, operating, maintaining and repairing the equipment. The authorisation is limited to IP cameras and NVRs, barring vendors from supplying or charging manufacturers for any other equipment or software.

All footage and recordings will remain the property of the FBR and will be treated as confidential, with sharing prohibited except as directed by the Board.

The FBR has introduced an online facility allowing steel melters and re-rollers to declare electricity consumption to calculate their sales tax liability when power distribution companies fail to report supplies or submit returns late.

Annex K of the sales tax return is mandatory for steel melters, re-rollers, and composite units to calculate sales tax liability under the Thirteenth Schedule of the Sales Tax Act 1990. The automated system normally obtains electricity consumption data after distribution companies file Annex C of their returns.

However, the FBR said taxpayers were facing difficulties when distribution companies either did not declare electricity supplied to them or filed their returns late, preventing the required consumption data from being automatically reflected in Annex K.
ir_summary: Pakistan's tax authority expands electronic monitoring of production in leather and paper sectors to curb tax evasion.

title: Discos’ sell-off faces investor trust deficit
text:
ISLAMABAD: To attract bidders for the successful privatisation of distribution companies (Discos) and allay concerns about contract sanctity, the government is expediting measures to improve regulatory predictability and considering political risk guarantees from multilateral agencies.

Informed sources told Dawn that the reopening of independent power producers' (IPPs) contracts and recent legal developments involving K-Electric had heightened risk perception among prospective bidders — both local and foreign — currently undertaking due diligence of the first batch of Discos.

They have stressed the need for binding legal guarantees and clear financial risk allocation to prevent post-privatisation contractual disputes, and demanded longer licence tenures than the existing 20-year term for Discos.

Interestingly, the prime minister's adviser on privatisation, Muhammad Ali — who was involved in renegotiations with IPPs that led to revised contracts during the PTI and PML-N tenures — now faces questions from prospective investors over regulatory and contractual guarantees.

Against this backdrop, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Wednesday presided over a meeting of the Steering Committee on Power Sector Regulatory Regime and Reform Options to advance reforms to strengthen the power sector's regulatory framework and promote efficiency, investment, competition and greater private-sector participation.

The finance minister noted that the evolving power sector landscape required a regulatory framework capable of responding to technological developments while supporting efficiency, investment, consumer interests and greater private-sector participation, an official statement said.

The meeting coincided with a stay order on Wednesday from the Sindh High Court against recent decision of the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) and its appellant tribunal regarding K-Electric's Multi-Year Tariff (MYT) that effectively curtailed federal government's subsidy to KE worth around Rs200 billion. Aggrieved by the appellant tribunal and Nepra decision, KE had challenged it in SHC which suspended those notifications and orders and issued notices to the respondents for next date of hearing on Oct 15.

The finance minister-led committee discussed Pakistan's power sector transformation and discussed the significant changes taking place in the industry, including growing solarisation and changing demand patterns. "The committee discussed key structural and emerging challenges facing the sector, including legacy capacity obligations, changing grid-demand patterns, service quality, investment constraints and the need to further strengthen incentives for efficiency", an official statement said.

"The discussion also focused on improving regulatory predictability, better targeting of subsidies and strengthening the overall investment climate to support a more efficient, competitive and financially sustainable power sector", the statement added.

The minister called for developing a market structure that provides clearer incentives for efficiency and service quality, while creating greater space for competition, private-sector participation and investment.
ir_summary: Pakistan's government seeks to privatize power distribution companies amid investor concerns over regulatory risks and contract guarantees.

title: PM Shehbaz orders fast-track ML-1 upgrade
text:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday directed authorities to accelerate work on the Main Line-1 (ML-1) railway upgrade and introduce corporate-style reforms in Pakistan Railways.

The ML-1 project aims to upgrade and modernise key infrastructure to enhance freight and passenger connectivity from Karachi to Peshawar.

Presiding over a meeting on Pakistan Railways on Wednesday, the prime minister appreciated the efforts of teams from the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) and the Ministry of Railways, led by the NAB chairman, to identify and recover encroached railway land, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.

"Modernising ML-1 is of key importance for the development of Pakistan Railways, improving passenger services and increasing freight transport," he was quoted as saying.

The prime minister directed that ML-1 be developed on a commercial basis by utilising identified railway land worth billions of rupees.

"The real commercial potential of railway properties needs to be harnessed," he said, calling for the effective use of valuable railway land for commercial purposes to contribute to the national economy and the development of Pakistan Railways.

He said corporate-style reforms to strengthen the railways and make it economically self-sufficient were among the government's priorities. He added that the railway minister was working to make the organisation profitable and improve its operations.

Mr Shehbaz, during the meeting, approved securing bank financing through commercial projects on railway land and utilising the funds for the project.

He directed authorities to present a comprehensive plan within two weeks based on the actual commercial potential of railway land.

The meeting was informed that the 1,726-kilometre ML-1 upgrade had been divided into four major sections: Karachi-Rohri, Rohri-Multan, Multan-Lahore and Lahore-Peshawar.

International financing was being used for the Karachi-Rohri section, while plans were being prepared to finance the remaining sections through domestic resources, the meeting was told.

Officials briefed the meeting on various stages of the ML-1 project, progress on the Karachi-Rohri section and railway-owned land, as per the PMO.

Civil work on the first phase of the ML-1 is likely to begin in January 2027. It covers the 480km Karachi-Rohri/Sukkur section, where new up and down tracks will be laid along with fencing on both sides to prevent unauthorised access by people, animals and vehicles.
ir_summary: Pakistani PM orders acceleration of ML-1 railway upgrade project and corporate reforms for Pakistan Railways.

title: Hundreds arrested in French school protests
text:
PARIS: Mass protests over decrepit conditions at France's high schools descended into sporadic violence on Tuesday, leading to nearly 500 arrests and prompting President Emmanuel Macron to call an emergency meeting. The protests started in late September with students blocking entrances to hundreds of high schools for 15- to 17-year-olds over complaints of dilapidated facilities and teacher shortages.

US President Donald Trump weighed in on Tuesday to blame the unrest in France on "mass migration" and Islam, as he pushed his global right-wing narrative ahead of tough midterm elections at home. In France, parents, teachers and union workers joined the high school students' movement in the capital Paris and other cities.

The interior ministry said 256,000 people protested nationwide, while union organisers put the figure at 450,000. Macron was expected to meet top officials on Tuesday, including Interior Minister Laurent Nunez and Education Minister Edouard Geffray, in response to the unrest, a government source said. At least 488 people were arrested and 43 members of the security forces were wounded on Tuesday, the interior ministry announced. Rights groups, unions and the students have accused authorities of using disproportionate force. A teenager lost a hand on Monday after police fired a stun grenade.

A 14-year-old student in northwest Paris was hit in the face with a tear gas grenade at such close range that he lost several teeth. A policeman was charged Tuesday over that incident.
ir_summary: French students protest school conditions, leading to arrests and government emergency meeting amid accusations of police brutality.

title: Trump orders firing squad for Fort Hood gunman
text:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump has ordered the use of a firing squad to execute the former US Army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas, in a 2009 shooting spree the gunman later described as retaliation for US wars in the Muslim world, the Pentagon said on Monday.

The decision to put former US Army Major Nidal Hasan to death by army firing squad was approved by the president at the recommendation of Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said on X.

Parnell noted that Hasan killed 12 unarmed active-duty soldiers and a retired serviceman, and wounded 32 others. The secretary of the army will set the time and place of the execution, Parnell said.

A military jury sentenced Hasan to death in August 2013, after finding him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted premeditated murder for opening fire with a laser-sighted handgun in a medical facility at the sprawling central Texas military base.

The shooting came weeks before Hasan, now 56, was scheduled to be deployed to Afghanistan. He was left partially paralysed and confined to a wheelchair.

In a statement responding to Trump's decision, the group Death Penalty Action, which opposes capital punishment, said: "There is nothing Donald Trump loves more than the power to kill." Military executions are rare, and under the Uniform Code of Military Justice a death sentence imposed by court-martial may not be carried out "until approved by the president."
ir_summary: President Trump orders a firing squad execution for the Fort Hood shooter convicted of killing 13 people.

title: UK considers expelling Israeli diplomats if Tel Aviv shuts Jerusalem consulate
text:
TEL AVIV: Britain is considering expelling Israeli diplomats if Israel carries out its order to shut the British consulate in East Jerusalem this week in a dispute over sanctions targeting Israeli settlements, four sources said.

Israel on Sept 8 ordered Britain to close the East Jerusalem consulate within 30 days and remove its diplomats from the city, after Britain said it would impose a ban on trade of goods made in Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

The 30-day deadline for Britain to close the consulate ends on Thursday, which will impact around 30 British diplomats who work there, along with their family members, the sources said. Britain is considering expelling Israeli diplomats from Israel's embassy in London in response to any closure of the consulate, the sources said, speaking on condition of anonymity.

It would be a highly unusual step for allies to expel each others diplomats. Despite the current strains, the UK and Israel are close economic, security and intelligence partners. The British Foreign Office and the Israeli Foreign Ministry declined to comment. An Israeli official said any action against Israel would be met with a response.

A fifth source, also speaking on condition of anonymity, said Britain was still hopeful that an agreement could be reached to prevent the consulate from closing. If it did close, the source added, London was not expected to take any action until after Israel's Oct 27 election, if at all.

After Britain announced the sanctions, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar accused London of interfering in this month's election. A spokesperson for Saar said on Monday the consulate would close on Thursday.

The British sanctions announcement, and Israel's response, mark a new low in the relationship between the once steadfast allies. Britain has repeatedly criticised Israel over its actions in the war in Gaza and over Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians. Israel's government has accused Britain's governing Labour Party of being hostile towards Israel.

The British consulate, in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood of East Jerusalem, handles the country's relations with Palestinians in the city as well as in the West Bank and Gaza. It also provides consular services to Palestinians. The consulate has been in Jerusalem for almost 200 years, long before the State of Israel was established in 1948.

Britain's top national security adviser, Jonathan Powell, had quietly visited Israel last week in an attempt to keep the consulate open but failed to reach an agreement. Two other sources said that Britain has asked European countries to raise the issue with Israel in hope of convincing the government to reverse its decision.
ir_summary: UK considers expelling Israeli diplomats in response to Israel's order to close British consulate in East Jerusalem.

title: Crew missing after drones hit ships in Black Sea off Bulgaria
text:
SOFIA: Bulgarian authorities on Tuesday were searching for the missing crew of a ship that sank in the Black Sea after drones hit two vessels in what EU leaders condemned as an "unacceptable" attack. The dual strike came a day after another ship had caught fire and sank off the Romanian coast, killing one and leaving one missing. Ukraine said the drone attack was launched by Russia. Black Sea shipping has been hit by growing fallout from the Ukraine-Russia war in recent months.

Early on Tuesday, "sea and air drones" attacked two merchant vessels, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said, adding that it was too soon to determine from which country the drones came.

A Bulgarian ferry that witnessed the explosion and rushed to the scene discovered overturned life rafts and life jackets near the ship that sank.

No crew members from that ship have been found, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev told reporters. He did not specify how many people were missing.

Eighteen crew — 11 Turkish and seven Indian — were rescued from the other ship. The attack within Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone "constitutes a flagrant violation of maritime law and, more broadly, of the rules of navigation", Radev said, adding it was "absolutely unacceptable".

A search operation was launched 70 nautical miles east of the coastal town of Byala, authorities said. Both vessels are Turkish-owned, according to the Equasis merchant shipping database.

According to the available information, the Able was carrying wheat and heading south, while the Alfa Watan was sailing north, Radev said.

"The situation significantly complicates navigation in the Black Sea, drives up insurance premiums, and makes maritime traffic extremely difficult," Radev said before convening an emergency meeting of ministers. The ship that sank was the Togolese-flagged Alfa Watan, according to the Maritime.bg specialised website. The second ship, the Able, registered in Palau, was set on fire. Two of the rescued crew members were hospitalised, one suffering from burns and one from a head injury.

European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen also called attacks on civilian shipping in the Black Sea "unacceptable". "While exact circumstances of these incidents are still being established, the developments are very concerning," von der Leyen wrote online. Romanian foreign minister Oana Toiu on X also "firmly" condemned the attack.

Neighbouring Romania reported on Monday that a grain ship had caught fire and sank in the Black Sea. Ukraine blamed the attack on the Turkish-owned Royad Mammadov on Russia.

The Azerbaijani captain died, while one Azerbaijani crew member remains missing, according to Azerbaijan's foreign ministry, as cited by Russia's Ria Novosti news agency. Amid mounting fallout from Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, incidents involving drones have become increasingly frequent in recent months across eastern European countries. The conflict has also spread across the eastern Black Sea.

At least 45 merchant vessels have been attacked over the past 12 months in areas of the Black Sea previously not listed as high-risk, maritime risk expert Ambrey said last month.
ir_summary: Drones attacked two ships in the Black Sea, sinking one vessel and leaving crew missing, with Ukraine blaming Russia.

title: Manchhar in peril
text:
MANCHHAR lake is filling up, but for families who live around it, that has brought little relief. Pakistan's largest freshwater lake receives polluted water from the Main Nara Valley Drain at 2,000 cusecs a day. More Indus water has lowered salinity from about 6,000 to 4,000 TDS, but the lake remains contaminated. For local communities, this means fewer fish to catch, less income to bring home and drinking water that cannot be relied on. Many families that once depended on fishing and other lake-based work are struggling to survive, while dozens of reverse-osmosis plants in settlements are not working. A lake that should sustain the people around it is instead becoming a source of hardship. A higher water level may make Manchhar look healthier from a distance. Up close, the people living beside it know otherwise.

None of this is unknown. Experts have long called for polluted drainage to be diverted away from Manchhar and for the RBOD-II drainage project to be completed so harmful flows can be carried towards the sea. Yet the work has dragged on while the lake has deteriorated and livelihoods have disappeared. The first duty of the state is clear: restore safe drinking-water supplies, repair broken RO plants and provide health support to affected communities. But relief alone is not enough. Sindh and federal authorities need a firm timetable for stopping contaminated inflows and completing the drainage works, with public reporting on water quality and progress. Fisherfolk who have lost their earnings will need support while the lake recovers. Every delay leaves more families with less to live on and fewer reasons to believe official promises. Manchhar can still be restored, but not by allowing pollution to continue and hoping fresh water will hide the damage. The source must be stopped. The people around the lake have already waited far too long.
ir_summary: Pollution of Pakistan's Manchhar Lake threatens local livelihoods and drinking water, with calls for government action on drainage projects.

title: PSX rebounds 2,593 points on IMF optimism
text:
KARACHI: After a sluggish overnight start stemming from regional and political uncertainty, the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Tuesday saw strong buying interest at attractive valuations, helping the benchmark KSE-100 index recover from recent lows to above the 168,000 level, apparently supported by expectations of a positive conclusion to the ongoing review talks with the visiting International Monetary Fund staff mission.

Media reports suggest negotiations with the IMF are set to conclude on a positive note later this week, paving the way for the disbursement of about $1.2 billion under two programmes — the $7bn Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the $1.4bn Res­il­ience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).

Topline Securities Ltd said the KSE-100 index rebounded sharply, gaining 2,593 points, or 1.56 per cent, to close at 168,460. The index traded between 165,652 and 168,626 during the session.

Buying interest returned across major sectors, including banks, oil and gas exploration, cem­ent, automobiles, OMCs, refineries, and power. Heavyweights such as United Bank, Habib Bank, Oil and Gas Development Company, Pakistan Petroleum, Pakistan Oilfield, and Hub Power supported the recovery.

The rebound came as investors appeared to take advantage of the previous session's sharp correction, while easing concerns about oil prices provided some relief. Brent crude was trading around $98.32 per barrel, down about 2pc on the day.

Ali Najib, Deputy Head of Trading at Arif Habib Ltd, said that following an overnight sharp sell-off, the market rebounded as international oil prices eased and Middle East oil flows improved, helping to restore investor sentiment.

On the sectoral front, oil production declined 6.4pc week on week to 637,000 barrels of oil per day, primarily due to lower flows from northern fields. Gas production fell 1.4pc to 2,999 mmcfd, mainly due to reduced output from Mari, Sui and Sharf.

On the corporate front, sales of Sazgar Engin­eering Works Company rose 22pc year-on-year to 10,872 units in 1QFY27, driven by a 45pc increase in three-wheeler sales, while four-wheeler sales fell 12pc year-on-year.

Engro Holdings, United Bank, Hub Power, Habib Bank, OGDC, Mari Energies, Fauji Fertiliser, PPL, National Bank, and Meezan Bank collectively contributed 1,493 points.

Market activity remained stable, with trading volume rising 2.36pc to 432.01 million shares and total turnover value jumping 28.19pc to Rs20.1bn. Cnergyico PK led the volume chart with 55m shares.

Analysts expect the market to sustain its recovery momentum if oil prices remain subdued and concerns about Middle East supply continue to ease. However, geopolitical uncertainty and elevated volatility are likely to keep investors cautious.
